THE ENUMERATION PROPERTY IS THE ONE TO KNOW ABOUT. The verify result type carries NO reason - not unknown_phone, not wrong_code, not expired, not too_many_attempts. Five distinct failure modes return one shared REFUSED object, because a result type with reasons in it eventually becomes a route with different responses, which is the patient-list oracle LOOP 3 named as the obvious attack. Two assertions guard it and the negative arm proved BOTH are needed: injecting a distinguishable refusal did not fail the deep-equality test (vitest's toEqual ignores undefined-valued keys) and was caught only by the Object.keys assertion.

THE DURABLE LIMITER FAILS CLOSED. If the store throws, the verdict is refuse. That is the opposite of the usual availability instinct and it is right: this limiter guards the OTP verify path, so failing open turns a database blip into an unlimited guessing window against a 6-digit code.

REMAINING ON THIS LOOP: the request/verify ROUTES (rate-limited before the auth check, per the session route's posture), the Drizzle OtpStore implementation against 0056, trusted-device issue and check (30 days, fixed at issue, never extended on use), WF-07 phone-match linkage with its refusals, and the three pt-PT degradation copies (no phone, landline, shared number). None of it is blocked.

PROGRESS 2026-08-05: routes, linkage and degradation copy built. LOOP 3 is now ONE STEP from complete - only the session mint remains.

THE ROUTES. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request answers 204 for ANY well-formed number, known or not, and never queries the patient table at all - so membership cannot leak even through the timing of a lookup that is never performed. The only distinguishable outcomes are 400 (malformed input, which tells the caller about their own typing) and 429. Two independent limits, per client key AND per phone hash, because either alone is bypassable: one by rotating the number, the other by rotating the source. The phone limit is applied AFTER normalization, so '912345678' and '+351912345678' cannot be spent as two budgets against one handset.

POST /verify returns ONE 401 with ONE body for all five failure modes. Tested by deep-equality across them, not by both being falsy. It reaches the patient table only AFTER the code verifies - WF-07's claim time - and a test asserts linkage is never called when the code fails.

WF-07 LINKAGE. All four predicates are in the SQL rather than applied afterwards in JS, so a later edit cannot silently widen the candidate set by dropping a filter. LIMIT 2, not LIMIT 1, and that is the load-bearing detail: LIMIT 1 returns the same single row for one match and for five, silently turning an ambiguous match into a confident mis-link.

THE COST IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a patient whose number sits on two rows sees exactly the same screen as someone who mistyped a digit, and cannot be told why. WF-07 accepted that. The alternative confirms to any caller that a number is in this clinic's files, and how many times.

DEGRADATION COPY. Three pt-PT strings for no phone, landline, shared number - each naming the clinic as the next step, because WF-07 is deliberately fail-closed and these will be read by real people who did nothing wrong. They are distinct from each other on purpose, which is NOT a contradiction of the identical-refusal rule: these are shown to a patient the clinic has already identified, where being specific is the remedy. The generic otp_refused stays generic and is tested against leaking any predicate.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is one thing: THE SESSION MINT. verify returns the resolved patientId and NOTHING else - no cookie, no token, asserted by test. That is deliberate rather than incomplete: the mint must land in the SAME transaction as consuming the code, for the reason 0054 couples a token action to its consumption record, and shipping half of that is what Decision D forbids. Also still to wire: the trusted-device issue/check on the verify path (the store is built and tested), and the portal UI screens that call these routes.

SESSION MINT IN BUILD 2026-08-05, branch portal/W13-03-session-mint. The last remaining step of this loop. What it is: the CLAIM is one transaction - verifyCode proves the code, WF-07 linkage resolves the patient, store.consume spends the code, and the trusted device is issued, all on one connection, committing together or not at all (0054 coupling).

THREE CONTRACT CHANGES THIS FORCED, each with a reason that is not cosmetic. (1) OtpStore.consume now RETURNS A BOOLEAN. The consumed_at IS NULL guard stopped the race loser WRITING but nothing stopped it GRANTING - both requests would have claimed one code. (2) verifyCode NO LONGER CONSUMES; it returns codeId and the caller spends inside its own transaction. Consuming inside verifyCode put the spend outside the caller transaction, which is exactly the split 0054 exists to prevent. (3) both stores and the linkage read now take the caller db handle, defaulting to getDbAdmin, so they can be enrolled in that transaction.

NEW ROUTE, POST /api/v1/auth/otp/trusted, which is the isTrusted() check that had to exist somewhere for the 30-day window to be more than a stored fact. It takes NO PHONE NUMBER deliberately: folding it into /otp/request would have meant either querying the patient table on the enumeration surface or ignoring a parameter the caller supplied.

OPEN OWNER DECISION, NOT INVENTED HERE, carded separately: which artefact carries the PORTAL SESSION after a verified OTP. getPatientPrincipal accepts only a Supabase-issued JWT; no-session-minting.test.ts bans every Supabase session-minting call in apps/api; and WF-07 linkage refuses any patient row whose auth_user_id is already set, so the first login would set it and every later login would refuse. Those three cannot all hold for a working portal login.

=== THE BUILD HALF OF LOOP 3 IS COMPLETE. #817 MERGED (ca3efbd). PG1 IS NOT, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS. ===

All TEN of LOOP 3 machine-verifiable DoD lines now pass: indistinguishable refusals, attempt cap, expiry, single use, rate limits on both routes, trusted device accepted at 30 days and refused at 31, no session minted outside a verified OTP, Twilio not invoked with the flag off while the sink is, three pt-PT degradation copies, sendPatientActivation deleted with its pasted no-caller search, and lint/typecheck/test/build.

WHAT #817 ADDED: the claim is ONE transaction (prove the code, resolve the patient per WF-07, spend the code, remember the device). OtpStore.consume returns a BOOLEAN because the consumed_at IS NULL guard stopped the race loser writing but nothing stopped it granting. verifyCode no longer consumes; the caller spends inside its own transaction, which is 0054 coupling. Both stores and the linkage read take the caller db handle. New route POST /api/v1/auth/otp/trusted, which takes NO phone number - the answer comes from the device cookie alone, because folding it into /otp/request would have meant querying the patient table on the enumeration surface.

THE TEST LESSON, RECORDED BECAUSE IT ALMOST SHIPPED: the first concurrency test PASSED with the consume guard hard-coded to true. On a fast database the first request commits before the second opens its transaction, so the second is refused by findLive and the guard is never reached - the test was measuring nothing and looked green. The replacement holds both claimants at a barrier after their read. CI now runs it with the guard patched out and REQUIRES a non-zero exit; verified in the merged run (guard disabled: exit=1).

WHY PG1 STAYS FAIL. The loop built the mechanism; a patient still cannot log in. Two things stand between: the SESSION ARTEFACT decision (card W13-03a-session-artefact, blocked on Ivan) and the portal login SCREENS, which cannot be finished without it because the screen after the code is the one that needs a session. PG1 is a WF-03 gate anyway - it closes on the owner deployed screen at the acceptance session, not on green CI.

=== THE SCREENS ARE BUILT 2026-08-06 (branch portal/W13-03-login-screens, 119742f). PG1 STILL FAILS, BY DESIGN: it is a WF-03 gate and closes on Ivan's deployed screen. ===

WHAT WAS BUILT: /auth/login is now a phone screen then a code screen, both posting to a server action that calls the API server-to-server and stores the session with writePortalSession. The trusted-device check runs on load, and only when the browser actually holds a device cookie, so a first-time visitor pays no round trip.

A PREMISE CORRECTION, and it is load-bearing rather than pedantic. W13-03b's card says the device token "belongs to the browser, and the portal has no use for it". The first half is true; the second cannot be. The API plants __Host-ojp_device on ITS OWN host, and under Option B the only caller of that route is the PORTAL SERVER. A Set-Cookie on a server-to-server fetch lands in the portal's response object and is discarded, so the browser never saw it: the 30-day device row was being written at every login and read by nobody. The portal now copies the token into its own first-party cookie and forwards it back as the Cookie header the API's readDeviceToken parses. A copy, not an interpretation - nothing in the portal decodes anything. apps/portal/lib/auth/device.ts, and otp.test.ts asserts the copy happens.

THREE MORE DEFECTS THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE LOGIN USELESS, each found by following the patient PAST the button:
1. proxy.ts asked Supabase for a session. An OTP patient has none by construction (WF-07 refuses a patient row already linked to an auth user), so every patient who logged in was redirected straight back to the login screen.
2. app/page.tsx did the same at the root URL, which is the URL a patient types.
3. account/actions.ts built its Authorization header from the Supabase cookie only, so "editar dados" would have answered 401 for every OTP patient.
All three now read the portal session.

AND LOGOUT: it called supabase.auth.signOut(), which cannot clear an httpOnly portal cookie. It now clears the session AND the trusted device, because a sign-out that leaves a 30-day credential on a shared handset is exactly what a patient signs out to prevent.

THE PASSWORD DOOR IS SHUT, which is Decision D's "no session minted from any other artefact" rather than tidying: /auth/reset-password, /auth/activate and /auth/callback each minted a Supabase session for a patient. They survived the 2026-08-05 magic-link removal only because deleting them then would have left the portal with no login at all - the condition these screens end. All three deleted; the dead "change password" row on the account screen went with them; the guard test INVERTED (it asserted signInWithPassword was present, it now asserts its absence) and additionally asserts the three files are gone and nothing links to them.

THE THREE DEGRADATION COPIES (LOOP 3 step 8) render as STANDING GUIDANCE on the code screen, never as a diagnosis. The API answers ONE 401 for six failure modes so the screen cannot become a patient-list oracle; branching to one of the three would have rebuilt that oracle inside the portal. All three are shown together, always.

E2E HAD TO CHANGE AND IT GOT BETTER. The portal patient signed in with an email and a password, which no longer exist. It now presents a SEEDED TRUSTED DEVICE and lets the ordinary on-load check mint the session: no test-only code in the app, and it exercises the path a returning patient takes every day. The OTP code itself is unreadable to a test by construction - the transport is off outside production and the sink holds the code in the API process's memory - and reading it would have needed the back door this loop exists to remove.

FOUR NEW pt-PT STRINGS were needed and are additive only: otp_invalid_phone, otp_unavailable, otp_help_title, otp_trusted_checking. The eleven the dispatch named all existed.

STILL OPEN ON THIS CARD: the owner merge its gate requires, PORTAL_TENANT_ID (card W13-03c), and the deployed-screen evidence, which WF-03 batches to the acceptance session.

MERGED 2026-08-06 as #828 (6596d15). NOT CLOSED: WF-03 makes the owner's deployed screen the closing evidence, so this card stays in flight until the acceptance session. Two things still stand between the merge and a patient logging in: PORTAL_TENANT_ID (card W13-03c) and OTP_LIVE_SEND, which stays off until LAUNCH-01 arms it.

ONE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN CI, worth recording because the mistake was mine and it was a reasoning error rather than a typo. The e2e planted the trusted-device cookie with addCookies against an http url and every shard died at the setup: 'Protocol error (Storage.setCookies): Invalid cookie fields', 58 tests never ran. TWO DIFFERENT RULES LOOK LIKE ONE HERE. The Chrome DevTools Protocol validates the URL's SCHEME before storing a Secure cookie and refuses http://localhost outright; the BROWSER separately treats localhost as trustworthy and both accepts and sends Secure cookies there, which is why the portal's own cookies work in dev. I read the second as if it governed the first. Fixed by storing against the https origin - cookies are scoped by host, not scheme - and VERIFIED against a real Chromium before pushing: http rejected, https accepted, and the cookie then arrived on a plain http request. The same probe confirmed the other half nobody had checked: a __Host- Secure cookie set by Set-Cookie from an http://localhost RESPONSE is accepted, captured by storageState, and replayed by a restored context. That is what the portal server does on every login.

=== CORRECTION 2026-08-06, MINE, BEFORE IT WAS BUILT ON. THE CONFIRM AXIS IS THE WRONG AXIS. ===

WHAT I WROTE THREE TIMES - on this card, in #829's body, and to the owner: 'no migration is needed, appointment_confirmation_state has existed since 0024 and is orthogonal to appointment_status by design.' The no-migration half is right. The rest is wrong, and it would have produced a real defect.

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY SAYS, re-derived rather than remembered. apps/web/lib/scheduling/estado.ts:8-20 defines the two axes: lifecycle appointment_status, and confirmation appointment_confirmation_state. The confirmation axis answers 'DID THE PATIENT REPLY TO THE REMINDER' - it is written by the Twilio inbound webhook, and appointment-drawer.tsx:1188-1192 shows it READ-ONLY with the comment 'never edited here (BACKLOG specs a display only, no edit control)... shown separately so the two are never visually or semantically conflated.'

SO RECEPTION ACCEPTING A PEDIDO IS NOT THAT AXIS. It is the LIFECYCLE axis: status scheduled -> confirmed. Writing the confirmation axis for a reception action would record 'the patient confirmed' when no patient did, which is the same class of collision as record_status vs ai_review_state (CLAUDE.md rule 4), and it would corrupt the reminder-reply data the clinic reads.

THE CORRECTED DESIGN, and it still needs no migration:
  QUEUE: derive it from the notification rows. staff_notifications of kind appointment_request already exist per R1, already fan out to reception plus both therapists per R2, and already carry appointment_id. Join to appointments and keep the ones still status=scheduled. THIS IS THE ONLY WAY TO IDENTIFY A PORTAL PEDIDO: there is no provenance column, and packages/db/tests/appointments-created-by-provenance.test.ts proved (7/7 against live Postgres) that created_by CANNOT identify portal rows. Do not add a column for it - the notification IS the provenance record.
  CONFIRM: set status = confirmed. That already renders as 'Confirmada' through deriveEstado, and reception can already do it by hand through the Estado selector in the drawer, so the control is a shortcut for an action the product already supports, not a new state.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: no migration, the in-flight slot stays with LOOP 5.

=== THE CONFIRM SURFACE IS BUILT, AND THE OPTION-B RULING LANDED WITH IT (2026-08-06). ===

On conflict nothing is written, the pedido stays scheduled and stays in the queue, and reception is told in pt-PT which appointment took the slot.

DECLINING IS CANCELLING, and no new status was invented. A declined pedido leaves the queue through the same status predicate that removes a confirmed one. There is no declined value on the lifecycle axis and adding one would have been a migration nobody asked for.

THE AXIS CORRECTION HELD THROUGH THE BUILD. The action writes status only. Two tests assert it: a behavioural one over every set() payload, and a source read of the function body, because a behavioural test can only prove the path it happened to take.

PATIENT COPY, the ruling's point 3. Verified rather than assumed: the old wording did not promise the slot outright, but it called a pedido a marcacao and said nothing about the time being provisional, which reads as a reservation. Now "Pedido recebido", and both pending strings state the time is only reserved once confirmed. Patient-visible, so WF-03 applies and it closes on Ivan's deployed screen at the acceptance session.

That membership check IS Decision C rather than a comment claiming it: a service since turned off for patients, made internal-only, or bound to a deactivated location drops the PRESELECTION and never a row from the list.

=== THE E2E GAP I CARDED DID NOT EXIST. MY GREP WAS WRONG. 2026-08-07. ===

I recorded that the positive preselection case could not be e2e-covered because "seed-e2e.mjs creates no appointments". THAT IS FALSE, and the reason is worth more than the correction: the grep behind it searched apps/web/e2e/seed-e2e.mjs, A PATH THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The file is apps/web/e2e/seed/seed-e2e.mjs. ugrep printed "No such file or directory" and I read the empty result as evidence of absence.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: ensureDeclaracaoAppointment (seed-e2e.mjs:322-337) gives Maria Silva a COMPLETED Osteopatia appointment dated 2022-03-15, and fixtures.ts:238 says "Maria Silva's patient row doubles as the portal test patient". So the portal patient has EXACTLY the history Decision C preselects from, and the positive case is not merely coverable - it is the fixture's DEFAULT state.

HOW IT SURFACED, and it is the good news: CI failed on my own assertion that the badge was ABSENT. Expected 0, received 1. The badge was there because preselection WORKS - priorCompletedServiceId found the completed Osteopatia, and Osteopatia is patient_bookable after the seed fix. A test written on a false premise was corrected by the system it was testing.

THE TEST NOW ASSERTS THE WHOLE RULE instead of half of it: the badge appears exactly once, it is on the RIGHT row (a badge on the wrong service would satisfy a bare count), the OTHER bookable service is still offered, the step is not skipped, and every row is enabled. That last-but-one is the Decision C invariant and the one that fails the moment preselection becomes a filter.

THE LESSON, third time this pattern has cost this project: a grep that returns nothing because it searched the wrong place reads identically to a grep that returns nothing because the thing is not there. Check the path resolves before believing an empty result.

cards.title: A hardcoded mint date plus a 12h TTL turned main red at midnight UTC - fixed, kept as the pattern

evidence.ref: FIXED in #830 (0987ee7), commit f3392d9. apps/api/lib/auth/patient-session.test.ts beforeEach now pins the clock with vi.useFakeTimers() plus vi.setSystemTime(NOW), verified present on main at line 56. 18/18 green, and the Lint+typecheck+test job went from fail to pass on the very next CI run.

cards.notes:
CARDED AFTER THE FACT, 2026-08-07, and it is ALREADY FIXED. The fix rode in #830 rather than waiting for its own PR, because it was the thing BLOCKING #830 and leaving main red overnight to keep a change tidy would have been the wrong trade. Recording the reconciliation rather than re-doing the work.

WHAT HAPPENED. patient-session.test.ts mints every token at a hardcoded NOW of 2026-08-06T10:00:00Z and then VERIFIES it. Verification checks exp against the REAL clock and PATIENT_SESSION_TTL_MS is 12h, so the token expired at 06T22:00Z. CI ran at 07T00:12Z. Two hours too late.

IT WENT RED WITH NO CODE CHANGE ON ANY BRANCH, on the feature branch AND on main at the same moment. git show origin/main carried the identical hardcoded date. A pre-existing LOOP 3 defect that simply reached its detonation date.

THE FIX: beforeEach pins the clock for the whole file. The expiry tests in that same file already did exactly this themselves and were never affected, so the fix only extends the idiom the file had already chosen. Whether a token round-trips is now a question about the code and never about the calendar.

WHY THE CARD SURVIVES THE FIX. The PATTERN is what matters. A test that mints at a FIXED instant and verifies against the REAL clock is a bomb with a fuse as long as the TTL: it passes for months, then fails at a date boundary with no diff to blame, and the first instinct is to hunt the most recent change, which is exactly the wrong place. Anyone adding a signed, expiring artefact to a test should pin the clock in the same commit.

NO OTHER INSTANCE FOUND, but the search was not exhaustive and I am saying so rather than implying coverage. The reminder-token suites and the OTP suites both mint expiring artefacts and are the first places to look if this recurs.

cards.title: Hydration mismatch on the patient profile notes list - toLocaleString differs server vs client
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-07 in an E2E WebServer log while chasing an unrelated failure. Located precisely rather than guessed at, and NOT attributed to the change that happened to be under test.

apps/web/app/patients/[id]/notes-list.tsx:139 renders new Date(note.createdAt).toLocaleString("pt-PT"). The server formats in the Node/ICU timezone and the browser formats in the viewer's, so the two strings differ and React logs "Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client".

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SAID HONESTLY: it is a console error, not a test failure. Every patients.spec.ts test around it passes, and React recovers by re-rendering on the client. What it costs is a real error in the log that trains people to ignore errors in the log.

PRE-EXISTING. Nothing in W13-04 touches this file. It surfaced only because an E2E log was being read line by line for a different reason.

FIX SHAPE, matching how this repo already solves it elsewhere: format on ONE side only. apps/web/app/notificacoes/page.tsx formats server-side with an explicit timeZone: "Europe/Lisbon" and passes strings down, and UpdatePasswordClient uses useSyncExternalStore for the browser locale without a hydration mismatch. Either pattern works here; the second is right if the note timestamp should follow the viewer.

CLOSES ON: the warning absent from a clean E2E run of patients.spec.ts.

The existing consent block is MIGRATION-FREE ON PURPOSE: it lives in clinical_records.data jsonb under the reserved key _consent (consent.ts:40), because an underscore-prefixed key cannot collide with a template field or the twelve AI ingestion keys, and validateRecordData only checks required template fields so the extra key rides along untouched. A THIRD ITEM IN THAT BLOCK WOULD NEED NO MIGRATION AT ALL.
   What forces storage is the word PER PATIENT. _consent is per RECORD. The card requires patient_id, accepted_at, terms_version, recorded_by, and the gate must answer "has THIS PATIENT accepted" without scanning every clinical record they own. That question cannot be answered from a jsonb key on a record set.

4. THE OWNER FORK, and it decides the migration shape rather than whether there is one. Does the acceptance need HISTORY?
   A. LATEST ONLY: three columns on patients (terms_accepted_at, terms_version, terms_recorded_by). Smallest migration, one row per patient, trivially indexed, and the patients table already carries exactly this kind of per-patient scalar - activatedAt, nifExempt, the four contraindication booleans, reminderSmsEnabled. Re-accepting a new terms_version OVERWRITES the old one.
   B. FULL HISTORY: a patient_terms_acceptances table, one row per acceptance, so "which version did they accept and when" is answerable for every version. Bigger migration, an RLS policy and an isolation test of its own per CLAUDE.md rule 2 and the repo RLS rule.
   RECOMMENDED: B. The card says this flow is THE SOLE LEGAL PATH to the fee line ever shipping, and JP confirmed no existing signed document contains the fee rule. A legal basis that OVERWRITES its own history cannot answer "what did this patient agree to in March" after the terms change - which is the one question that matters if the fee is ever disputed. A prevents that answer permanently and cannot be migrated back into afterwards, because the overwritten rows are gone.

5. WHAT DOES NOT NEED DECIDING. REMINDERS_FEE_NOTICE_ENABLED stays SPECIFIED NOT BUILT, default OFF - the card is explicit and the packet says so, because claiming a protection that does not exist is the pattern the notification lane spent a session removing. The gate is per-patient acceptance AND the global flag, never the flag alone.

6. STILL TO READ BEFORE AUTHORING, and it is small: SignatureConsent.tsx render loop (the file path contains bracket characters that broke a shell read this session - open it with a tool, not a glob), the i18n keys clinical.consent.<item>.label/.body so the terms item follows the same key shape, and whether writeConsentState has a caller that assumes exactly two keys.

NOTHING WAS COMMITTED BY THIS RECON. The migration slot is untouched and is still this card's, with W13-04a-availability-exclusion sequenced after it.

=== STORAGE RULED 2026-08-06: OPTION B, FULL HISTORY. THE FORK IS CLOSED. ===

patient_terms_acceptances, one row per acceptance, its own RLS policy and an isolation test in the same PR per CLAUDE.md rule 2 and the repo RLS rule. Rationale as ruled: this is the sole legal path to the fee line, terms change over time, only append-only history answers what a patient agreed to at a given DATE, and option A is not upgradeable to B after the fact because the overwritten values are gone.

MIGRATION: slug only, number DERIVED AT AUTHORING, never reserved here. Full post-0057 apply-block doctrine - worktree path verified against the filesystem before the block is issued, a COMMITTED checker naming exactly what the migration created (a TABLE, so check-migration-tables.mjs, never a one-off), evidence written in the SAME TURN the output arrives. Apply before merge. Ivan runs the block after strategy validates it.

=== RECON CLOSED 2026-08-06. THE THREE OUTSTANDING ITEMS ARE READ, AND ONE OF THEM IS A TRAP. ===

1. THE RENDER LOOP IS GENERIC. SignatureConsent.tsx:313 is CONSENT_ITEM_KEYS.map((key) => ...). A third key renders automatically with no component change.

2. THE i18n SHAPE IS TYPE-ENFORCED. CONSENT_ITEM_STRINGS is Record<ConsentItemKey, ConsentItemStrings> (consent.ts:94) keyed clinical.consent.<item>.label and .body. Adding a key to ConsentItemKey without adding its strings is a COMPILE error, so that site cannot be forgotten.

3. NO CALLER ASSUMES EXACTLY TWO KEYS IN A WAY THAT BREAKS SILENTLY. RecordForm.tsx:113 spreads readConsentState(d) and sets one key by variable - fully key-agnostic. emptyConsentState() hardcodes both keys but ConsentState is Record<ConsentItemKey, ConsentDecision>, so omitting a third is again a compile error. Every addition site is forced by the type system.

*** AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS IS DANGEROUS. THE TRAP, NAMED SO THE AUTHORING SESSION DOES NOT WALK INTO IT: ***
Adding "terms" to CONSENT_ITEM_KEYS makes everything COMPILE AND RENDER CORRECTLY, and it will be WRONG. The render loop picks it up, the type system is satisfied, the checkbox appears in the right place with the right ternary - and RecordForm.tsx:113 then writes it into data._consent, which is PER CLINICAL RECORD. The card requires PER PATIENT. The result would be an acceptance that exists on one record and not on the patient, a fee gate that answers the wrong question, and NOTHING IN CI WOULD FAIL. There is no test that could catch it, because every existing test asserts the per-record behaviour that is correct for treatment and rgpd.

SO THE TERMS ITEM IS NOT A THIRD ConsentItemKey. It renders IN that block for the user, and persists through a SEPARATE path to patient_terms_acceptances. The authoring PR must keep CONSENT_ITEM_KEYS at two and add the terms row beside the map rather than inside it, or add a test that asserts _consent never contains a terms key. Preferably both.

NOTHING WAS COMMITTED BY THIS RECON. Authoring opens the moment #830 merges.

=== #833 GREEN 2026-08-07. RETURN CONDITION: MIGRATION APPLY REQUEST. ===

The migration half of LOOP 5 is complete and proven. What CI actually proved, beyond a green tick: the RLS suite ran against a real Postgres and confirmed tenant isolation both ways, recorded_by pinned to auth.uid(), UPDATE and DELETE both refused, the blank-version CHECK, the table gate being exactly SELECT plus INSERT for authenticated and nothing at all for patient, and a negative control proving RLS was actually on rather than everything being refused.

TWO GRANT MISTAKES WERE CAUGHT BY TESTS, NOT BY REVIEW, and both are worth remembering. First, the migration granted NOTHING - a new table does not inherit 0003 blanket grant - which made both append-only assertions pass for the wrong reason while the table was unusable. The positive control caught it. Second, the comment claimed the REVOKE was insurance against a FUTURE blanket grant; it is load-bearing TODAY, because Supabase default privileges hand authenticated UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE at CREATE time. Delete that REVOKE and the table silently stops being append-only.

ONE FLAKE, EVIDENCED NOT SHRUGGED AT. nif-required.spec.ts timed out on all three retries at 0df8668 and passed at a4de096, with a diff between those commits of comment-only SQL plus one db test - no app code, no seed, no spec. Re-run passed in 6m28s. Recorded on LE-e2e-nif-edit-404 as its second occurrence.

NEXT: strategy validates docs/migration-apply-0058.md, then Ivan runs it, then the journal output is verified and written into the repo IN THE SAME TURN it arrives, then #833 merges. The ficha UI and the server action follow on the same branch after the apply.

=== APP HALF BUILT 2026-08-07, branch portal/W13-05a-ficha-terms-ui. ===

carrying the flag, the copy and THE GATE. The eleventh registry entry,

THE FEE LINE IS ON THE 24h REMINDER, NOT THE NO-SHOW NOTIFICATION, and the
briefing did not say which. Re-derived from the packet rather than assumed:
docs/notifications-approval-packet.md "Variante A / Variante B" are both the 24h

cards.title: Dark mode: an ink token should replace the hard-coded #fff on brand-filled controls

evidence.ref: #777 MERGED 2026-08-04T15:25:07Z, branch board/LE-darkmode-ink-token, squashed to 0158af7 on origin/main. docs/board/board.css only. Both defects closed and MEASURED, not eyeballed: white ink on the seven dark-mode accent fills scored 2.08:1 to 2.88:1, every one failing WCAG AA 4.5:1; the --on-accent token scores 6.58:1 to 9.13:1 on the same seven. Light mode is byte-identical (the token resolves to #ffffff). color-scheme is now restated in both [data-theme] blocks, so UA surfaces (scrollbars, native selects, date pickers) follow the viewer's toggle instead of the OS. Verified against the RENDERED output, since render-board.mjs inlines the CSS: 0 hardcoded #fff, 0 leftover #170a12, 4 --on-accent declarations, 4 --stakeholder declarations, 7 consumption sites, 2 color-scheme restatements.

cards.notes:
Found during the board-parity work and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED there, because both defects are visible changes to the platform board's dark mode and fixing them inside a byte-parity ticket would make the diff unreviewable: a reviewer could no longer tell an intended generalisation from an unrelated colour edit. Two defects. (1) `color-scheme: light dark` is declared only on `:root` (board.css:22) and never restated per [data-theme], so scrollbars, native select popups and date pickers follow the OS rather than the viewer's toggle. (2) Hard-coded #fff on light dark-mode fills, seven sites: board.css:216 .btn.primary (on dark --brand #45b9a7), board.css:287 .pips button.pass (for system-dark viewers who never touched the toggle - the #170a12 patch at board.css:286 is scoped to :root[data-theme="dark"] only), and the five .segrow.status button[aria-pressed="true"] fills at board.css:461-465 (shipped, blocked, in_flight, halted, todo). The fix is one theme-driven ink token used in all seven places, the same job --brand-ink already does for brand-tinted surfaces. Also worth folding in while there: two person-coupled sites that survived the parity work untouched because the additive-only rule forbade editing an existing declaration - board.css:323 colours the rodica_batch lane RAIL with var(--rodica), so on this board the STAKEHOLDER FEEDBACK lane wears a person's colour for a person who is not on it, and board.css:395 colours the `stakeholder` gate badge the same way, which five cards on this board carry. Neither is wrong-looking today; both are a token whose name has outlived its meaning.

--- CLOSED 2026-08-04 (#777) ---
The card's line citations for the two person-coupled sites were WRONG and were re-derived rather than transcribed: board.css:323 and :395 as written, 325 and 399 in fact. The seven #fff citations were correct.

Both were fixed with ONE token each rather than seven patches. --on-accent is deliberately not --ink: --ink is text on paper, --on-accent is text on a filled accent, and the two move in OPPOSITE directions between themes, which is why a single literal could never be right in both. --stakeholder carries the identical value to --rodica in both themes, so the role/person split is a rename by indirection with zero visual change; --rodica stays for the two sites that really do mean the person.

The deleted :root[data-theme="dark"] .pips button.pass patch was itself the shape of the bug: it fixed the gate pip only for viewers who had touched the toggle and left every system-dark viewer on 2.41:1.

ONE FINDING DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: light-mode --todo (#a86f10) with white ink is 4.25:1 and already failed 4.5:1 before this PR. Fixing it means changing a light-mode palette VALUE, which is a visible redesign rather than a tokenisation - and silently altering the light palette inside a dark-mode ticket is the same mistake this card was created to avoid. Flagged, not folded in.

board.css is shared, so the PLATFORM board picks the same fix up at its next render. No platform board JSON was touched from this portal session.

cards.title: Shard the Playwright e2e gate across three runners, required check name held stable

evidence.ref: #774 MERGED 2026-08-04 (5fc88a2). MEASURED, not estimated, on run 30942125889 - the first run where all three shards completed on one commit with the isolation defect fixed: shard 1 6m43s, shard 2 6m58s, shard 3 7m10s, aggregate gate 3s. Wall clock ~7m13s, and the number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average. Against the same day's unsharded runs on real code changes (12m30s, 13m00s, 13m22s, 13m57s, 14m08s) that is roughly a 45% cut. The split is now even - 27s between fastest and slowest - where before the fix it ran 6m27s to 13m22s because shard 3 was spending 6.3 minutes on doomed retries, which is exactly why no figure was quoted earlier. Required check name held: 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' reported and passed as the aggregate, and branch protection needed NO change - the hard constraint on the whole design.

cards.notes:
Not a Wave 13 loop. Infrastructure that pays back across every PR of the wave, dispatched by the owner before LOOP 1.

THE CONSTRAINT: branch protection pins three contexts by exact string, and a check context IS a job name. Sharding the existing job in place would have renamed its checks to 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB) (1)' and friends; the required context would never report again and every PR would hang forever on a check that no longer exists. So the work moved to a job named 'E2E shard' and a new aggregate job inherits the exact old name, runs no tests, and fails unless all three shards succeeded. NO REPOSITORY SETTINGS CHANGE IS NEEDED - which was the stated fallback condition.

Workflow file and matrix only: zero test-file edits, zero playwright.config.ts edits, retries untouched (no --retries flag on pull_request, so the config's CI ? 2 : 0 still governs).

VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED: setup runs in every shard. Pinned Playwright 1.60.0, runner/index.js:2443-2465 - the shard filter iterates rootSuite.suites, which holds top-level projects only, and dependency projects are prepended afterwards from the UNFILTERED suite. That is also why the invocation now passes --project=chromium alone: naming setup explicitly promotes it to top-level and puts its tests INTO the shard filter, the one arrangement where a shard could receive no setup tests.

THE RED PATH IS PROVEN, and not by a contrived test. A deliberate forced-failure run was planned; it turned out to be unnecessary because attempt 1 produced the exact scenario that needed proving: shard 3 genuinely failed while shards 1 and 2 passed, and the required check 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' went RED in 4 seconds. That is the partial-failure case - one leg red, two green - which is the one that matters and the one a designed-to-work argument could not have settled. `if: always()` plus a strict 'success' comparison behaved exactly as intended. Skipped is deliberately NOT accepted as success; this repo has already been bitten by a green that was really a skip.



--- CORRECTION AND DIAGNOSIS, 2026-08-04. THE EARLIER CHECKPOINT WAS WRONG. ---
Board checkpoint 01 (#776, merged) recorded that the cross-file-dependency hypothesis was CHECKED AND REFUTED. That was WRONG, and it was wrong because the check was too narrow: it asked who else REFERENCES the fixture constant AI_REVIEW_DRAFT, when the question that mattered was who else MUTATES the shared review queue. Correcting it here rather than leaving a merged board claim standing.

THE REAL CAUSE, proven rather than hypothesised. e2e/clinical.spec.ts:169-188 HARD-DELETES AI_DELETE_DRAFT, which fixtures.ts defines as a SECOND draft belonging to the SAME patient, Joao Pereira. e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts:36-39 finds its queue row by getByRole("row").filter({hasText: patientName}).first().
Unsharded, clinical.spec.ts runs BEFORE revisao-consulta.spec.ts (file order, c before r), so by the time revisao-consulta reads the queue there is exactly ONE Joao Pereira row and .first() is unambiguous.
Sharded, the local listing puts clinical.spec.ts in SHARD 1 and revisao-consulta.spec.ts in SHARD 3. AI_DELETE_DRAFT is therefore never deleted in shard 3, two Joao Pereira rows sit in the queue, and .first() selects the wrong one - whose Assumir never becomes clickable. Hence a 120s locator.click timeout, three times, 6.3 of the 10.4 minutes, which is also why shard 3 was the long pole.

THIS IS A LATENT TEST-ISOLATION DEFECT THAT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. revisao-consulta.spec.ts has always depended on another spec file having run first. Any change to file order would trigger it.

PARKED per the owner ceiling of one working session. The enabling fix is one line in a TEST file - scope the row by data-record-id, exactly as clinical.spec.ts:173 already does, instead of hasText + .first() - and this PR was dispatched with zero test-file edits, so it does not belong here.

UNBLOCK CONDITION, exact: authorise the one-line test-isolation fix to e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts as its own PR. Once that is on main, #774 needs no change of its own - re-run its checks and all three shards should go green.
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: authorise it. The defect is real independently of sharding and the fix makes the test say what it means.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN AND SURVIVES THE PARK: the required-check name held stable (three new E2E shard (N) contexts appeared, Playwright E2E (seeded DB) kept reporting, branch protection untouched); setup ran in all three shards; and the RED PATH works - one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds.
WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN: the wall-clock win. Shards 1 and 2 came in at 7m27s and 6m27s against the 13m21s baseline, but shard 3 spent 6.3 minutes on three doomed retries, so no honest speed figure exists until the test is fixed. The number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-04, and the park was the right call ---
Parking it rather than merging on a red run is what produced the correct diagnosis. Merging it green-by-retry would have shipped the shard split on top of a live test-isolation defect and left the next person to find it.

The red path was proven twice over: once by accident on attempt 1 (one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds), and the planned deliberate forced-failure run was never needed.

--- OWNER RULING 2026-08-05: THE SPEC DRIFT CHECK BECOMES REQUIRED. ---
Ivan is making the branch-protection change dashboard-side; no repo change is needed and none was made. THE EXACT CONTEXT STRING GITHUB LISTS IS THE JOB NAME, NOT THE WORKFLOW NAME, which is the same trap this card was created by: the workflow is named "OpenAPI drift" (.github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml:1) and the job is named "Validate spec + drift check" (:19). The string to tick is "Validate spec + drift check". If it is absent from the list, it is because GitHub only offers contexts it has SEEN report on the default branch in the last week - the workflow is path-filtered (apps/api/app/api, apps/web/app/api/v1, docs/api/openapi.yaml, scripts/check-openapi-drift.mjs, its own file), so it does not run on PRs that touch none of those. Merge one PR that touches a path in that filter and the context appears.

cards.title: Address the review-queue row by record id, not by patient name

evidence.ref: #785 MERGED 2026-08-04 (0b32eed). Owner-authorised. revisao-consulta.spec.ts now passes in 8.3s with no retry, where in shard 3 it was timing out at 120s three times over. Two files: the spec's locator, plus data-record-id on the review queue's desktop <tr> and mobile <li>.

cards.notes:
A LATENT DEFECT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. fixtures.ts seeds TWO drafts for the same patient (AI_REVIEW_DRAFT and AI_DELETE_DRAFT, both Joao Pereira). revisao-consulta.spec.ts found its row by patient NAME and took .first(), which was only ever correct because clinical.spec.ts runs earlier in file order (c before r) and hard-deletes the second one at clinical.spec.ts:169-188. So the spec silently depended on ANOTHER SPEC FILE having run. Renaming a spec, or adding one that sorts between them, would have broken it with no sharding involved.

WIDER THAN A TEST EDIT, and flagged as such at the time: the queue row carried only a React `key`, which never reaches the DOM, so there was nothing addressable. data-record-id was added to the markup, mirroring the attribute the patient Registos tab already uses - which is how clinical.spec.ts:173 targets that very record. Inert: no behaviour, no styling, no data beyond an id already in that row's own links.

SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION IN BETWEEN, recorded because the lesson is the useful part: putting the attribute on BOTH layouts and then writing an unqualified [data-record-id=...] locator matched two elements - the queue renders desktop table AND mobile list into the DOM at all times, hidden by CSS - and Playwright strict mode refused it. The hook was right; the selector was ambiguous. Qualifying it to tr[...] fixed it. It shipped because an e2e locator change was made without running e2e, the same shape of miss as running a filtered test suite instead of the root gates.

Owner screenshot of docs/notifications-approval-packet.md section 3 shows the 48h body action line reading 'Para confirmar, remarcar ou cancelar:' with the 24h bodies unchanged at 'Para remarcar ou cancelar:'. That is exactly the scope JP approved - one line in one body. Code side: apps/web/lib/reminders/templates.ts amended in both locales, and the 48h email carries its own approvedAt of 2026-08-05 via a separate constant so the nine bodies JP approved on 2026-08-03 keep their date.

cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-04:

"Patient confirm-from-SMS is deferred post-launch. No short-link scheme is built pre-launch. Counsel's confirm-only token row stays enforced server-side. For launch the confirm action is delivered by the 48h email channel only. Next session verifies whether the approved email body already carries the confirm link; if it does not, that gap returns to Ivan as a JP re-approval question, never as a silent wording change."

WHY THIS RULING EXISTS. The token is too long for a single SMS segment, so apps/web/lib/reminders/dispatch.ts sends the 24h SMS with the clinic phone number and NO LINK. Counsel's per-offset matrix (docs/rgpd-token-flow.md section 5) gives that offset confirm-only, and W13-01 enforces it inside the signature - a confirm-scoped token refuses cancel before any database contact. So the RULE is built and unit-tested; only its DELIVERY channel is absent.

NEXT SESSION'S CHECK, and it is a real one: read the approved 48h email body in apps/web/lib/reminders/notification-registry.ts and confirm it actually renders the rescheduleLink. All ten bodies are approved:true / approvedBy JP (#766). If the confirm link is NOT in the approved wording, adding it CHANGES AN APPROVED CLINICAL BODY, which re-opens JP's approval. That returns to Ivan as a question. It is never edited quietly.

VERIFICATION DONE 2026-08-05, AND THE GAP IS REAL. This ruling instructed: 'Next session verifies whether the approved email body already carries the confirm link; if it does not, that gap returns to Ivan as a JP re-approval question, never as a silent wording change.' It has been verified against committed code, and the answer is nuanced enough that both halves matter.

THE MECHANISM CARRIES CONFIRM. apps/web/lib/reminders/dispatch.ts:219 signs the 48h email link with scope 'confirm_cancel' (and :446 likewise), the scope travels INSIDE the signature (link-token.ts:29-42), and the landing page derives its offered actions from that scope, rendering both a confirm and a cancel CTA (apps/web/app/r/[token]/page.tsx:54-61). So a patient who opens the 48h email link IS offered confirm. Counsel's per-offset matrix is satisfied by the code.

THE WORDING DOES NOT. The approved pt-PT 48h body (apps/web/lib/reminders/templates.ts:56-65) reads 'Para remarcar ou cancelar: {{reschedule_link}}' - reschedule or cancel. It never mentions confirming. The EN body says the same ('To reschedule or cancel'). So the confirm action is available but UNDISCOVERABLE: a patient reading that line has no reason to click in order to confirm.

WHY THIS MATTERS AT LAUNCH RATHER THAN LATER. This ruling makes the 48h email the ONLY delivery channel for confirm pre-launch, because the token is too long for a single SMS segment and no short-link scheme is being built. If the only channel that can deliver confirm never tells the patient it can, then confirm effectively does not ship, even though every line of it is built and tested.

NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. Changing the body is a copy change to one of the ten bodies JP approved blanket on 2026-08-03, and any change re-opens the clinical review and enters the registry approved:false. The ruling itself forbids the silent edit in as many words. So it goes back as a question, and the card is blocked on Ivan to carry it to JP. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT if JP wants the smallest possible change: amend the 48h line only, to name confirming alongside remarcar/cancelar, leaving the 24h bodies untouched - the 24h SMS is confirm-only by counsel's matrix and carries no link at all.

ANSWERED 2026-08-05. JP approved amending the SINGLE 48h line, relayed by Ivan. The line becomes 'Para confirmar, remarcar ou cancelar'. NO OTHER BODY CHANGE - the other nine approved bodies are untouched, and the 24h bodies keep their existing wording because the 24h SMS is confirm-only by counsel's matrix and carries no link at all.

UNBLOCKED from Ivan's column: the decision is made, so what remains is the edit itself. Patient-visible, so WF-03 applies and the rendered body goes into VERIFY-QUEUE rather than closing on a green gate.

CLOSED 2026-08-05 on the owner's screenshot. The gap this ruling existed to find - confirm built and enforced server-side but never mentioned to the patient in the only channel that could deliver it - is closed.

The owner found it by opening the portal. No CI signal existed for it, and none was going to.

IN FORCE FROM NOW, not from execution. It changes what 'shipped' means on this board for any card a patient can see: merged and green is necessary and NOT sufficient. The evidence field on such a card carries a screenshot reference from the owner, kind 'screenshot', alongside the PR.

It does not apply to infrastructure, migrations, CI or board work, which no patient can observe and for which a passing gate IS the proof.

cards.title: Portal deployment failure: every apps/api call from the portal is failing

evidence.ref: CLOSED 2026-08-05 on the DEPLOYED portal per WF-03. Ivan screenshots of osteojp-portal.vercel.app/portal/dashboard: "Ola, ZZ" with the greeting populated and the appointments card rendering, and /portal/appointments rendering "Nao tem consultas marcadas" - the LOADED-AND-EMPTY state, not the PL-34 error state. That distinction is the proof: before PL-34 both a real empty list and a failed fetch rendered identically.

cards.notes:
ROOT CAUSE, TWO LAYERS, BOTH PROVEN AND BOTH FIXED.

LAYER 1 - ZERO PATIENT LINKAGE. All 21 prod patients had auth_user_id NULL. The access-token hook (public.custom_access_token_hook, 0010_patient_identity_layer.sql:204-221) resolves a patient by p.auth_user_id = v_user_id; on a miss it stamps NO claims and still returns the event, so a perfectly signed token is issued carrying nothing. parsePatientPrincipal (packages/auth/patient.ts:50-56) then rejects it and every patient route 401s. No error, no log, nothing observable - which is why it survived.

LAYER 2 - STAFF IDENTITY PREEMPTION. Ivan was testing as owner staff accounts (info@a-and-i-automation.com, then ivanbong333@gmail.com, the latter proven staff role_slug=owner by the 0b check BEFORE any write). The hook checks the staff branch FIRST; a staff identity can never receive patient claims. Correct design, wrong test identity. The portal shell admits any valid session and role enforcement happens at the api, which is why login appeared to succeed while every data call 401ed.

THE FIX: a dedicated non-staff identity linked to a dedicated ZZ TESTE patient row. No real patient record was touched - linking a real patient to Ivan's login would have handed him another person's clinical data, which is the boundary this entire wave exists to defend.

BUILD HALF, closed earlier the same incident: the deployed osteojp-api was serving a stale build - /api/v1/patient/profile 404ed while /api/health answered. A no-cache rebuild of the SAME commit (1131f2d) flipped it to a correct 401. Cause confirmed, no code change.

FALSE TRAILS KILLED ALONG THE WAY, recorded so they are not re-walked: root-directory config (verified correct), deployment protection (api root page renders openly), split-brain Supabase projects (anon key identical across all three Vercel projects), stale build (production current at 1131f2d), path mismatch (both route files exist at the composed paths), middleware 404 (updateSession only ever returns NextResponse.next), and the two health-URL 404s which were CHAT GUESSES at paths that never existed - the real path is /api/health.

THE CHECK THAT PAID FOR ITSELF: step 0b, the staff-exclusion predicate, ran BEFORE any write and caught ivanbong333@gmail.com as owner staff. Without it the fix would have been applied to an identity that could never work, and the failure would have looked identical.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WAVE, carded against LOOP 3: no patient portal login can ever have worked against prod, because provisionPatientAuthUser (activation.ts:65-95) is the ONLY code that ever wrote auth_user_id and it is registered approved:false and slated for deletion. LOOP 3 must SUPPLY the linkage mechanism, not merely replace activation.

cards.title: apps/web DB-gated harness, so LOOP 1's remaining DoD lines can be proven

evidence.ref: #791. DB-gated job, run 30988239651: 'lib/reminders/redeem.db.test.ts (7 tests) 538ms' PASSED, and the skip-guard reports 'RUN redeem.db.test.ts 7/7 executed' followed by 'All 9 DB-gated suites executed non-privileged against the seeded DB.' Executed, not skipped - which is the whole point of the card.

cards.notes:
NEXT SESSION'S FIRST ITEM. LOOP 1 (W13-01) cannot reach its Definition of Done without this, which is why W13-01 is still in flight and PG3 is still FAIL.

THE BLOCKER. The DB-gated job runs `pnpm exec vitest run` with working-directory packages/db (.github/workflows/db-tests.yml:122-128). redeemActionToken lives in apps/web. packages/db importing from apps/web is the wrong dependency direction, so the three outstanding DoD lines have nowhere to run today.

THE THREE PIECES:
1. A test-file CONVENTION for apps/web tests needing a live database - they must SKIP cleanly when DATABASE_URL is unset, or ci.yml (which has no database) goes red. packages/db/tests/rls-harness.ts already models this with `const live = Boolean(url)` and `live ? describe : describe.skip`.
2. A WORKFLOW STEP in db-tests.yml running that suite with working-directory apps/web, against the Supabase stack already stood up in that job.
3. THE SKIP-GUARD. .github/scripts/assert-rls-executed.mjs is pointed at packages/db results (db-tests.yml:130-136) and asserts the suites actually EXECUTED rather than silently skipping. It must cover the new suite too, or an apps/web DB suite that skips reports green and proves nothing - which is the exact failure mode that guard exists to catch, and the same shape as the vitest include hole found in W13-01d where an app-level test was never collected at all.

THEN the three DoD lines land: action and consumption commit or roll back TOGETHER with a forced failure between them; a cancel token issued at 48h and redeemed at 30h before start refused with the pt-PT telephone copy; a refusal writes an audit row. Plus the partial line - that a consumed token's response is byte-identical to a forged token's.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-05 ---
Three pieces landed: the suite (gates on DATABASE_URL, so ci.yml skips it cleanly), the db-tests.yml step running it against the same Supabase stack, and the skip-guard extension that makes the first two mean anything - assert-rls-executed.mjs now merges SEVERAL vitest JSON reports and hard-requires redeem.db.test.ts. Non-json arguments are still ignored, so the historical argv[3] run-log invocation is untouched.

THE GUARD WAS PROVEN TWICE. Once synthetically, against a hand-built report where the suite skips and the other eight pass - exit 1, 'redeem.db.test.ts: 0/1, 1 not-run'. And once for real: the suite's FIRST CI execution went red on a fixture bug (a JS Date bound as a timestamptz through the raw sql template, which the driver rejects; drizzle's typed insert builder converts it, a raw template does not). All seven cases failed identically at seedAppointment, so nothing about redeemActionToken had been exercised - and the guard could not have hidden that. A harness whose first act is to catch its own author is a harness that works.

cards.title: Duplicate NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL scoped to Preview, Sensitive, value unreadable

If previews are ever used for portal review, it silently decides which API every preview deployment talks to, and a wrong value there is indistinguishable from a correct one until a preview misbehaves.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT, post-fix: delete it and recreate with a known, non-sensitive value. NEXT_PUBLIC_* is compiled into client bundles by definition, so marking it Sensitive protects nothing while costing all verifiability. Owner action on his own screen; this terminal makes no cloud calls.

cards.title: Supabase Auth SMTP cannot send - password recovery is dead in production

evidence.ref:
CLOSED 2026-08-05 by Ivan, dashboard-side, with live deployed verification.

FOUND STATE: Supabase custom SMTP enabled, host smtp.resend.com, port 465, username resend - but the Sender email address was clinic.osteojp@gmail.com. Resend refuses unverified sender domains and gmail.com can never be verified, so EVERY Supabase auth email (password recovery, sign-in links, email changes) failed silently from setup onward. No error surfaced anywhere.

FIX: Sender email address changed to no-reply@send.osteojp.pt, sender name OsteoJP kept, no other field touched, saved with the stored credential intact.

LIVE VERIFICATION, Ivan's screen, 2026-08-05 11:36: an auth email requested from the DEPLOYED login page arrived within one minute. Inbox shows sender OsteoJP <no-reply@send.osteojp.pt>, subject 'Your sign-in link'. The link was deliberately NOT clicked and was left to expire - correct discipline, since clicking it would have minted a session.

cards.notes:
LAUNCH-BLOCKING. A patient who forgets their password has NO recovery path.

REPO-GROUNDED HYPOTHESIS: apps/api/lib/notify/clients.ts:53-56 records that the verified Resend identity lives on send.osteojp.pt and that a root-domain sender such as no-reply@osteojp.pt is REJECTED by Resend. That exact defect was found and fixed in application code. Supabase Auth SMTP is a SEPARATE sender configuration the app code never touches, so if its sender is a root-domain address it fails the same way.

WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE: PG5 REMINDERS passed using Resend DIRECTLY from app code via REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM. Same provider, different configuration surface. The notification-lane sweep covered code; this is dashboard config.

IVAN CHECKS: Project Settings -> Authentication -> SMTP Settings -> Sender email. It must be a verified identity on send.osteojp.pt.

NOT fixed during INC-05 by the one-variable-at-a-time rule; the portal test was unblocked by creating an identity with a typed password instead.

SEVERITY RE-ASSESSED 2026-08-05 against WF-07 (R4) and Decision D, without changing the card's state. Decision D makes patient login a 6-digit SMS OTP with no password at all, and WF-07 makes the account link a phone-match at OTP claim time. Once LOOP 3 ships, PATIENT password recovery is not merely broken, it is GONE as a concept - there is no password to recover. What survives is STAFF recovery, which still runs through Supabase Auth SMTP and is still dead. So this remains a real defect with a smaller blast radius than when it was filed: staff-only, not patients. Stays blocked on Ivan; the fix is a Supabase console action and every console write is owner-terminal. Re-check after LOOP 3 merges to confirm no patient-facing path still depends on it.

--- CLOSED 2026-08-05 ---

THE HYPOTHESIS ON THIS CARD WAS RIGHT, AND THE MECHANISM WAS EXACTLY AS PREDICTED. The card said: apps/api/lib/notify/clients.ts records that the verified Resend identity lives on send.osteojp.pt and a root-domain sender is REJECTED; Supabase Auth SMTP is a separate sender configuration the app code never touches, so if its sender is wrong it fails the same way. It was worse than a root domain - it was a gmail.com address, which can never be verified at all.

THE FAILURE CLASS IS FAIL-CLOSED-INVISIBLE, the same one as the INC-05 hook miss: the system refused correctly and told nobody. There was no error in the app, no bounce to the clinic, and no signal in any dashboard - the only way to find it was to ask why something that should have arrived never did. Recorded in docs/notifications-work-notes.md under its own dated section.

CONFIG GROUND TRUTH, THE THREE SENDERS, so nobody merges them again:
  auth mail  = no-reply@send.osteojp.pt  (Supabase Auth SMTP, dashboard-side, NOT an env var)
  invites    = convites@send.osteojp.pt  (INVITES_EMAIL_FROM, osteojp-platform, all scopes,
               non-Sensitive, confirmed set)
  reminders  = REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM      (unchanged)
Three senders, three configuration surfaces, one verified domain (send.osteojp.pt). The auth one is the only one NOT in an env var, which is precisely why it was invisible to every code sweep.

cards.title: Owner ruling R1: extending the patient-change event contract from 2 kinds to 4 is growth, not a redesign
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R1, answering Q1):

"R1 - event contract (Q1): extending the patient-change contract from 2 to 4 kinds (booked, cancelled, rescheduled, pedido de marcacao) is ratified as growth of the existing contract, not a redesign. The wave doc's consume-do-not-redesign clause is satisfied. Proceed."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. WAVE-13.md LOOP 2 section 5 forbids redesigning the event contract the precondition PR stubbed, and LOOP 2 section 6 makes an insufficient contract a HALT rather than a fork. The contract as committed carries two kinds and PG4 requires four, so the loop could not start without knowing whether adding two kinds counted as the forbidden redesign. It does not.

RE-DERIVED FROM MAIN, not taken from the dispatch: apps/api/lib/notifications/patient-change.ts:31 reads `export type PatientChangeKind = "cancelled" | "rescheduled";` - exactly the 2 kinds this ruling grows to 4. The file's own header calls the contract FIXED and says adding a field is meant to be a deliberate act with a diff. This ruling is that deliberate act, recorded before the diff.

SCOPE LIMIT. It ratifies adding kinds. It does not license changing the existing field set, loosening the PII rule in that file's header (identifiers and instants only, no name, phone, email, service name or clinical content), or changing the audience shape. Those remain redesign.

CONSUMED BY: W13-02 (LOOP 2). Closes one of that loop's two halt conditions; see WF-05 for the other.

cards.title: Owner ruling R2: for dual-therapist services, BOTH assigned therapists are notified
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R2, answering Q2):

"R2 - dual-therapist (Q2): derived from JP's standing ruling that every patient-initiated change notifies reception plus the assigned therapist: for dual-therapist services, BOTH assigned therapists are notified. Engineering derivation of JP 2026-08-03, no new JP trip."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. WAVE-13.md LOOP 2 section 6 halts the loop if fan-out to 'assigned therapist' is ambiguous for multi-therapist appointments, and says ASK, DO NOT GUESS. Massagem 4 Maos and Sessao Familia are dual-participant services and the primary/secondary model is locked, so 'the assigned therapist' has two referents. This resolves it to BOTH, by derivation from JP's existing standing ruling rather than by a new clinical decision.

WHY DERIVATION IS LEGITIMATE HERE, since guessing a product decision is forbidden: JP's ruling of 2026-08-03 (WAVE-13.md section 1.2, docs/notifications-work-notes.md:206-211) is that every patient-initiated change reaches reception AND the assigned therapist, in-app. Notifying only one of two assigned therapists would leave a therapist who is on the appointment unaware that the patient moved it. That is the failure JP's ruling forbids, so BOTH is the only reading consistent with the ruling already in force. The alternative - notify the primary only - would be a NEW restriction JP never stated, and inventing that is the actual guess.

BUILD CONSEQUENCE. NotificationAudience at patient-change.ts:38-43 carries a single `practitionerId: string`. Serving this ruling means that field admits more than one practitioner. That is a contract change, licensed under WF-04's growth reading, and it must carry a test proving a dual-therapist appointment produces an entry for BOTH assigned therapists and still none for an unassigned one.

CONSUMED BY: W13-02 (LOOP 2). Closes that loop's second halt condition.

cards.title: Owner ruling R3: the OTP rate limiter gets a durable store on the EXISTING Postgres - no new vendor
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R3, answering Q3):

"R3 - OTP rate limiter (Q3): durable store approved, implemented on the EXISTING Postgres. NO new external vendor: a vendor addition reopens the lawyer's subprocessor annex mid-close. If Postgres genuinely cannot serve the requirement, halt-card with reasoning, never add a vendor silently."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. WAVE-13.md LOOP 3 section 6 halts if the rate-limit store is undecided. apps/api/lib/rate-limit/limiter.ts exists on main; whether OTP limits could live in memory, needed Postgres, or justified a Redis-class dependency was open. It is Postgres.

THE REASON IS LEGAL, NOT TECHNICAL, and that is why it is stated as a hard constraint rather than a preference. A new external vendor is a new subprocessor. The clinic's RGPD counsel work is mid-close (docs/rgpd-token-flow.md, LE-rgpd-token-flow-to-lawyer, LE-inngest-dpa, LE-dpf-participant-list all open). Adding a subprocessor now reopens the annex and costs more than the engineering saves. This also sits under standing rule 13, no new third-party dependency or vendor without asking first.

ESCAPE HATCH, and its shape is specified so it cannot be used as cover: if Postgres genuinely cannot serve the requirement, the answer is a HALT CARD with the reasoning written out - not a vendor added quietly, and not a weaker limit shipped in silence. A rate limiter that cannot meet its own spec must say so on the board.

CONSUMED BY: W13-03 (LOOP 3). If the store needs a table it is migration-bearing; WF-11 (R8) governs the choreography.

R3 MUTATED 2026-08-05 BY WF-15, AND THE RULING SURVIVES IT. A new vendor no longer trips a lawyer-annex question inside engineering; it is carded to external counsel for review instead. THE NO-NEW-VENDOR DEFAULT FOR OTP STORAGE STANDS UNCHANGED.

Worth being precise about why, because the original ruling's stated reason was the legal one and that reason has now moved off this board: the ENGINEERING justification is independent and unaffected. A durable counter on a Postgres we already run, back up and hold a DPA for costs no new operational surface; Upstash or equivalent adds a second datastore to the failure model of the login path. The table shipped in 0056 and the decision does not need re-litigating.

cards.title: Owner ruling R4: patient linkage is phone-match at OTP claim time, and it REFUSES on anything but exactly one match
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R4, answering Q4):

"R4 - linkage mechanism (Q4): phone-match at OTP claim time, per Decision D. If EXACTLY ONE live patient row (deleted_at null, merged_into_id null, auth_user_id null) carries the proven phone, link it. Zero matches, multiple matches, or any candidate already linked: REFUSE with a clear pt-PT message directing the patient to the clinic. Card the staff-assisted activation path as post-launch. Mis-linking a medical record is the failure class the refusal exists to prevent."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. Decision D (WAVE-13.md section 1.4) makes patient login a 6-digit SMS OTP, phone only. It does not say how a proven phone number becomes a link to a patient row. Without that, LOOP 3 cannot build the claim step.

THE PREDICATE IS EXACT, and every clause of it is load-bearing. A candidate row must have deleted_at null (not soft-deleted), merged_into_id null (not the losing side of a patient merge), and auth_user_id null (not already claimed by someone). EXACTLY ONE such row must carry the proven phone. Any other count refuses. So does any candidate that is already linked - a phone reaching an already-claimed row is either a shared number or a re-registration, and neither is safe to resolve automatically.

IT IS DELIBERATELY FAIL-CLOSED AND WILL REFUSE REAL PATIENTS. Shared household numbers, a clinic row holding the wrong phone, a patient with two rows: all refuse. That is the trade the owner made explicitly, and the reason is on the ruling - mis-linking a medical record hands one patient another patient's clinical history. A refused login is an inconvenience and a phone call. A mis-link is a data breach with two named patients in it.

REQUIRED SHAPE OF THE BUILD: the refusal copy is pt-PT, in packages/i18n, and directs the patient to contact the clinic. It must NOT tell the patient which predicate failed - 'no row found' versus 'several rows found' versus 'already claimed' are three different disclosures about who else exists in the database, so the refusal is generic, exactly as the token rejection is generic under counsel's section 3. Refusal-style tests per the Decision B precedent: zero-match refuses, multi-match refuses, already-linked refuses, and the single live match links.

FOLLOW-ON CARDED: LE-staff-assisted-activation, post-launch, for the patients this legitimately locks out.

CONSUMED BY: W13-03 (LOOP 3).

cards.title: Owner ruling R5: delete sendPatientActivation - it grants a session by design and has no caller
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R5, answering Q5):

"R5 - sendPatientActivation (Q5): delete it. It grants a session by design, violating Decision D, and has no caller. Include a refusal-style test where applicable, per the Decision B precedent."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. WAVE-13.md LOOP 3 step 7 makes this function's fate a decision to be taken inside the loop, and section 6 halts the loop if it turns out to have a live caller. The board has carried it as a CANDIDATE FOR OUTRIGHT DELETION since seeding. It is now decided: delete.

RE-DERIVED FROM MAIN before recording, per standing rule 1.6. A full caller search across the repo (git grep over *.ts, *.tsx, *.md) returns: the definition at apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:167; its own test file apps/api/lib/auth/activation.test.ts (8 references, all inside that suite); a comment at apps/api/lib/notify/registry.ts:8 that already records it as DEAD CODE with no caller; and three documentation mentions. NO PRODUCTION CALL SITE EXISTS. The halt condition in LOOP 3 section 6 is therefore not triggered.

WHY DELETION RATHER THAN LEAVING IT DORMANT. It mints a Supabase RECOVERY link and delivers it by SMS. A recovery link is a session grant. Decision D says no password, no magic link, no session minted from any other artefact. Dead code that grants a session is one route handler away from being live code that grants a session, and it is registered approved:false today only because the notification registry happens to gate it. Deleting it removes the capability rather than the permission.

SIDE EFFECT THAT CLOSES A TRACKED RESIDUAL: fallback 6 in the loud-at-boot inventory (apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:117, PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL silently omitted) was deliberately LEFT because the code was dead. Deleting the function retires that residual instead of fixing it. Reflect that on LE-env-sweep-scope when the deletion merges, and check whether PATIENT_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL and PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL become unreferenced.

TEST OBLIGATION. 'Refusal-style test where applicable' per the Decision B precedent: after deletion there is no function left to test, so the enforceable artefact is a test asserting that NO code path mints a Supabase recovery link or any other session for a patient. That is the property Decision D actually protects, and it survives the function it was written about.

CONSUMED BY: W13-03 (LOOP 3).

cards.title: Owner ruling R6: owner verifications are batched - trigger at 3 or more waiting, or when nothing else is buildable

Trigger ONE batched checklist session when 3 or more items are waiting OR when nothing else is buildable. Checklist format: numbered, one URL plus expected screen per item. Ivan's deployed screenshot remains the only closer for patient-visible cards per WF-03."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. WF-03 makes the owner's deployed-screen observation the only closer for a patient-visible card. Applied naively that interrupts him once per card. This sets the interrupt policy without weakening the standard.

IT DOES NOT DILUTE WF-03. Batching changes WHEN he is asked, never WHAT counts. A patient- visible card still closes only on his observation of the deployed URL. Green gates still close nothing patient-visible. PG3 flipping today on his /r/anything check is the pattern.

cards.title: Owner ruling R7: no launch date - the condition is a patient completing every planned portal feature end to end

WHAT IT RESOLVES. Whether schedule pressure could trim wave scope. It cannot. There is no date to miss, so there is nothing to trade scope against.

'2-3 days' is the owner's EXPECTATION at current cadence, and it is not a commitment, not a deadline, and never a reason to cut a DoD line or skip a verification. 'A patient can use every planned portal feature start to end' is stricter than 9/9 on the launch gate: it is an end-to-end patient journey on the deployed app, which is the WF-03 standard applied to the whole portal rather than card by card. Expect a final batched verification session under WF-09 to be the thing that establishes it.
