cards.title: Owner ruling R8: migration choreography unchanged - author, PR, paste-ready apply block, halt THAT loop, verify journal, then merge
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R8, answering Q8):

"R8 - migration applies (Q8): choreography unchanged for the two remaining migration-bearing loops (slugs booking-modes and terms-acceptance, numbers re-derived at authoring). Author, open PR, produce Ivan's paste-ready apply block (one command per line, no backticks, zsh, prod-apply worktree at ~/Documents/Projects/GitHub/osteojp-prod-apply, env ~/osteojp-secrets/new-prod.env), halt THAT LOOP until Ivan pastes journal output, verify the journal before merge. While a migration loop waits, work any card that does not depend on its merge. One migration in flight at a time, repo-wide. Ivan has committed to same-day turnaround."

WHAT IS NEW HERE, since the choreography itself is unchanged from WAVE-13.md section 1.5: the WAIT IS NOT AN IDLE. Previously a migration halt stopped the lane. This ruling says the LOOP halts and the executor moves to any card that does not depend on that merge. Combined with the owner's same-day turnaround commitment, a migration costs a loop's latency and not the wave's.

THE APPLY BLOCK FORMAT IS PART OF THE RULING, not a nicety: one command per line, no backticks, zsh, run from the prod-apply worktree at ~/Documents/Projects/GitHub/osteojp-prod-apply with env ~/osteojp-secrets/new-prod.env. Env var NAMES only ever appear; values never enter this terminal's context. The branch is checked out DETACHED (git checkout origin/<branch>) because on main db:migrate silently no-ops - that has cost this project a migration twice.

APPLIED MEANS PASTED JOURNAL OUTPUT. A claim of applied without it is not an apply; see the 0038-0041 incident in docs/handoff/WAVE-12-CLOSE-20260727.md. Verify the journal BEFORE merge.

NUMBERS ARE RE-DERIVED AT AUTHORING, never reserved in advance. Last committed on main is 0054_patient_audit_log_and_token_consumption at journal idx 53, 54 entries, applied by W13-01. Next free is 0055. WAVE-13.md section 5 predicts 0055 for LOOP 4 and 0056 for LOOP 5, and that table is labelled INTENT, NOT TRUTH for the reason recorded there: a session-held reservation of 0053 was silently consumed by PL-31.

COUNT DISCREPANCY, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED. This ruling names TWO remaining migration-bearing loops. The board carries THREE: W13-04 (booking-modes) and W13-05 (terms-acceptance) as the ruling names, plus W13-02 (LOOP 2), whose gate is owner_merge precisely because persisted per-user notification state was expected to need a table, and whose DoD requires the unread count to be derived from data rather than a client-only counter. WAVE-13.md section 5 omits LOOP 2 from the reservations table, which is where the two came from. Treated as a count error and not a permission list: this choreography governs ANY migration-bearing loop, LOOP 2 included. LOOP 2's recon establishes whether it needs a table at all. Surfaced to the owner as a batched question.

--- R8 RE-AMENDMENT, OWNER 2026-08-05 ---

The LOOP 3 storage finding is RATIFIED IN FULL: an OTP codes table, a trusted-device table, and the durable rate-limit store on the existing Postgres per WF-06. LOOP 3 is migration-bearing.

THREE APPLIES REMAIN IN TOTAL from this point: the LOOP 3 auth-storage migration, booking-modes (LOOP 4), and terms-acceptance (LOOP 5). Slugs only. Numbers are re-derived at authoring time and NEVER pre-assigned in a plan or a card - the standing rule that exists because a session-held reservation of 0053 was silently consumed by PL-31.

THE COUNT HAS NOW BEEN WRONG TWICE IN THE SAME DIRECTION, both times by omitting a loop whose storage need was recorded in the repository rather than in the plan. LOOP 2 needed a table for per-user read state; LOOP 3 needs three, and the rate limiter says so in its OWN header (apps/api/lib/rate-limit/limiter.ts:8-20: 'the OTP flow therefore needs a DURABLE shared store before it ships. That store is a pending decision'). The lesson worth carrying rather than the correction: a migration count derived from a plan document undercounts, because the plan lists what was DESIGNED and the code records what is MISSING. Re-derive from the code.

The choreography itself is unchanged and governs all three: author, PR, paste-ready apply block, halt THAT LOOP for the owner's journal output, verify, then merge, working other cards meanwhile. One migration in flight repo-wide.

cards.title: Owner ruling R9: REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND and INVITES_LIVE_SEND stay off through acceptance - arming is a supervised launch-day step
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R9, answering Q9):

"R9 - live send (Q9): REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND stays false through all acceptance testing. Arming is a launch-day step with a supervised first send, canary-style. Add it to the launch-day sequence card. INVITES_LIVE_SEND likewise stays unarmed until launch."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. PG5 passes and all ten patient bodies are JP-approved, so REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND is now the only thing between an approved body and a real patient's phone (WAVE-13.md section 1.4). Whether acceptance testing needed it armed was open. It does not.

BOTH FLAGS, and the second one matters more than it looks. INVITES_LIVE_SEND governs the staff invite path, which LE-env-sweep-scope proved is NOT Inngest-driven - lib/admin/staff.ts -> lib/invites/email.ts -> sendEmail in lib/reminders/clients.ts. Before #778 it could be armed with its env missing and degrade silently to a temporary-password hand-off with no email, no error and no boot signal. It now fails loudly, which is exactly why arming it is a deliberate supervised step rather than a checkbox.

SUPERVISED, CANARY-STYLE means the first send after arming is watched, to one known recipient, before any volume follows. The suppression path has never been observed end to end (LE-suppression-observation); the first armed send is when that observation becomes possible, so watch for the suppression log line then.

CARDED: LAUNCH-01 carries the launch-day sequence. LE-invites-live-send is answered by this ruling - the answer is HOLD - and folds into LAUNCH-01.

TEST THAT MUST NOT REGRESS: 'sends NOTHING with live send off, even though all 10 are approved' is load-bearing from here on, per Decision-in-force in WAVE-13.md section 1.4.

AMENDED 2026-08-11 BY docs/rulings/R9a-otp-live-send-not-separable.md. R9 ITSELF IS UNCHANGED and nothing in it is superseded: REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND and INVITES_LIVE_SEND stay off until supervised launch-day canaries, exactly as ruled.

WHAT R9a ADDS is a THIRD flag R9 never named. OTP_LIVE_SEND was proposed as SEPARABLE from the other two on blast-radius grounds - 'user-initiated and one-to-one'. That argument is FALSE AS BUILT and the amendment was VOIDED before it was written. The OTP request endpoint is unauthenticated, performs no patient lookup, and is one-to-ANY across ~200M accepted inputs (SEC-otp-unauthenticated-sms-pump). R9a's binding position: OTP_LIVE_SEND may be armed ONLY for the duration of a supervised acceptance sitting and MUST be disarmed at the end of it. Arming it and leaving it is PROHIBITED.

cards.title: Owner ruling R10: credential rotation confirmed by Ivan 2026-08-05 - the exposure card closes
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R10):

"R10 - security: owner credential rotation CONFIRMED by Ivan 2026-08-05. Close the exposure card."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. INC-06 recorded that live credentials sat in two committed docs since June - a dev Supabase database password with two connection URLs, an IfThenPay backoffice key and password, and a QA portal account password. The files were deleted, but the card's own text is explicit that deletion is not the fix: they have been in git history since June, so ROTATION IS THE ONLY FIX. The card was written to stay open until rotation was confirmed. It is now confirmed.

THE CARD IS NOT ON THIS BOARD, and this session did not move it. INC-06 lives on docs/board/prelaunch-board.json (the platform board), owner_terminal GREEN, status blocked on ivan. PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md section 6 states: 'The platform board is a different board. Do not duplicate its cards here and do not edit it from a portal session.' That instruction and this ruling's 'close the exposure card' point in opposite directions, so per standing rule 5 the conflict is REPORTED rather than silently reconciled, and the conservative side was taken: the ruling is recorded here as law, prelaunch-board.json is untouched, and the close is surfaced to the owner as a batched question.

WHAT THE CLOSE SHOULD RECORD WHEN IT HAPPENS, because INC-06 enumerates four owner actions and this confirmation is one line: (1) dev Supabase password for project ufbkzbyghvxtosyrkgjq rotated and propagated - note scripts/perf-seed-loadtest.mjs still references that project; (2) IfThenPay backoffice key and password rotated; (3) QA portal account reset or deactivated; (4) the git-history judgement call made, rewrite or accept rotation as sufficient. If the confirmation covers all four, the card closes whole. If it covers fewer, close what it covers and say which remain - never flip past the evidence, which is the rule PG3 was held under for a day.

RELATED: INC-04, the prod DB password exposure the owner accepted on 2026-08-02 with a commitment to rotate everything once the work was done. This confirmation appears to be that sweep landing.

=== HARD DEPENDENCY ADDED 2026-08-07: SECURITY DEFINER OWNERSHIP. ===

The rotation this ruling closes on is scoped as "rotate the exposed credentials".
There is a second-order effect nobody has recorded, and it is the reason this
appears here rather than only on its own card.

ROTATING A PASSWORD IS SAFE. Same role, new secret, no effect on function
ownership. That is the expected case and nothing changes.

CHANGING THE ROLE IS NOT. Every SECURITY DEFINER function in production is owned
by whoever ran migrate, no migration pins it, and RLS is ENABLE not FORCE so that
ownership IS the RLS bypass the availability path depends on. If a rotation moves
the apply to a different principal - a new service account, a personal login
replaced by a shared one, a project migration - every function applied afterwards
inherits a different owner, the set splits in two, and NOTHING DETECTS IT. CI
structurally cannot: supabase db reset builds a database where one principal
creates everything.

SO THE ROTATION PLAN MUST RECORD WHICH PRINCIPAL APPLIES MIGRATIONS, BEFORE AND
AFTER. If it changes, ownership is pinned for all twelve functions in the same
change and verified by reading pg_proc.proowner, not inferred.

Mechanism and the full failure analysis: docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md, section
"SECURITY DEFINER ownership is UNPINNED, and it is a rotation dependency". Card:
SEC-function-owner-unpinned, which holds the read-only query and gates any
migration on its result.

cards.title: Awaiting Ivan verification - the batched deployed-screen checklist queue (WF-09)
cards.notes:
THE MECHANISM WF-09 (R6) REQUIRES. This card's notes ARE the awaiting-Ivan-verification list. Every patient-visible card that is built, merged and green but not yet observed by the owner on a deployed URL lands here instead of interrupting him.

TRIGGER, verbatim from the ruling: ONE batched checklist session when 3 OR MORE items are waiting, OR when nothing else is buildable. Not per item.

FORMAT, verbatim from the ruling: numbered, one URL plus expected screen per item.

WHEN TRIGGERED: this card flips to status blocked, blocked_on ivan, which derives it into the BLOCKED ON PEOPLE lane under his column and starts the answer-latency clock. When his observations land, each closes its own card with evidence kind screenshot per WF-03, this list empties, and the card returns to todo.

QUEUE AS OF 2026-08-05, UNDER WF-16. It accumulates SILENTLY for the whole wave and is resolved in ONE acceptance session at wave end. It no longer triggers at 3, and this card is no longer blocked on Ivan between sessions - an item sitting here is not owed work, it is scheduled work.

PRUNED 2026-08-05 by owner ruling: the agenda grid and the portal login screen are OFF the queue. Both were already owner-verified on 2026-08-05 with evidence cited on their own cards, and re-checking a surface that has been seen is waste. THE SESSION COVERS ONLY SURFACES NEVER SEEN ON AN OWNER SCREEN.

1. NOTIFICATION CENTRE, POPULATED (W13-02, gate PG4 already passed on the empty state).
   TRIGGER, stated so nobody waits for it early: it verifies the first time a REAL patient change
   flows through the portal. There is no backfill, so entries exist only from the first cancel,
   reschedule or booking after deploy. Expected DURING the acceptance session itself, once OTP
   login lands and a patient can actually reach the portal to make one.
   EXPECTED: an entry for the change, visible to reception AND to the assigned therapist, with no
   service name and no clinical content on it.

2. THE OTP LOGIN FLOW end to end, once the session mint lands (W13-03).
   EXPECTED: request a code on a real phone, receive one SMS, enter it, reach the dashboard.
   Then the three degradation paths if reachable: no phone on file, a landline, a shared number -
   each showing pt-PT copy that names the clinic rather than an error.
   NOT YET RUNNABLE: OTP_LIVE_SEND is off and the session mint is unbuilt. Queued, not owed.

REMOVED FROM THIS QUEUE, verified 2026-08-05 and not to be re-run: the /r/[token] route check (flipped PG3), the bell and notification centre empty state (flipped PG4), the agenda grid with the :30 slot still booking, the 48h email wording, and the portal login screen after the magic-link removal. LE-token-roundtrip-observation left by deferral, not by verification.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-05, QUEUE ITEM 2 FORWARD PLAN. The OTP end-to-end check CANNOT be done with OTP_LIVE_SEND off - no SMS reaches a handset and there is no code to type. It therefore requires a SUPERVISED CANARY, armed for the acceptance session only, mirroring the reminders canary pattern: owner-supervised, armed at the start of the session, disarmed or explicitly confirmed still-armed at the end, with which one it was recorded on this card. OTP_LIVE_SEND STAYS OFF UNTIL THAT SESSION and no build turns it on. Arming is an owner action on the deployment environment, never an executor one. The arming and disarming steps are part of the acceptance session plan, not a separate request, so this ruling costs no extra touchpoint.

3. SPLIT-SHIFT AVAILABILITY (W13-A), staff-visible, WF-03 applies.
   EXPECTED: /admin/staff, Gerir on a therapist, Horarios. A one-period day looks exactly as it did,
   plus a small "+ Adicionar 2.o periodo" text button. Add it, set 08:00-13:00 and 14:00-19:00, Guardar.
   RE-OPEN and confirm both periods came back. Then open the agenda for that therapist on that weekday
   and confirm the 13:00-14:00 gap behaves as OUTSIDE working hours - that last step is the one that
   tests the no-migration recon rather than the screen.

=== QUEUED 2026-08-06, the W13-03 login screens (#828, 6596d15). WF-03 evidence, batched. ===

On the deployed portal, after PORTAL_TENANT_ID is set (W13-03c). Steps 1, 2 and 5 are checkable with OTP_LIVE_SEND still off; steps 3 and 4 need the code, so they belong to the supervised canary.
1. Open the portal. EXPECT: 'Entrar com o seu telemovel' and a single phone field. No email field, no password field, no 'Recuperar acesso' link.
2. Visit /auth/reset-password directly. EXPECT: the portal's not-found page. Same for /auth/activate.
3. Enter a number and submit. EXPECT: the code screen, the number shown above the field, and the notice 'Se o numero estiver registado, enviamos um codigo por SMS.'
4. On that screen, below the card. EXPECT: 'Nao recebeu o codigo?' and three lines - no mobile on record, a landline, a shared number - each ending in 'Contacte a clinica'.
5. Enter six wrong digits. EXPECT: one red banner, 'Nao foi possivel entrar...', and NOTHING naming which of the six failure modes occurred.
6. After a successful login, sign out from the account screen, then reopen the portal. EXPECT: the phone screen, NOT an automatic entry - sign-out drops the trusted device as well as the session.

=== THE ACCEPTANCE SESSION PLAN IS WRITTEN, 2026-08-07. docs/acceptance-session-wave-13.md ===

One sitting, 23 numbered items, each a URL and an expected screen. It covers every
accumulated WF-03 item plus the work that landed after the queue was last touched:
the portal login screens, the reception confirm surface INCLUDING the 0059
free-then-refuse pair, the terms flow, split-shift, the populated notification
centre, the staff invite, the Gmail-aged recovery link, and the OTP_LIVE_SEND
supervised canary with its arming AND disarming steps.

THREE THINGS IN IT THAT ARE NOT OBVIOUS AND ARE THE REASON IT IS A DOCUMENT
RATHER THAN A LIST:
  The Gmail recovery link is TRIGGERED AT STEP 0c and read at step 7, so the
  15-minute scanner wait runs in the background instead of stalling the session.
  The wait IS the test; five previous rounds failed for want of it.
  Item 6 is the single most important behavioural check: book a staff appointment
  OVER a pedido (must save), then confirm the pedido (must refuse). Both halves
  have to be true or JP's option B is half-applied.
  Disarming is step 23 and explicitly permits "left armed" as an outcome, as long
  as WHICH ONE is recorded. Not deciding is the failure mode, not either choice.

IT ALSO STATES WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE: PG6, PG8 and PG9 are unbuilt loops that no
screen check can close, and the fee-line copy needs JP and counsel rather than a
screen. And it carries WF-16's sentence about an open gate awaiting the batch
being healthy state, because that is the one most likely to be misread later.

THE PLAN IS THE WAVE'S STOP CONDITION. When every item has an answer, the wave is
complete.

cards.title: Launch-day sequence: arm the live sends under supervision, in order, with a canary first send
cards.notes:
CREATED 2026-08-05 by WF-12 (R9), which requires a launch-day sequence card and puts the arming of both live-send flags on it. This card is the sequence. It executes on launch day, not before, and every step is owner-terminal: env changes are cloud writes and PURPLE performs none of them.

PRECONDITION FOR THE WHOLE SEQUENCE, per WF-10 (R7): a patient can use every planned portal feature start to end. Not a gate count, a behavioural condition on the deployed app.

SEQUENCE:

1. REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND stays FALSE through all acceptance testing. It is armed here and nowhere earlier. Env var NAME only; PURPLE never sees or sets the value.
2. FIRST SEND IS SUPERVISED AND CANARY-STYLE: one known recipient, watched, before any volume follows.

4. INVITES_LIVE_SEND is armed in the same session, not earlier (LE-invites-live-send, answered HOLD by WF-12). Note it governs a NON-Inngest path - lib/admin/staff.ts -> lib/invites/email.ts -> sendEmail in lib/reminders/clients.ts - which before #778 degraded silently with no boot signal. It now fails loudly at boot, so a misconfiguration surfaces immediately rather than as invites that appear to work and send nothing.

The packet was wrong and is now corrected. The test is unchanged and still load-bearing.

evidence.ref: deferred-by-decision under WF-16 point 3; PG3 already passed 2026-08-05 on the deployed route check, and LOOP 1 DB-gated suite proves the redemption properties

cards.notes:
NOT GATING. PG3 passed on 2026-08-05 on the deployed route check (https://app.osteojp.pt/r/anything returning the generic pt-PT rejection). This card tracks the one thing that check could not cover: a REAL signed token redeemed end to end on the deployed app.

WHY IT IS OWNER-RUN: generating a valid token needs REMINDERS_LINK_SECRET. That value never enters this terminal - env var NAMES only, standing rule 3. PURPLE cannot produce this evidence and must not try.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN WITHOUT IT, so this is confirmatory depth and not a hole: LOOP 1's DB-gated suite proves a second redemption is refused with a byte-identical body to a forged token; that the action and the consumption record commit or roll back together, forced by colliding the token hash inside the action's transaction; that a 48h cancel token redeemed inside the cutoff is refused with the pt-PT telephone copy AND not consumed; that a 24h SMS token cannot cancel even when the request asks; and that the landing payload carries no service name for a treatment-identifying service. The route is deployed-proven and the rule is unit-proven. What is unobserved is the two together on a live token.

QUEUED in VERIFY-QUEUE as item 1 under WF-09's batching rule. Expected screen is recorded there.

UNBLOCKED FROM PURPLE 2026-08-05: apps/web/scripts/sign-reminder-token.mjs is committed. It is self-contained (node:crypto only, no build step, no database, no network) and guarded - link-token.script-parity.test.ts asserts a token built the script's way VERIFIES with the real verifyRescheduleToken, so the duplicated wire format cannot drift silently into signing something the server no longer accepts. Expiry is 30 minutes rather than the server's tie-to-appointment-start, because the script cannot know the start without a database read; short enough that a token in shell history is not a standing credential.

--- DEFERRED BY DECISION 2026-08-05 (WF-16 point 3), owner ruling ---

NOT PENDING. Someone decided this, and the difference matters: a pending item looks like owed work forever, a deferred one has a reason attached.

WHY: the signing secret is NOT in the owner's env file - it lives only in Vercel on osteojp-platform - so exercising this would mean copying a live signing key onto a laptop for a confirmatory check that moves no gate. Against that, PG3 already passed on the deployed route check, and all five properties this would observe are unit-proven by tests that fail on regression: single use, byte-identical rejection for consumed vs forged, transactional consumption, cutoff re-checked at redemption, and no service name on the landing page. The parity test additionally pins the signing script's wire format to the real verifier, so the script cannot drift into signing something the server rejects.

EXERCISED NATURALLY by the first real reminder after launch, when a genuine token reaches a genuine patient. That is a better test than a synthetic one anyway.

LEFT VERIFY-QUEUE. It is not owed work and must not be listed as such at the acceptance session.

CLOSED 2026-08-06 AS DEFERRED-BY-DECISION, per WF-16 point 3: a non-gating confirmatory check whose properties are already unit-proven is DEFERRED, not queued. Deferred means someone decided; pending means someone forgot. It stops appearing as owed work and PURPLE stops listing it.

cards.title: Owner ruling: GREEN is retired - custody of the platform board transfers to PURPLE, closure-only
cards.notes:

"GREEN is retired, platform work complete. Custody of prelaunch-board.json transfers to PURPLE for closure-only edits. No other edits to prelaunch-board.json are licensed."

This ruling resolves it properly, by transferring custody rather than by asking anyone to ignore a standing rule.

cards.title: Owner ruling: legal and regulatory work leaves engineering - external counsel owns it
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05:

"An external lawyer and a cybersecurity representative now own all legal and regulatory connections, policies and filings. Engineering scope is code and platform function only."

WHAT IT CHANGES. Legal and regulatory ERRANDS leave the engineering board: obtaining a DPA, checking a public register, delivering a document to counsel. They are reassigned rather than deleted, so the work is visible and owned, and they stop counting against Ivan's queue.

WHAT IT EXPLICITLY DOES NOT CHANGE, quoted from the ruling's own item 4: 'Compliance properties implemented in code (audit log per patient write, identifiers-only Inngest payloads, fail-closed token handling, notes never patient-facing) are PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS and remain in force. This ruling removes legal errands, not engineering guarantees.'

That distinction is the whole ruling and it is worth restating in engineering terms: counsel no longer tells us WHETHER to keep these properties, because they are now product requirements we hold regardless. The enforcement points stay exactly where they are and every one of them is a test that fails on regression - patient_audit_log's append-only trigger and grants (0054), payload-minimization.test.ts, the identical-rejection and transactional-consumption proofs in redeem.db.test.ts, and the notes-privacy tests in apps/api/lib/appointments/. None of them is relaxed by this ruling and a future session must not read 'legal work left engineering' as licence to touch one.

R3 MUTATES, per the ruling's item 5: a new vendor no longer trips a lawyer-annex question INSIDE engineering, but any new vendor is still CARDED to external counsel for review. The no-new-vendor default for OTP storage stands unchanged - see WF-06, where the durable store was ruled onto the existing Postgres, and note that its engineering justification survives the legal one: a table we already operate beats a vendor we would have to operate.

MECHANICS ON THIS BOARD. The people set is pinned by the validator to the blocked_on_people lane's own columns, which are ivan | jp | lawyer. There is no 'external-counsel' value and inventing one fails validation - but 'lawyer' already MEANS external counsel here, as PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md section 6 states ('Rodica is not a portal stakeholder; counsel is, which is why the third column is the lawyer'). So reassignment uses the lawyer column and the lane note now records that it covers the external lawyer AND the cybersecurity representative. Same intent, valid board, no new enum.

PG8 WAS NOT TOUCHED. The ruling's item 3 said to reassign 'PG8 (lawyer RGPD sign-off) if present in the gate array'. It is not present: PG8 on this board is SYNC - 3C proven, portal booking removes the slot from the staff agenda and vice versa - and no RGPD sign-off gate exists anywhere in the array. Recorded rather than resolved by editing the nearest gate.

cards.title: LIVE: the deployed portal offers magic-link login, which Decision D forbids - and the SMTP fix just made it work

evidence.ref:
#808 MERGED 2026-08-05, squashed to a5d8dd0 on origin/main. BOTH HALVES removed: the surface that OFFERED a sign-in link (signInWithOtp, login/page.tsx:68) and the code that HONOURED one (the #access_token fragment handler calling setSession, :15-37). Removing the button alone would have left a link already in an inbox, or one issued from the Supabase dashboard, still minting a session. Five guard tests split across the two halves. Gates: lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, test 8/8 tasks (portal 40 up from 35). NOT CLOSED as patient-visible - WF-03 governs and the login screen is in VERIFY-QUEUE.

CLOSED 2026-08-05 on the owner's DEPLOYED screen per WF-03 (portal.osteojp.pt): email field, password field, a single Entrar button, and NO magic-link option anywhere. Recovery and activation links present as 'Recuperar acesso' and 'Ativar conta' - labels differ from the wording the queue item predicted, functionally the same links, NOT a defect and explicitly ruled so by the owner. He then completed a normal password sign-in as a patient identity and the dashboard rendered: greeting, empty consultas state, Marcar consulta CTA.

THE SECOND HALF IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED. Removing the magic link left password login as the ONLY way into the portal until OTP ships, so a successful sign-in was the real check - the absence of a toggle proves nothing if nobody can get in.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-05 while running the template-dependency check the owner asked for. It is not a template issue; it is an auth-model one, and it is LIVE.

WHAT EXISTS. apps/portal/app/auth/login/page.tsx:63-81 defines handleMagicLink, which calls supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, emailRedirectTo: '/auth/callback' }). It is not dead code: the form's onSubmit switches to it at :110 and the mode toggle is rendered to the patient at :167. Any patient on the deployed login page can request a sign-in link by EMAIL.

WHY IT IS FORBIDDEN. Decision D (WAVE-13.md section 1.4), verbatim: 'patient login is a 6-digit SMS OTP, phone only, with a trusted device of 30 days. NO PASSWORD, NO MAGIC LINK, no session minted from any other artefact.' A magic link mints a session on click. This is the same class of thing WF-08 deleted sendPatientActivation for - and that one was DEAD code, while this one is wired to a button.

THE SMTP FIX IS WHAT MADE IT REAL, and this is the part worth understanding rather than alarming about. Until 2026-08-05 every Supabase auth email failed silently on the gmail.com sender, so the magic-link button produced nothing and the violation was inert. Correctly fixing the sender - which staff password recovery genuinely needed - ALSO switched this on. The owner's own verification email ('Your sign-in link') IS this path working. He did not click it.

SEVERITY, stated honestly rather than inflated. This is NOT unauthorised access: an attacker needs control of the patient's mailbox. It is a ruled-against auth model running in production - patient authentication is email-based today, when the clinic ruled it must be phone-based - and it widens the credential surface Decision D deliberately narrowed to one channel.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: remove the magic-link mode from the portal login page NOW, as a small isolated change, rather than waiting for LOOP 3 to replace the whole auth surface. LOOP 3 removes it as a side effect of building OTP, but LOOP 3 is days away and this is live today. The password path at :52 is also Decision-D-forbidden and is the known committed state the board already records; it is NOT newly enabled by anything and should go with the same LOOP 3 replacement.

PATIENT-VISIBLE, so WF-03 applies to whatever ships.

--- REMOVED 2026-08-05, #808 ---

RECON, all three apps, offers AND honours:
  OFFERS  portal login signInWithOtp -> REMOVED; portal reset-password resetPasswordForEmail -> kept.
  HONOURS portal login #access_token -> setSession -> REMOVED; /auth/callback ?code= -> exchangeCodeForSession -> kept.
  STAFF APPS: NONE. apps/web and apps/admin call signInWithPassword only, and the staff login page documents it at page.tsx:141 - 'The staff app exposes no magic-link or password-reset entry.'

PREMISE CORRECTED. The dispatch said the sign-in email came from the app.osteojp.pt RECOVERY flow. It cannot have: the staff app has no recovery entry point, and 'Your sign-in link' is Supabase's MAGIC LINK template rather than its recovery template. The conclusion the dispatch wanted still holds and is now proven instead of assumed - STAFF RECOVERY USES NO SIGN-IN-LINK TEMPLATE, because staff recovery does not exist in the product at all; it is done from the Supabase dashboard. No dashboard setting change was needed, so no click-by-click steps are owed.

THE PORTAL IS NOT LEFT WITHOUT A LOGIN, so the pre-accepted cost did not materialise. The page had two modes and only the magic one went; PASSWORD LOGIN STILL WORKS and is the single way in until LOOP 3 ships OTP. A test asserts signInWithPassword is still present, precisely so a later cleanup cannot remove it and lock every patient out.

STILL DECISION-D-FORBIDDEN AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: password login itself, and the reset-password + activate flows. All three are the existing committed auth the board already records, none is newly enabled, and LOOP 3 replaces the whole surface. Removing them now would strand patients with no replacement built.

QUEUE ITEM CLOSED 2026-08-05. Both halves verified on the deployed portal: the link-login option is gone AND a patient can still sign in. Label variance on the two remaining links was ruled not-a-defect by the owner.

cards.title: Supabase auth emails send Supabase's default ENGLISH body to a pt-PT product

evidence.ref: CLOSED 2026-08-07. All six templates re-pasted by Ivan from e97dcdd and verified by a live recovery email showing the CORRECTED footer. Re-derived rather than accepted: git diff --stat e97dcdd 0987ee7 -- supabase/templates/ is EMPTY, so no template file changed between the commit he pasted from and merged main - his paste IS current. The token_hash template rewrite belongs to the unbuilt recovery-fix branch and is tracked on LE-auth-recovery-deadend, not here. Guard: apps/web/lib/auth/supabase-email-templates.test.ts 52/52.

cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-05 from the owner's downstream check. It was NOT already covered - a board search for supabase/template/auth-mail cards returned only LE-supabase-auth-smtp and an unrelated scripts card.

THE OBSERVATION, from Ivan's live verification: the email that arrived carried Supabase's stock English body - subject 'Your sign-in link', text 'Follow the link below to sign in'. Everything else patient-facing in this product is pt-PT and routes through packages/i18n; these emails do not, because they are rendered by Supabase from dashboard-side templates the repo never sees.

WHO ACTUALLY RECEIVES THEM, re-derived rather than assumed:
  PATIENTS, today: apps/portal/app/auth/login/page.tsx:68 (signInWithOtp magic link) and apps/portal/app/auth/reset-password/page.tsx:26 (resetPasswordForEmail).
  STAFF: apps/web and apps/admin log in with signInWithPassword, which sends no mail. No resetPasswordForEmail call exists in either app, so staff recovery today runs from the Supabase dashboard rather than from a product screen.

SCOPE SHRINKS SHARPLY WHEN LOOP 3 LANDS, which is why this is medium and not high. Decision D replaces patient auth with SMS OTP through our OWN transport, whose body is already pt-PT and already in the repo (apps/api/lib/auth/otp-transport.ts otpMessageBody). Both patient callers above disappear with that work - see SEC-portal-magic-link. What SURVIVES is staff-side auth mail, which is internal and where English is far less of a defect.

SO THE REAL DECISION IS SEQUENCING, not translation: customise the Supabase templates now and much of that work is thrown away by LOOP 3, or wait and translate only what remains. RECOMMENDED: wait for LOOP 3, then translate the residual staff templates.

NO TEMPLATES WERE MODIFIED in this session, per the owner's instruction. Note for whoever does: Supabase auth templates live in the dashboard, not the repo, so this is an owner-terminal edit and cannot be reviewed in a PR. Patient-visible, so WF-03 applies to anything patient-facing.

=== BODIES AUTHORED 2026-08-06. THE SEQUENCING QUESTION IS RESOLVED, AND ONE PREMISE ON THIS CARD WAS WRONG. ===

THE RECOMMENDATION ON THIS CARD WAS TO WAIT FOR LOOP 3. LOOP 3 LANDED (#828), so the wait is over and the residual set is now known rather than predicted.

PREMISE CORRECTION, re-derived by grep on main rather than trusted from this card. This card said the patient callers would disappear and staff-side auth mail would SURVIVE. The first half is right: signInWithOtp and resetPasswordForEmail both have ZERO callers now. The second half is wrong. NO code path in this repo causes Supabase to send an email at all:
  signInWithPassword sends nothing.
  admin.createUser (provision.ts:72,157) and admin.updateUserById (:195) both pass email_confirm: true, so no confirmation round-trip is sent.
  admin.generateLink({type:recovery}) (:223) RETURNS a link and sends nothing - staff.ts:213 mails it through Resend with our own pt-PT body.
  auth.updateUser is metadata or an authenticated password change; neither mails.

SO WHY DO IT AT ALL, and this is what keeps the card open rather than closing it as moot. TWO live exposures remain: (1) staff password recovery today runs from the SUPABASE DASHBOARD, not a product screen - this card already said so - and a reset triggered there renders the English body to a real staff member; (2) the moment anyone re-enables resetPasswordForEmail, English goes out with no gate and no warning. Correct bodies make both a non-event.

WHAT LANDS: six templates in supabase/templates/, the full GoTrue set, because translating five of six leaves a gap nobody notices until it fires. Five interpolate ConfirmationURL; reauthentication interpolates Token instead, because it is a code and a URL there renders EMPTY. Accented characters are HTML entities on purpose - the dashboard editor and older mail clients have too many ways to mangle a raw UTF-8 byte.

GUARD: apps/web/lib/auth/supabase-email-templates.test.ts, 34/34 green. It asserts the full six-file set, the right variable per file, lang=pt-PT, no Supabase stock English, brand teal, the clinic footer, no emoji, both addresses named in the change-email body, and a decoded pt-PT "se nao" reassurance line in every template. It decodes the entities before asserting on prose, so it tests the words and not the encoding.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, stated rather than glossed: nothing in this repo can read the dashboard, so the guard keeps the COMMITTED copy honest and cannot keep the DASHBOARD honest. supabase/config.toml is deliberately NOT wired to these files - that block configures the local stack only, where mail goes to Mailpit and nobody reads it, so wiring it would add an unverifiable change for no production benefit.

BLOCKED ON IVAN: six paste operations in Authentication > Emails > Templates, the sender check (no-reply@send.osteojp.pt on the VERIFIED send.osteojp.pt identity, not the root domain), and one recovery email to himself as the acceptance check. Full steps: docs/supabase-auth-email-templates.md section 3.

=== APPLIED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-06, AND THE VERIFICATION EARNED ITS KEEP. ===

All six pasted, sender verified, pt-PT body confirmed in a real inbox. The card stays IN FLIGHT rather than shipped because the same email surfaced two defects that a screenshot of a subject line would have missed:
  1. The footer rendered the literal text "OsteoJP &middot" and stopped. Fixed at source in this branch - the separator is now plain ASCII. ALL SIX files changed, because the footer is identical in all six, so all six need ONE re-paste.
  2. The dashboard-triggered recovery dead-ends. Carded separately as LE-auth-recovery-deadend.

THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: the committed source was byte-correct and the guard test was green. Neither could see a defect that only exists after a dashboard paste and a mail client. The one thing that found it was a person opening a real email. That is what WF-03 is for, and this is the first time it has paid out on something a test could not have caught.

=== CLOSED 2026-08-07. ===

Six templates applied, footer defect fixed and re-pasted, sender verified, live recovery email confirms the corrected footer. The git diff between the commit Ivan pasted from and merged main is empty for supabase/templates/, so nothing has drifted since.

DO NOT RE-LIST. The remaining auth work is the RECOVERY LINK mechanism, which is LE-auth-recovery-deadend and will change these templates again (ConfirmationURL to TokenHash). That is a different card and a different re-paste, when it ships.

cards.title: Dashboard-triggered staff recovery dead-ends on the login page - the only live recovery path is unusable

evidence.ref: #837 MERGED 2026-08-07, squashed to a3937bb. The link changed SHAPE: it no longer goes to Supabase /auth/v1/verify, it carries token_hash as an inert query param to our own page, and verifyOtp runs only from the explicit submit. Both templates moved off {{ .ConfirmationURL }}; provision.ts builds its URL from hashed_token. 39 tests including source-level assertions that the GET stays inert. STATUS STAYS in_flight: this closes on ONE real Gmail-aged link reaching the set-password screen and setting a password, and Ivan must re-paste two templates first (docs/supabase-auth-redirect-urls.md section 9).

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-06 by Ivan verifying the redirect fix. Reproduced TWICE on fresh tokens.

SYMPTOM: a recovery sent from the Supabase dashboard lands on app.osteojp.pt root carrying the recovery hash. The login page renders. No set-password screen is ever offered, and the link cannot be reused.

MECHANISM, FROM THE CODE, AND THE OBVIOUS DESCRIPTION OF IT IS WRONG. The token is NOT consumed by our app. Supabase /auth/v1/verify consumes the single-use token SERVER-SIDE before redirecting, and hands the session material to the browser in the URL FRAGMENT. A fragment is never transmitted to a server. So:
  apps/web/app/page.tsx is a SERVER component - getRequestContext() finds no cookie and redirects to /login. The fragment survives the redirect (RFC 7231) but the server never saw it.
  apps/web/app/login/page.tsx is "use client" but creates NO Supabase browser client; it posts to a server action. Nothing reads the fragment.
  The fragment is dropped on the next navigation. The link is already spent, so a retry returns otp_expired - which is why two fresh tokens were needed to reproduce it twice.

WHY THE ENV VAR DID NOT PREVENT IT: STAFF_INVITE_REDIRECT_URL is read ONLY at provision.ts:222, which serves the IN-PRODUCT staff invite path. A DASHBOARD-triggered recovery passes no redirect_to of its own and falls back to the Site URL. Two different triggers, two different mechanisms, and the doc conflated them - corrected in docs/supabase-auth-redirect-urls.md section 3.

apps/web/app/auth/update-password/UpdatePasswordClient.tsx is the ONE route that handles this correctly, and its header documents the exact fragment shape it expects. The flow never reaches it.

IMMEDIATE STOPGAP, DASHBOARD ONLY, ZERO CODE, AND WORTH DOING NOW because this is the only live recovery path and it is dead: set Site URL to https://app.osteojp.pt/auth/update-password. NO allowlist change needed - that exact URL is already listed. Full instruction in docs/supabase-auth-redirect-urls.md section 7.

WHY THAT IS A STOPGAP AND NOT THE FIX: the Site URL is the fallback for EVERY flow that passes no redirect_to. Today that is only staff recovery, so pointing it at the set-password screen is correct. The moment a second such flow exists - an email-change confirmation, say - it would land on a set-password screen and be wrong.

THE DURABLE FIX, on its own branch AFTER #830 merges, never onto #830: mount a hash guard in apps/web/app/login/page.tsx, which is already "use client". On mount, if location.hash carries type=recovery or error_code=, router.replace("/auth/update-password" + location.hash). Small, contained, and it makes ANY future misrouting self-correcting rather than depending on one dashboard field staying set. Once it ships the Site URL can return to the root, or stay as-is harmlessly.

DO NOT attempt to read the fragment server-side. It is never transmitted. That mistake would produce code that looks right and never fires.

CLOSES ON: one recovery email that reaches the set-password screen and successfully sets a password. WF-16 - accumulates, no return to Ivan until the fix ships and that one email proves the full chain.

=== STOPGAP APPLIED, ROUTING FIXED, LINK STILL FAILS. FIFTH FAILURE. 2026-08-06. ===

Site URL is now https://app.osteojp.pt/auth/update-password, allowlist has exactly that one entry, the patient wildcard is deleted. The link LANDS correctly now - the routing half is closed. The page then renders "Ligacao invalida".

*** THE REPORTED CAUSE IS PLAUSIBLE BUT THE OBSERVED ERROR STRING ARGUES AGAINST IT BEING THE WHOLE STORY. HALTING ON THAT BEFORE THE FIX IS BUILT. ***

THE DISCRIMINATOR, from the page source. UpdatePasswordClient.tsx:124-128 maps outcomes to exactly two failures:
  error_code === "otp_expired"  ->  reason "expired"  ->  "Ligacao expirada ou ja utilizada"
  anything else, INCLUDING NO FRAGMENT AT ALL  ->  reason "invalid"  ->  "Ligacao invalida"
A CONSUMED TOKEN IS otp_expired. If a scanner had spent it, Supabase would redirect with error_code=otp_expired and the page would say EXPIRED. Ivan sees INVALID. So on the evidence in hand, prefetch is not what produced this particular screen.

WHAT DOES PRODUCE IT, and it is a second independent defect that needs no scanner: THE PAGE READS ONLY THE URL FRAGMENT, AND THE CLIENT IS ON PKCE. parseHashParams() at :63-66 reads window.location.hash and nothing else. @supabase/ssr 0.10.3 HARDCODES flowType: "pkce" (createBrowserClient.js:40). Under PKCE the verify redirect returns ?code= in the QUERY STRING, and errors arrive as query params too. hadHash is therefore false, and :126-128 settles "invalid" - the exact screen observed. This would fail on a pristine, never-prefetched link.

ONE DATUM SETTLES IT, and it costs one copy-paste: THE FULL LANDING URL, query string and fragment included, from the address bar after clicking. ?code=... means the PKCE mismatch. #error_code=otp_expired means prefetch. Both means both. Nothing else is needed.

THE PREFETCH EXPOSURE IS REAL REGARDLESS, and Supabase documents it: the auth-email-templates guide warns that providers prefetch links and consume the token, producing "Token has expired or is invalid". So it is fixed either way - but if only prefetch were fixed and the page kept reading the hash, the link would STILL fail, and that is the sixth failure this triage exists to prevent.

=== THE FIX, DERIVED FROM SUPABASE DOCS AND FROM THIS REPO, NOT GUESSED ===

Supabase recommended pattern, verbatim from the guide: link to your own endpoint as ?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=...&redirect_to={{ .RedirectTo }}, then call supabase.auth.verifyOtp({ token_hash, type }).

ONE DEVIATION FROM THEIR EXAMPLE, DELIBERATE AND STRICTER. Their sample verifies ON THE GET and redirects. That is still prefetch-vulnerable - a scanner following to our domain would spend the token there instead. The requirement is that the GET a scanner makes must be INERT. So: the emailed link carries token_hash and type as inert query params to our page, the page renders and verifies NOTHING, and verifyOtp runs only from an explicit user action.

*** THIS SHAPE IS ALREADY PROVEN IN THIS REPO. DO NOT INVENT IT. *** apps/web/app/r/[token]/page.tsx is exactly this: the GET renders a confirmation screen and, in its own words at :217, "Still performs nothing"; redemption happens through a form POST to redeemAction. The reminder lane solved prefetch-safety already; the auth lane never adopted it. Copy that structure.

TEMPLATE CHANGE THAT RIDES WITH IT: supabase/templates/reset-password.html and invite.html currently use {{ .ConfirmationURL }}, which IS the /auth/v1/verify GET that spends the token. They move to the token_hash form. Both need a re-paste when it ships.

COPY DEFECT, confirmed and small: auth.setPassword.invalidBody says "Abra o link mais recente do email de CONVITE" and is shown for a RECOVERY too. The page was built for the invite flow and recovery was bolted onto it, which is itself evidence recovery was never exercised end to end through this screen.

=== THE SAME EXPOSURE ACROSS EVERY OTHER EMAILED ONE-TIME LINK, AUDITED ===
  STAFF INVITE set-password link: SAME EXPOSURE, SAME TWO DEFECTS. provision.ts generateLink returns an /auth/v1/verify action_link which staff.ts emails through Resend, and it lands on this same hash-reading page. It is not a separate fix, it is the same one.
  REMINDER /r/<token> links: ALREADY SAFE. GET renders, POST redeems, and the generic rejection at :128-129 is identical for malformed, forged, expired, unknown and already-consumed so a scanner learns nothing either. No change needed, and it is the model for the fix.
  PATIENT OTP: not a link. SMS six-digit code through our own transport. No prefetch surface.

VERIFICATION PATH, as instructed: a real Gmail inbox, because the scanner is the thing under test and no local harness reproduces it. CLOSES ON one recovery email that reaches the set-password screen and successfully sets a password, from a link that was sitting in Gmail long enough to be scanned.

BRANCH: its own, after #830 merges. Not onto #830.

=== THE BARE URL IS EXPLAINED, AND IT ENDS THE DIAGNOSTIC LINE. 2026-08-06. ===

ANSWER: BOTH OF OUR OWN COMPONENTS STRIP THE EVIDENCE, INDEPENDENTLY, BEFORE A HUMAN CAN READ THE ADDRESS BAR. The bare URL is therefore consistent with EVERY hypothesis and discriminates NONE of them.

  THE FRAGMENT is erased by OUR OWN CODE. UpdatePasswordClient.tsx scrubHash() at :75-79 runs window.history.replaceState(null, "", pathname + search) and it is called from settle() at :101 - on EVERY outcome, including the error path. So a #access_token or #error_code fragment is gone from the address bar the instant the invalida screen renders.
  THE QUERY is erased by SUPABASE-JS. auth-js GoTrueClient.js:3062-3063 does url.searchParams.delete("code") then window.history.replaceState. A ?code= is removed by the library itself as part of detectSessionInUrl, which is on by default (:22).

  THE MIDDLEWARE IS RULED OUT, checked rather than assumed: apps/web/proxy.ts calls updateSession and returns NextResponse.next(); lib/supabase/middleware.ts only calls supabase.auth.getUser() to refresh cookies. Neither redirects, neither rewrites, neither touches query or fragment. No hop drops anything.

SO CHROME HISTORY SHOWING A BARE PATH PROVES NOTHING EITHER WAY, exactly as the relay suspected of fragments - and now also of the query, because the library removed it client-side after the page had already loaded, which no history entry would capture.

*** DIAGNOSIS STOPS HERE, ON PURPOSE. FURTHER URL FORENSICS HAS NO DECISION VALUE. *** Three hypotheses remain live - PKCE ?code= with no code_verifier (an emailed link opened in a browser that never started the flow CANNOT have one, and incognito guarantees it), a race between the client constructor detecting the URL and the effect body reading the hash, and scanner prefetch. THE DURABLE FIX IS INVARIANT ACROSS ALL THREE:
  token_hash arrives as OUR OWN query param, which auth-js does not touch (it deletes "code", not "token_hash").
  No fragment is involved, so scrubHash is irrelevant.
  verifyOtp needs no code_verifier, so the PKCE mismatch cannot arise.
  The GET is inert, so prefetch cannot consume anything.
Spending another cycle deciding WHICH of the three it is would change nothing about what gets built. Build it.

ONE EXTRA DEFECT FOUND WHILE ANSWERING THIS, and it is why five attempts produced no diagnosis: THE PAGE DESTROYS ITS OWN DIAGNOSTICS. scrubHash() runs on the ERROR path too, so the one screen a human is looking at is the screen that has just erased what caused it. The fix should capture the arriving params into the error state BEFORE scrubbing, and surface them - even as a copyable detail line behind a disclosure. A failure screen that cannot tell you what failed cost this project five verification rounds.

=== BUILT 2026-08-07, branch portal/LE-auth-recovery-token-hash, PR #837. ===

BUILT WITHOUT DECIDING WHICH OF THE THREE HYPOTHESES IT WAS, exactly as this card
ruled. The fix is invariant across prefetch, PKCE and the race, and spending
another cycle discriminating them would have changed nothing about what got
built.

WHAT SHIPPED:
  link-params.ts, a PURE module. The parsing that five verification rounds could
  not pin down is now unit-testable without a browser. It reads BOTH shapes, and
  it reads errors from the QUERY as well as the fragment - which the old page did
  not, and which is the second independent defect this card identified.
  UpdatePasswordClient.tsx rewritten. The token_hash path resolves in a PURE
  DERIVATION during render, not in an effect: no network call, no session lookup,
  no token spent, and no async step to lose a race in.
  Both email templates off {{ .ConfirmationURL }}.
  provision.ts builds its own URL from properties.hashed_token instead of
  returning properties.action_link, so the IN-PRODUCT staff invite is fixed by
  the same change - this card's audit said it was the same defect, and it was.

TWO DESIGN DECISIONS THAT ARE NOT IN THE CARD AND ARE WORTH RECORDING.

  THE LANDING URL IS HARDCODED IN THE TEMPLATES, not {{ .RedirectTo }}. That
  variable is populated only when the caller passed a redirect_to, and a
  DASHBOARD-triggered recovery passes none - it would render EMPTY and break the
  link. That is the same one-variable-two-trigger-paths conflation this card
  already identified as the root cause of the STAFF_INVITE_REDIRECT_URL
  confusion. Hardcoding removes the variable rather than trusting it. Documented
  in the template header and in docs/supabase-auth-redirect-urls.md section 9.

  STAFF_INVITE_REDIRECT_URL BECAME REQUIRED. Before, unset meant Supabase fell
  back to the Site URL and the link still worked; now we build the URL ourselves
  so there is no fallback to be had. It fails LOUDLY (console.error naming the
  variable, value never logged) and the invite falls back to its existing
  temporary-password hand-off, which is a visible working outcome. PG7.

THE ERROR SCREEN NOW SAYS WHAT FAILED, which is this card's own last finding. The
old page scrubbed on every outcome including the error path, so the screen a
human was looking at had just erased the evidence. Params are captured during
RENDER via useSyncExternalStore - strictly earlier than any effect - and surfaced
behind a "Detalhes tecnicos" disclosure, with token_hash, access_token,
refresh_token and code redacted to a character count. Presence is diagnostic;
value is not, and the screen may be pasted into a support thread.

THE COPY DEFECT IS FIXED: invalidBody said "email de CONVITE" and was shown for a
recovery too. Both bodies now name neither flow specifically.

A LINT ERROR CAUGHT A REAL DESIGN PROBLEM, worth recording because the first
implementation was wrong in a way that would have passed review. Setting state
synchronously in the mount effect trips the cascading-renders rule, and the rule
is right. Restructuring to a pure derivation (phaseFromUrl) removed the state to
set AND removed the last async step on the new path - a better design arrived at
by taking the linter seriously rather than suppressing it.

STILL OPEN, and it is the whole point of the card: ONE REAL GMAIL-AGED LINK.
The scanner is the thing under test and no local harness reproduces it. Ivan
re-pastes the two templates (docs/supabase-auth-redirect-urls.md section 9 lists
exactly which, and says the other four are untouched), triggers a recovery to a
real Gmail address, LEAVES IT A FEW MINUTES so the provider scans it, then opens
it. Clicking immediately proves nothing.

cards.title: Split-shift availability: two working periods per therapist-day instead of one continuous block

evidence.ref: #818 (6c906f4) - split-shift availability; e2e "a SPLIT SHIFT saves, survives a reload, and can be removed" green in shard 3 (6.8s)

cards.notes:
OWNER-APPROVED 2026-08-05. Origin: clinic admin request relayed by Ivan. No JP trip - scheduling UX, not clinical, fiscal or legal. Committed per WF-01 BEFORE any execution.

GOAL: admin sets a morning period (e.g. 08:00-13:00) and an afternoon period (e.g. 14:00-19:00) per therapist-day, so the gap between them is outside working hours and unbookable.

=== RECON VERDICT: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. NO MIGRATION. DOES NOT QUEUE BEHIND LOOP 3. ===

The data model already supports this and so does the slot engine. Re-derived from committed code, not assumed:

1. availability_templates is ALREADY a row-per-period table: (tenant, user, location, weekday, start_time, end_time) plus an optional validity window (packages/db/src/schema.ts:770-813). A split shift is simply TWO ROWS for the same weekday.

2. The unique constraint does NOT prevent that. availability_templates_dedupe_uq covers the FULL tuple INCLUDING start_time and end_time (0006_availability_timeoff.sql:14), so it blocks exact duplicate rows only. Two rows sharing (tenant, user, location, weekday) with different times are legal today. This was the load-bearing question and the answer is the reason no migration is needed.

3. The slot engine already computes over MULTIPLE windows per day. apps/web/lib/scheduling/day-availability-core.ts:82-83 does templates.filter(t => t.weekday === weekday && isWithinValidity(...)) into `working: TimeInterval[]` - the type's own comment reads 'Working windows from availability_templates (merged, sorted)'. Plural, by construction.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REQUIREMENT 5, which asked for no new semantics and no lunch concept: there is nothing to build. The between-periods gap is outside working hours automatically, because anything not inside a `working` interval already is. No code or copy anywhere needs the word lunch, and none will be added.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REQUIREMENT 2, backwards compatibility: satisfied for free and with zero risk. Every existing schedule is already one row = period 1 with no period 2. Nothing is migrated, nothing is rewritten, and a therapist keeping one continuous block is byte-identical before and after.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REQUIREMENT 6: the migration choreography does not apply, so this card does NOT wait for the LOOP 3 apply. The slug split-shift-availability is NOT reserved and no number is derived, per the standing rule that numbers are never pre-assigned - there is simply no migration to number.

SO THE REAL WORK IS THE ADMIN UI AND ITS VALIDATION, and only that:
  - Requirement 3: extend the Horarios editor in the Gerir dialog IN PLACE. Each day row gains an optional second period behind a small add affordance, removable once added. No new page, no new dialog. Space-efficient: the day list must NOT double in height for one-period therapists, so the second period is absent rather than empty-and-hidden.
  - Requirement 4: period 2 starts at or after period 1 ends, same day, no overlap. This is form-level integrity and MAY hard-block saving the SCHEDULE form. It does not touch the standing rule that availability warnings never block APPOINTMENT saves, which stays in force.
  - Write the save path so two rows are created/updated/removed cleanly, and a removed period 2 deletes its row rather than leaving a zero-length one (the start_before_end CHECK would refuse that anyway, which is a useful backstop).

PRIORITY: medium, and it NEVER preempts LOOP 3. LOOP 3 is the launch-critical path (PG1); this fills halt gaps and post-loop slots, per the owner's own sequencing.

VISUAL GATE, requirement 7: staff-visible, so WF-03 applies and the owner's screen is the DoD. On green it enters VERIFY-QUEUE as: open a therapist Gerir dialog, set a two-period day, save, re-open to confirm persistence, and confirm the agenda reflects the gap.

RECON ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-05 WITH VERIFICATION TEETH. The apply count stays at two (booking-modes, terms-acceptance); this card authors no migration.

CONDITION ON THE VISUAL GATE: it must exercise the FULL claim end to end, not just the new UI. The VERIFY-QUEUE entry, when built, is: Ivan sets a two-period day, SAVES, RE-OPENS to confirm persistence, and then confirms ON THE AGENDA that the between-periods gap behaves as outside working hours. That last step is the one that tests the recon rather than the screen - the claim is that the storage and the slot engine already support this, and only the agenda can show whether they do.

HALT CONDITION: if ANY layer of the claimed existing support turns out to be absent during the build - the second row not persisting, or the slot engine collapsing two windows into one - HALT LOUD. Do not improvise a schema. The no-migration verdict was derived from three specific facts (row-per-period table, dedupe constraint covering the times, day-availability-core filtering into a plural TimeInterval[]), so if it is wrong, one of those three is wrong and the right response is to say which.

DEEP RECON 2026-08-05, BEFORE BUILDING. NO HALT: all three facts the no-migration verdict rested on still hold. But a FOURTH layer exists that the verdict did not enumerate, and it is where the actual work is - recorded precisely so the next session starts from truth rather than from my earlier summary.

CONFIRMED AGAIN:
  1. availability_templates is row-per-period.
  2. The dedupe unique constraint covers the full tuple INCLUDING times, so two rows per weekday are legal.
  3. day-availability-core.ts filters into a plural working: TimeInterval[].

THE FOURTH LAYER, apps/web/app/admin/staff/page.tsx:100-118. `buildDays` builds ScheduleDay[] through a Map called firstByKey, keyed userId:weekday, which KEEPS ONLY THE FIRST TEMPLATE PER WEEKDAY. Its own comment states the intent: 'tracks exactly one id per weekday, matching the W4-14 reconcile invariant.'

THAT IS NOT A DEFECT AND NOT THE HALT CONDITION. The halt condition was 'if any layer of the claimed EXISTING SUPPORT turns out absent'. Storage and the slot engine were the claim, and both hold. buildDays is UI plumbing deliberately written to a one-row-per-day invariant - it is the thing this card exists to change, not a discovery that invalidates the verdict. The migration count stays at two.

BUT IT DOES MEAN THE WORK IS FOUR FILES, NOT TWO, and a build that only touched the modal would silently drop period 2 on every reload - the row would save and then vanish, which is the worst failure shape available here. The full set:
  a. StaffManageModal.tsx: ScheduleDay gains p2On/p2Id/p2Start/p2End (optional). Render a second
     period behind a small add affordance, removable once added. Space-efficient: ABSENT rather
     than empty-and-hidden, so a one-period therapist's row does not grow.
  b. admin/staff/page.tsx buildDays: stop collapsing. Keep the FIRST two templates per weekday,
     ordered by start_time (the loader already orders by startTime, so first = morning).
  c. horarios/actions.ts saveScheduleAction: the reconcile loop runs for BOTH periods. Same
     enabled+id -> update / enabled+no id -> create / disabled+id -> archive rules, with the
     period-2 fields posted as d{wd}p2_*. Period 2 reuses period 1's location (the card scopes
     this per therapist-day-LOCATION).
  d. Validation: p2 start >= p1 end, same day, no overlap. Form-level, MAY hard-block the
     SCHEDULE form. Does NOT touch the standing rule that availability warnings never block
     APPOINTMENT saves.

WATCH FOR: the W4-14 reconcile invariant is named in at least three comments across those files. Changing it without updating those comments leaves the next reader trusting a rule that no longer holds - the exact class of defect the stale approval packet was.

NOT STARTED. Deliberately not begun at the end of a context window: a half-built version that saves a second period the loader then discards is worse than nothing, because it looks like it works once.

BUILT 2026-08-05 on portal/W13-A-split-shift, in the stated order: loader, reconcile, editor, validation. Gates green (lint 0 errors, typecheck 10/10, 189 web unit files).

THE FOURTH LAYER WAS REAL AND SO WAS A FIFTH THE DEEP RECON DID NOT NAME: buildDays existed TWICE, byte-identical, at app/admin/staff/page.tsx:100 AND app/horarios/page.tsx:60, feeding two editors (StaffManageModal, WeekScheduleEditor) that share one ScheduleDay type and two server actions holding two copies of the same reconcile loop. Teaching the admin path about period 2 and not the reception path would have meant reception saving a split shift and admin archiving it on the next Guardar. NOT A HALT: no claimed layer of existing support was absent - storage, the dedupe constraint and the plural TimeInterval[] all held exactly as recorded. It is duplication the card had not enumerated, so the loader, the reconcile and the day rows are now each ONE implementation shared by both surfaces.

THE W4-14 MULTI-SHIFT SAFETY PROPERTY IS PRESERVED AND RE-STATED WHERE IT NOW LIVES. saveTherapistScheduleAction promised that a second active template on the same weekday at a DIFFERENT LOCATION is never surfaced and never touched. Period 2 is therefore admitted ONLY when it shares period 1 location; a different-location row stays invisible, so a save cannot rewrite its location. All three W4-14 comments updated rather than left asserting a rule that no longer holds.

TWO BUGS CAUGHT DURING THE BUILD, both of the save-then-vanish class the card warned about: (1) period 2 id was posted inside the conditional block, so REMOVING a period dropped the id and the reconcile could never archive the row - the afternoon would come back. It now posts unconditionally. (2) archives run BEFORE writes within a weekday, because removing the afternoon and widening the morning across the day would otherwise make period 1 overlap a still-active period 2 and be refused for a schedule that is perfectly legal.

VALIDATION hard-blocks the SCHEDULE form only (Guardar disabled, reason printed on the offending day). That is not a breach of the standing rule: that rule is about APPOINTMENT saves. The server needs no second opinion - assertNoOverlap in lib/admin/availability.ts already refuses an overlapping sibling, so a crafted POST is refused by the check that has always guarded this table.

E2E ADDED, and it is the one test the card actually needed: add a second period, save, RE-OPEN and assert both periods came back with a non-empty p2 id, then remove it, save, and assert it is gone rather than hidden. Unit tests prove each layer; only the round trip proves they agree.

STILL OPEN: the WF-03 visual gate. Ivan sets a two-period day, saves, re-opens, and confirms ON THE AGENDA that the gap behaves as outside working hours - the last step tests the recon rather than the screen.

MERGED #818 (6c906f4). The e2e ran and passed in CI shard 3 in 6.8s: add a second period, save, RE-OPEN and assert both came back with a non-empty p2 id, remove it, save, assert gone. That is the round trip the card called for.

SHIPPED IS NOT DONE ON THIS CARD. The WF-03 visual gate is still open and sits in VERIFY-QUEUE item 3: Ivan sets a two-period day, saves, re-opens, and then confirms ON THE AGENDA that the between-periods gap behaves as outside working hours. The agenda step is the one that tests the no-migration recon rather than the screen.

evidence.ref:
#806 MERGED 2026-08-05, squashed to 4c2d5bb on origin/main. The faint :30 rule is removed; hour rules only. RECON HELD: the visual was one ternary branch and the 30-minute slot under it is load-bearing, so only the border class changed - the slot is still a focusable <button> with its own onClick and aria-label, still DISABLED inside a blocked span rather than merely covered, and SLOT_HEIGHT/minToPx/W12-02 edge placement are untouched. cards.notes:
OWNER-APPROVED 2026-08-05, relayed by Ivan. Committed per WF-01 before execution.

GOAL: the day grid draws a faint rule at the :30 mark inside each hour row. Remove it. Hour lines only.

=== RECON VERDICT: THE LINE IS DECORATIVE. THE 30-MINUTE SLOT UNDER IT IS LOAD-BEARING. ===

Requirement 1 asked exactly the right question, and the answer is that both halves are true at once, which is why this needs stating precisely rather than as 'safe to remove'.

THE VISUAL IS ONE TERNARY BRANCH. apps/web/app/agenda/agenda-grid.tsx, in the day-column slot map: `m % 60 === 0 ? (i === 0 ? '' : 'border-t border-v2-border') : 'border-t border-surface-muted'`. The final branch is the :30 rule. Removing the visual means emptying that branch and nothing else.

THE STRUCTURE UNDER IT MUST NOT MOVE. `slots` is a 30-MINUTE grid and each slot div is a clickable, keyboard-focusable booking target. Slots inside a blocked span are DISABLED rather than merely covered, and the code says why: an overlay alone still lets a keyboard user tab in and press Enter, which was the real 'bookable over blocked time' hole (CB QA item 3). SLOT_HEIGHT = 48 and minToPx() do position math in 30-minute units, and the W12-02 comments record that moving a rule between the top and bottom edge previously shifted the bold hour line a full slot.

SO: delete the faint rule's classes, change NOTHING about the slot map, the click targets, the disabled logic, SLOT_HEIGHT, minToPx, or which edge the hour rule sits on. A tempting 'simplification' to an hour-granularity grid would silently halve the bookable start times and reintroduce a keyboard accessibility hole; it is out of scope and would be a defect.

Requirement 2: the line only. No other agenda visual change.

SMALL AND INDEPENDENT: buildable at any natural gap, including while halted on a migration apply. Never preempts LOOP 3.
