cards.title: JP's formal packet sign-off, gating template arming on launch day
cards.notes:
CARDED 2026-08-05 on the owner's instruction. CONFIRMED ABSENT FIRST: LAUNCH-01's sequence contained no JP step at all - a search of that card for JP, packet, sign-off and signed returned nothing. It arms REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND and INVITES_LIVE_SEND with no clinical gate above them.

UNBLOCK CONDITION: a signed packet from JP. BLOCKS ONLY LAUNCH-01's ARMING STEPS - nothing pre-launch, nothing in LOOP 3, nothing any patient can currently reach. It must not become a reason to stall build work.

THE ONE-LINE AMENDMENT DOES NOT SUBSTITUTE FOR IT. JP approved amending the 48h action line on 2026-08-05 (WF-02); that is approval of a change, not sign-off of the packet as a whole.

WHAT THIS CARDING TURNED UP, and it is the reason the step is worth more than a formality: THE PACKET WAS TEN-FOR-TEN WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN APPROVAL STATE. Every section read 'Estado: bloqueado (approved: false)' while the registry had carried approved:true since #766 on 2026-08-03. So the artefact JP would have signed said all ten bodies were blocked by approval when approval had already been given and the ONLY remaining lock was REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND.

THAT ERROR RAN IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: it UNDERSTATED the exposure. A reader counted two locks between an approved body and a patient's phone where there was one. Corrected in the same commit, with a drift guard added - the existing packet tests asserted STRUCTURE only (every template has a section, both 24h variants exist), never STATE, which is how a ten-fold divergence sat unnoticed through two waves.

SO WHEN JP SIGNS, HE SIGNS SOMETHING TRUE. That was not the case an hour ago.

SCOPED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-05, and the card stays. The rationale is worth keeping because it distinguishes two things that look alike: registry approval WAS recorded through board process (#766, 2026-08-03), but the PACKET is the formal sign-off artefact, its Aprovado checkbox was never ticked, and until this batch the document it offered for signature was FALSE.

SCOPE: JP signs the CORRECTED packet ONCE. It gates LAUNCH-01's template arming steps only - nothing pre-launch, nothing in LOOP 3, nothing any patient can reach today.

THE WF-02 ONE-LINE APPROVAL IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE. It is provenance for the 48h amendment and is recorded as such on the packet's own section 3 (dated 2026-08-05 rather than the blanket 2026-08-03). Approving a change is not signing the whole.

cards.title: Owner ruling: supervision minimized - one acceptance session at wave end, four return conditions
cards.notes:
RULING, OWNER 2026-08-05. Ivan exits checkpoint supervision.

1. R6 (WF-09) AMENDED. VERIFY-QUEUE no longer triggers at 3 items; it accumulates SILENTLY for the whole wave. ONE acceptance session at wave end - a single numbered checklist, URL plus expected screen per item, run in one sitting. Gates whose evidence is owner-screen (WF-03) stay open until then and flip in a batch.

   AN OPEN GATE AWAITING THE BATCH IS HEALTHY STATE, and that sentence is the one a future session most needs. Readiness will now UNDERSTATE what is built, deliberately. Nobody should read 4/9 as stalled, and nobody should be tempted to flip a WF-03 gate on green CI to make the number look right - that is the exact mistake WF-03 exists to prevent, and this ruling makes it more tempting rather than less.

2. RETURN CONDITIONS, EXACTLY FOUR: a genuine owner decision (money, launch, legal, clinical, vendor), a migration apply request, wave complete, or a live exposure. Nothing else returns. Questions not gating 2+ cards accumulate on the cards and surface at wave end.

3. NON-GATING CONFIRMATORY CHECKS whose properties are already unit-proven are DEFERRED-BY-DECISION by default, not queued. They stop appearing as owed work. The distinction that matters: deferred means someone decided, pending means someone forgot.

4. MIGRATION APPLIES REMAIN THE SINGLE STANDING TOUCHPOINT. Choreography unchanged - halt loud, exact apply block carrying its own checkout line, same-day turnaround, verify before merge. While halted, keep building everything schema-independent.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RELAX. WF-03 still governs what CLOSES a patient- or staff-visible card: the owner's deployed screen, not a green gate. This ruling changes WHEN he is asked, never WHAT counts - the same distinction WF-09 drew when batching was introduced. Evidence standards, the validator, migration choreography and the halt-loud rule on premise mismatch are all untouched.

cards.title: 14 appointments still 'scheduled' with starts_at in the past - days not being closed out

evidence.ref: Rodica via Ivan 2026-08-06: daily close-out (completed or no_show) becomes mandatory practice once real clients are migrated; the current stale rows are navigation-phase testing artifacts

cards.notes:
OBSERVED 2026-08-05 from the owner's own production query, run while finding an appointment for the token test. NOT A DEFECT, and carded as an operational observation so it is not mistaken for one.

THE DATA: status scheduled, n=14, earliest 2026-07-31 10:00, latest 2026-08-07 15:00. Alongside completed n=8, no_show n=1, cancelled n=1. So roughly a week of past appointments sits in a live state, never moved to completed or no_show.

MOST LIKELY CAUSE IS WORKFLOW, NOT CODE: reception not closing out the day. That is why this is low priority and routed to Rodica via Ivan rather than into a build queue.

TWO REAL INTERACTIONS, worth knowing before anyone 'fixes' the data:
  - listOpenSlots carries a past-slot floor that sweeps past times out of bookable slots, so these are not offered to patients. The stale status does not open a booking hole.
  - Migration 0052 made a no_show RELEASE its slot. An appointment left as scheduled never reaches that path, so the release never fires - harmless while the slot is in the past, but it means the 0052 behaviour is untested against real data.

DO NOT BULK-UPDATE THESE. Marking a past appointment completed asserts the patient attended, and marking it no_show asserts they did not; both are clinical and billing statements about a real person. Only the clinic can say which. A script that guessed would be writing false records at scale.

POST-LAUNCH, non-blocking. Nothing about launch depends on it.

CLOSED 2026-08-06 AS OWNER-ACKNOWLEDGED, which is the board convention for an operational observation the owner has taken and answered. Rodica, via Ivan: the team will close out each day (completed or no_show) as MANDATORY PRACTICE once real clients are migrated onto the platform, and the current stale rows are navigation-phase TESTING ARTIFACTS rather than a data defect.

COMPLETION TRIGGER IS LIVE OPERATION, not a build step. Nothing here is engineering work and no code changes. The two real interactions recorded above (listOpenSlots and the no-show slot release) are unaffected by testing artifacts and stay true.

IT DEPENDS ON A THING THAT HAS NO CARD, and that is the finding worth more than this closure - see LAUNCH-03-client-data-migration, created from this reply.

cards.title: Which artefact carries the PORTAL SESSION after a verified OTP - three committed facts cannot all hold

evidence.ref: #825 merged 2026-08-06 (aab93b0) - Option B ruled and built: the portal owns the patient session cookie, apps/api mints and verifies only. The 503-at-handler-scope posture for a missing PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET is pinned by three tests (verify 503 before the code check, trusted 503 before the device check, 503 distinguishable from the 401 refusal) plus a scan test that refuses a module-scope assertion.

cards.notes:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING THE SESSION MINT, 2026-08-05, and raised rather than resolved because resolving it means picking a product decision nobody has made. It does NOT block LOOP 3: none of LOOP 3 nine DoD lines requires it, and the claim transaction ships without it.

THE THREE FACTS, each re-derived from committed code, not remembered:
1. apps/api/lib/auth/patient.ts:63 getPatientPrincipal accepts ONLY a cryptographically verified SUPABASE-ISSUED JWT carrying role=patient. There is no other principal shape and no local signing key anywhere in the repo.
2. apps/api/lib/auth/no-session-minting.test.ts:41-50 scans all of apps/api and fails if ANY file mentions generateLink, signInWithPassword, signInWithOtp, setSession or admin.createUser. That test is WF-08 own artefact and it is what makes Decision D enforceable rather than aspirational.
3. apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.ts:65 refuses any patient row whose auth_user_id is NOT null (WF-07). So the first successful login would set auth_user_id and EVERY LATER LOGIN BY THE SAME PATIENT WOULD REFUSE - unless the trusted device carries them, and that expires at 30 days by ruling.

A working phone-only portal login cannot satisfy all three. Something has to give, and which one is a decision with real consequences.

OPTIONS, with the trade named:
(a) The API mints the Supabase user at claim time (admin.createUser + a session), and the scan grows ONE narrow allowance on the OTP claim path. Cost: the property in fact 2 stops being absolute, and it is the only reason Decision D is enforceable today.
(b) The session becomes OURS, not Supabase - a short-lived signed cookie the API issues and getPatientPrincipal learns to accept as a second principal source. Cost: a second auth boundary to keep correct, next to the one that already had a real incident (SEC-W1-patient-jwt-verify).
(c) auth_user_id stops being the linkage key: the OTP claim links by phone and the patient never gets a Supabase auth user at all. Cost: RLS jwt_patient_id() and docs/architecture.md:360-362 both assume auth.uid() to patients.auth_user_id, so this is a change to the RLS story, not just to a column.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT if no answer arrives: (b). It keeps fact 2 intact, keeps WF-07 refusal semantics intact, and confines the new surface to one file that can be adversarially tested the way jwt.ts already is. It is also the only option that does not touch production auth identities.

WHAT SHIPS MEANWHILE: verify returns the resolved patientId and plants the trusted-device cookie. The portal login SCREENS are not built either, and they cannot be finished without this answer, since the screen after the code is the one that needs a session.

=== RULED 2026-08-06: OPTION B. Own signed session cookie as a SECOND PRINCIPAL SOURCE. UNBLOCKED. ===

OWNER RATIONALE, recorded verbatim in substance: it is the only option that preserves BOTH committed protections - the no-Supabase-session scan stays binding, and WF-07 already-linked refusal stays - while touching no production auth identity and adding no vendor.

CONSTRAINTS AS RULED:
- HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, server-side signed.
- Signing secret in a NEW env var. PURPLE names it and states which Vercel projects and scopes need it; the VALUE is Ivan to generate and set, and never enters this terminal.
- Boot fails LOUD where the var is required and missing, matching the #763 posture.
- Lifetime is PURPLE to design within Decision D: trusted device 30 days, session SHORTER than that, refresh semantics documented on this card.
- The API accepts this cookie as a patient principal ALONGSIDE Supabase staff tokens, fail-closed on everything else.

PG1 DOES NOT FLIP ON THIS. It flips at the acceptance session on Ivan screen, per WF-03. Portal login screens are unblocked as of this ruling.

=== BUILT 2026-08-06. THE SESSION ARTEFACT SHIPS; THE LOGIN SCREENS DO NOT YET. ===

DESIGN, all of it recorded here because the card is the spec under WF-01:

ENV VAR NAME: PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET. PLACEMENT: Vercel project osteojp-api ONLY, scopes Production + Preview + Development, marked Sensitive, minimum 32 characters (openssl rand -base64 32). The PORTAL project must NOT have it - the portal never verifies this cookie, it asks the API who the caller is, so one project holds the secret and one place rotates it. VALUE IS IVAN TO GENERATE AND SET; it never entered this terminal.

LIFETIME, the one judgement rather than a ruling: SESSION 12 HOURS, absolute, no sliding. Long enough for a clinic visit plus the booking afterwards, short enough that a cookie lifted from a shared or family device is dead the same day. Decision D fixes the device at 30 days and requires the session to be shorter; this is the shorter one.

REFRESH SEMANTICS: there is no refresh token, because the DEVICE COOKIE IS ONE. When the session expires the browser still holds the 30-day device cookie, so POST /api/v1/auth/otp/trusted mints a fresh session with no SMS and no code. Nothing slides and nothing extends itself: the device still dies on its original 30-day boundary, and when it does the patient gets an SMS like anyone else. Worst case for a stolen session cookie is bounded by the shorter of the two windows, and revoking the device ends both.

FAIL-CLOSED POSTURE: no development default, deliberately - a hard-coded dev secret is a signing key in a public repository. A missing or under-32-character secret makes mint THROW and verify return null. The two minting routes call assertPatientSessionEnv() at MODULE LOAD, so a misconfiguration fails at deploy rather than at a patient who typed the right code (the #763 class). Verification-only paths fail closed instead of taking the app down.

FORGERY DEFENCES: HS256 PINNED via an algorithms allowlist, so an attacker-controlled alg header cannot select none; issuer and audience pinned so a token minted elsewhere in the estate cannot be replayed; exp required; both ids re-validated as uuids after verification. Tested with a hand-built alg:none token and a wrong-secret token.

THE PRINCIPAL userId IS otp:<patientId>, NOT A UUID. That field is documented as the Supabase auth user id and an OTP patient has none; a synthetic uuid would be a fabricated identity. A test asserts it can never be mistaken for one. Nothing in apps/api reads it today.

CONTRACT CHANGE: isTrusted now returns { patientId, tenantId } instead of a bare patient id, for exactly the reason it already returned an id rather than a boolean - a second lookup is a second chance to attribute a device to the wrong patient, and now to the wrong TENANT, since the session carries a tenant claim. The tenant comes from the device ROW, never from a request; that route takes no body at all.

WF-08 SCAN EXTENDED, NOT WEAKENED: every Supabase session-minting symbol is still absent from apps/api. Three new assertions guard the new mint - it is reachable only from the two OTP routes, both assert the secret at boot, and neither puts the token in a response body.

CI: the DB-gated job gained a THROWAWAY fixture value, written in the open so nobody mistakes it for a secret, because the apps/api DB-gated suite imports the verify route and that route asserts at boot.

STILL TO BUILD ON THIS CARD: the portal login screens end to end (phone screen, code screen, the trusted-device check on load, and the three pt-PT degradation copies wired to real screens). PG1 flips only at the acceptance session on Ivan screen, per WF-03.

DEFECT IN MY OWN DESIGN, CAUGHT BY THE VERCEL BUILD AND FIXED 2026-08-06. The boot assertion was at MODULE SCOPE, and that failed the osteojp-api BUILD: "Failed to collect page data for /api/v1/auth/otp/trusted". Next.js imports route modules to collect page data during next build, and a build runs WITHOUT runtime secrets by design. A build is not a boot - that was a category error, and it would have blocked every PR, including ones touching nothing near auth, until the secret existed.

WHAT THE CONTROL WAS ACTUALLY FOR: not "an error early" but NO SILENT DEGRADATION - never a login path that returns a success-shaped nothing, and never a 401 a patient reads as "I typed it wrong". A 503 with a server log naming the variable satisfies that completely: it is not silent, it is not confusable with user error, and it is the honest status - the server is misconfigured, the request was fine.

SO THE CHECK MOVED INTO THE HANDLER, first line, before any parsing or lookup. Proven by rebuilding apps/api with the variable UNSET, which is exactly the Vercel condition that failed: the build now completes and both routes register. Three tests pin the posture - verify answers 503 without reaching the code check, trusted answers 503 without reaching the device check, and 503 is asserted DISTINGUISHABLE from the 401 refusal. The scan test now also refuses a module-scope assertion, so this cannot come back.

PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET IN FLIGHT 2026-08-06: Ivan is setting it on osteojp-api ONLY, all scopes, Sensitive, 32-byte random. The deploy-time behaviour stands as fixed this stretch - the assertion is at HANDLER scope, so a deployment without the value builds and deploys, then answers 503 with a server log naming the variable rather than 401.

CLOSED 2026-08-06. PR #825 merged at aab93b0. PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET was SET by Ivan on 2026-08-06, osteojp-api only, all scopes, Sensitive - so the deploy-time hazard this card was held on is gone, and the handler-scope assertion remains as the guard against it recurring.

cards.title: The new required check is path-filtered, so it never reports on most PRs and blocks every merge

evidence.ref: #820 (8059492) - required check now reports on every PR; proven on #818, which touches none of the filtered paths and reported "Validate spec + drift check pass 5s" where it previously reported nothing

cards.notes:
LIVE MERGE BLOCKER, found 2026-08-05 the moment the ruling took effect, and fixed the same day.

WHAT HAPPENED. The owner made "Validate spec + drift check" a required status check (INPUT 1 ruling 1, recorded on W13-CI-01). That workflow was PATH-FILTERED at the trigger: apps/api/app/api, apps/web/app/api/v1, docs/api/openapi.yaml, scripts/check-openapi-drift.mjs, and its own file. A pull request touching none of those paths does not run it, so the required context NEVER REPORTS and GitHub holds the PR at "Expected - waiting for status to be reported" indefinitely. Not slow. Never arriving.

PROVEN, NOT INFERRED: PR #818 (W13-A, a UI-only change) went green on every other gate - lint/typecheck/test, DB-gated, all three e2e shards, the aggregate - and gh reported mergeStateStatus BLOCKED with mergeable MERGEABLE. The branch-protection API lists four required contexts; the PR reported three of them. The missing one is this workflow.

SCOPE: EVERY future PR that does not touch an API route or the spec. That is most board cards - UI, board updates, docs, scheduling, reminders. The repository was one ruling away from being unable to merge anything.

THE FIX, and it is the pattern this repo already documented for itself. db-tests.yml carries the rule in its own header: "The job still runs (so the branch-protection check is always reported) but exits green immediately with a skip notice." openapi-drift.yml now does the same - the trigger is unconditional, a first step diffs base..head for the same five path patterns, and the lint and drift steps are gated on that step instead. Nothing installs when nothing relevant changed; the context always reports.

THE GENERAL RULE, worth more than this instance: a required check must be REPORTABLE ON EVERY PULL REQUEST. Any workflow wired into branch protection has to run unconditionally and decide internally what work to do, never decide at the trigger whether to exist. Same family as the W13-CI-01 lesson that a check context IS a job name - both are about branch protection depending on facts the workflow file controls silently.

FIXED AND PROVEN 2026-08-05, #820 (8059492). The proof is the PR that was stuck: after the fix merged, #818 - which touches no API route and no spec file - reported "Validate spec + drift check" as pass in 5 seconds, where before it reported nothing at all. #818 then merged with all four required contexts green. Total time from ruling to blocker to fix: one session.

cards.title: The bookable-services allowlist matches ONE of 20 production services - the portal offers at most Fisioterapia

evidence.ref: catalog write applied to production 2026-08-06 from osteojp-prod-apply detached at 2c0c708: preview 11 changes / 4 left alone, --execute applied 11, verification read confirms 12 bookable of 20. Full pasted record: docs/notifications-work-notes.md, "Catalog write applied to production (2026-08-06)"

cards.notes:
FOUND BY THE 0057 APPLY, 2026-08-05. The migration is correct; applying it is what made this visible. PREMISE MISMATCH, halted loud rather than reconciled.

THE TWO CONFLICTING STATEMENTS:
1. apps/api/lib/appointments/services.ts:32-44 calls BOOKABLE_SERVICE_NAMES the "Canonical patient-self-bookable OsteoJP services": osteopatia, fisioterapia, massagem terapeutica, pilates terapeutico.
2. The production services table holds 20 rows and only ONE of those four names exists in it: Fisioterapia. There is no row normalizing to osteopatia, none to massagem terapeutica, none to pilates terapeutico.

RE-DERIVED, not eyeballed: the production names were run through normalizeServiceName and compared to the allowlist. One match.

WHAT PRODUCTION ACTUALLY SELLS (verbatim from the read): 1.a consulta / Avaliacao (Osteopatia ou Fisioenergetica/Kinesiologia/Posturologia); Diversos; Drenagem Linfatica Manual (Metodo Wodere); Fisioenergetica/Kinesiologia/Posturologia; Fisioterapia; Massagem 4 Maos (2 terapeutas); Medicina Chinesa/Acupuntura; NESA; Osteopatia/Posturologia; Pilates - Aula Experimental (1.a vez); Pilates - Aula Individual; Pilates mensal 1x/semana - grupo; Pilates mensal 2x/semana - grupo; Pressoterapia; R.P.G. - Reeducacao Postural Global; Sessao Familia/Amigos (2 pessoas ao mesmo tempo); Tratamento Terapeutico. PLUS THREE ROWS LITERALLY NAMED "-".

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is live today, not introduced by anything in Wave 13. store.ts filters the portal catalog through isBookableServiceName, so the patient booking wizard offers AT MOST ONE service - Fisioterapia - and ZERO if that row is inactive or internal_only. An osteopathy clinic whose portal cannot sell osteopathy. "Osteopatia/Posturologia" is not "Osteopatia" to an exact normalized comparison, and nothing in the code was ever going to notice.

WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: every test of the allowlist uses FIXTURE names that match it, and the seed data uses matching names too. The rule was only ever tested against data built to satisfy it. The first time it met the real catalog was this apply.

WHAT IS NEEDED, and it is a product decision I will not guess (rule 15): WHICH of the real services may a patient self-book. That is per-service and partly clinical - NESA, R.P.G., 1.a consulta and Diversos are not obviously self-bookable, and Massagem 4 Maos / Sessao Familia / the Pilates mensal tiers are exactly the six LOOP 4 step 6 routes to request-mode rather than direct booking.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT if no answer arrives: flag patient_bookable = true for Osteopatia/Posturologia, Fisioterapia, Fisioenergetica/Kinesiologia/Posturologia, Medicina Chinesa/Acupuntura, Drenagem Linfatica Manual, Pressoterapia, Tratamento Terapeutico and Pilates - Aula Individual; request-mode for Massagem 4 Maos, Sessao Familia and both Pilates mensal tiers; and leave 1.a consulta, NESA, R.P.G., Diversos, Pilates Aula Experimental and the three "-" rows false. That is a starting point for JP to correct, NOT a ruling.

SECOND FINDING, smaller: THREE services are named "-". Data hygiene, own loose end, not part of this decision.

LOOP 4 step 4 (delete the allowlist, replace both call sites, add the missing internal_only check) is HELD until this is answered. Deleting the allowlist today would simply replace one broken rule with a faithful copy of it.

=== FULL PROD CATALOG READ 2026-08-06. THE NUMBER IS 1 OF 16. ===

All 20 rows, all bound to TODAS (every location), so there is no per-location dimension to this decision.

SELLABLE TODAY (active, not internal) - 16 rows, with price and duration:
  1.a consulta / Avaliacao (Osteopatia ou Fisioenergetica/Kinesiologia/Posturologia)  75.00  55min
  Drenagem Linfatica Manual (Metodo Wodere)  60.00  55min
  Fisioenergetica/Kinesiologia/Posturologia  70.00  55min
  Fisioterapia  55.00  55min  <- THE ONLY ONE THE PORTAL OFFERS
  Massagem 4 Maos (2 terapeutas)  70.00  55min
  Medicina Chinesa/Acupuntura  55.00  55min
  NESA  50.00  60min
  Osteopatia/Posturologia  70.00  55min
  Pilates - Aula Experimental (1.a vez)  45.00  60min
  Pilates - Aula Individual  35.00  60min
  Pilates mensal 1x/semana - grupo (3 a 4 pessoas)  125.00  60min
  Pilates mensal 2x/semana - grupo (3 a 4 pessoas)  125.00  60min
  Pressoterapia  35.00  50min
  R.P.G. - Reeducacao Postural Global  60.00  60min
  Sessao Familia/Amigos (2 pessoas ao mesmo tempo)  60.00  60min
  Tratamento Terapeutico  55.00  55min

NOT SELLABLE: Diversos (internal_only, correctly flagged already, 0.00) and THREE INACTIVE ROWS LITERALLY NAMED "-" with no price. CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER NOTE: those three are is_active=false, so nobody can book them, not reception either. They are dead placeholder rows and the hygiene item is LOW, not a risk.

SECOND PREMISE MISMATCH, SAME ROOT CAUSE, found in the same read. WAVE-13.md:233 rules request-mode for "Massagem 4 Maos, Sessao Familia, and the four Pilates mensal tiers". PRODUCTION HAS TWO Pilates mensal tiers, not four: 1x/semana and 2x/semana, both 125.00. So the ruled request-mode set is SIX services and only FOUR of them exist. The wave doc, like the allowlist, was written against a catalog that does not match production.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT, sharpened now that prices and durations are visible. A STARTING POINT FOR JP TO CORRECT, NOT A RULING:
  DIRECT (patient picks a slot, auto-confirmed) - 8: Osteopatia/Posturologia, Fisioterapia, Fisioenergetica/Kinesiologia/Posturologia, Medicina Chinesa/Acupuntura, Drenagem Linfatica Manual, Pressoterapia, Tratamento Terapeutico, Pilates - Aula Individual.
  REQUEST-MODE (pedido, reception confirms) - 4: Massagem 4 Maos, Sessao Familia, Pilates mensal 1x, Pilates mensal 2x. These are the multi-resource ones and they are the whole of the ruled set that actually exists.
  NOT PATIENT-BOOKABLE - 4: 1.a consulta / Avaliacao and Pilates Aula Experimental, because BOTH are first-visit products and a portal user is by construction an EXISTING patient (WF-07 links only an existing patient row, so a first consultation is not something a portal user needs); NESA, which is the contraindication-sensitive service; and R.P.G., which is a programme rather than a single session.

That is 12 of 16 offered in some form, against 1 today.

WAVE DOC ERROR RULED 2026-08-06: WF-01 already made the card the spec, so THIS CARD SUPERSEDES WAVE-13.md:233 and the wave doc is NOT rewritten. The correction of record: production holds TWO Pilates mensal tiers (1x/semana and 2x/semana, both 125.00), not four. The ruled request-mode set is therefore SIX NAMED and FOUR REAL.

=== JP INTERIM RULING 2026-08-06, RELAYED BY IVAN. WRITE STILL HELD. ===

JP answered: "start with option B for now, then see how it goes."

WORKING INTERPRETATION, stated because it is an interpretation and not a quote: LAUNCH POSTURE IS REQUEST-MODE FOR ALL BOOKABLE SERVICES. All 12 bookable services (the proposed 8 plus the 4 multi-resource) start as a pedido that reception confirms. ZERO auto-confirmed direct bookings at launch. The 4 not-bookable stay off: 1.a consulta, Pilates Aula Experimental, NESA, R.P.G. Direct booking becomes a post-launch graduation JP rules per service.

CONFIRMATION IS PENDING and the alternative reading REMAINS POSSIBLE until JP confirms in one line: that "option B" meant the 8-direct-plus-4-request split exactly as proposed. Both readings are live, so BOTH are parameterized in the write script and NEITHER is executed.

BUILD CONSEQUENCE: request-mode is now the PRIMARY LAUNCH PATH and takes priority inside LOOP 4 - pedido creation, the reception confirm surface, the R1 event kind for pedido de marcacao, and notifications to reception plus the assigned therapist per R2. Direct booking is still built, because it is both the graduation target and the alternative reading, but it comes second.

=== JP CONFIRMED 2026-08-06, verbatim "certo", relayed by Ivan. THE INTERPRETATION IS NOW THE RULING. ===

LAUNCH POSTURE: request-mode for ALL 12 bookable services, ZERO auto-confirmed. The 4 excluded stay off (1.a consulta, Pilates Aula Experimental, NESA, R.P.G.). Direct booking is a post-launch graduation JP rules per service, so the 8/4 split survives ONLY as the graduation target and is no longer a live alternative reading.

JP ADDED AN EXPECTATION, and it is build-blocking rather than a nice-to-have: PORTAL PEDIDOS MUST SURFACE IN THE NOTIFICATION CENTRE. Any unbuilt or unwired link in that chain - portal pedido creation, the R1 event emission, the R2 fanout to reception plus the assigned therapist, the bell - is in-scope LOOP 4 work and not a deferral.

THE WRITE IS UNBLOCKED. Variant 1 is the ruling; the script ships parameterized anyway so the graduation can reuse it per service without a rewrite.

WRITE SCRIPT BUILT AND PROVEN 2026-08-06: packages/db/scripts/w13-04-set-patient-bookable.mjs. PREVIEW BY DEFAULT, --execute to apply. Preview runs in a READ ONLY transaction; the write is tenant-scoped and id-scoped and touches patient_bookable and nothing else; a verification read runs in the same invocation and REFUSES if the final count is not 12.

RUN AGAINST A LOCAL DATABASE SEEDED WITH THE REAL 20 PRODUCTION NAMES, not against fixtures: preview showed 11 changes (Fisioterapia was already true from 0057) and 4 left alone (Diversos plus the three inactive rows named "-"); --execute applied 11 and the verification read printed exactly 12 bookable of 20; a second preview showed 0, so it is idempotent.

IT CAUGHT A BUG IN ITSELF, WHICH IS THE POINT OF RUNNING IT. The first version carried MY hand-normalized spellings and SIX OF SIXTEEN WERE WRONG: production writes an EM DASH in "Pilates - Aula Individual" and "R.P.G. - Reeducacao Postural Global", and a feminine ordinal in "1.a consulta" and "Pilates - Aula Experimental (1.a vez)". Neither is a combining diacritic, so NFD-strip leaves them alone and my hyphens and plain "a" matched nothing. The STOP condition - a ruled name matching no row - fired and refused to execute.

THE FIX WAS THE RIGHT ONE OF TWO. The lists now hold the VERBATIM production display names and both sides go through the same norm(), so there is no hand-transcription left to get wrong. Extending norm() to fold em dashes was the other option and it is wrong: it would diverge from normalizeServiceName and from 0057 SQL, which is exactly the drift this script must not introduce.

WRITE APPLIED AND VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-06. Preview 11 changes and 4 left alone, --execute applied 11, verification read in the same invocation confirmed 12 bookable of 20 - exactly JP ruled 12. Eleven and not twelve because Fisioterapia was already true, which is this card own finding. Evidence committed the same turn the output arrived, per the ratified 0057 doctrine.

THE COLUMN IS NOW CORRECT AND NO PATIENT SEES IT YET: store.ts still filters the portal catalog through isBookableServiceName. Deleting that allowlist, switching both call sites to patient_bookable, and adding the missing internalOnly check at getBookableService is LOOP 4 step 4 - one PR, never staged. Until it lands the portal still offers exactly one service.

cards.title: Real client data has to reach the platform before live operation, and nothing anywhere tracks that
cards.notes:
CREATED 2026-08-06 FROM A GAP CHECK, not from a plan. Rodica reply about closing out days referenced "migrating all the info and real clients onto the platform" as the precondition for live operation. That dependency was load-bearing and INVISIBLE.

VERDICT OF THE SEARCH, so nobody repeats it: NO SUCH CARD EXISTS ON EITHER BOARD. Both were searched by id and title for migrate/import/onboard/client-data across 60 portal cards and 49 prelaunch cards. The ten hits were all SCHEMA migrations (0051, 0052, WF-11 choreography, PL-06b, PL-31 and similar) or unrelated. Not one concerns moving patient records from wherever they live today onto this platform.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS: real-patient acceptance. Every gate can pass, every loop can ship, and the clinic still cannot operate on a platform with no patients in it. It also silently gates WF-07 phone linkage, which resolves a patient by matching a phone against an EXISTING patient row - no imported patients means every portal login refuses, correctly, forever.

DELIBERATELY NOT DESIGNED HERE. The instruction was to make the dependency visible, not to solve it. What is undefined and needs the owner: the SOURCE (Fisiozero, Stylus.pt, spreadsheets, paper, some combination), the FORMAT, the IMPORT PATH, who verifies the result, and what happens to records that fail validation - NIF, phone and location are all now constrained on this platform in ways an old system may not satisfy. Note packages/fisiozero-extractor exists in this repo, which suggests an extraction path was at least started once; whether it is current, complete or abandoned is unknown and is part of what the owner needs to answer.

OWNER: Ivan plus the clinic team. Pre-launch. Blocking real-patient acceptance.

CONTEXT INCOMING 2026-08-06: Ivan is answering the source question - old system name, rough patient count, and whether packages/fisiozero-extractor is current or abandoned. HELD BLOCKED on that answer. Not designed, deliberately.

=== SOURCE QUESTION ANSWERED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-06. UNBLOCKED, AND RE-SEQUENCED. ===

1. SOURCE: the clinic's previous platform, vendor contact Eduardo. The vendor confirmed IN WRITING: a ONE-SHOT export, CSV files plus a ZIP of documents, with filenames referenced from each episode's CSV row. The vendor asks the clinic to name its LAST DAY on the old platform and pull everything once. NO REPEAT PULLS. Gigabytes of files.

2. SCALE: about 10,000 patients, each with appointment history, clinical records and document attachments.

3. SEQUENCING, owner ruling: the migration happens AFTER the platform and portal are fully validated and all clinic feedback is processed. It is not launch-blocking and it is not pre-launch work.

4. LOAD-BEARING IMPLICATION, and it is what makes this card real work before launch rather than after: THE EXPORT IS ONE-SHOT. There is no second pull to correct a mistake. So the import pipeline must be BUILT AND REHEARSED against a sample or synthetic dataset BEFORE the clinic names its last day. Card state: pipeline built pre-launch, rehearsed pre-launch, then the real pull.

=== RECON 2026-08-06, READ-ONLY, WITH FILE EVIDENCE. THE DISPATCH'S PATH WAS WRONG AND THE ANSWER IS BETTER THAN EXPECTED. ===

THERE IS NO packages/fisiozero-extractor. It is tools/fisiozero-extractor (@osteojp/fisiozero-extractor, private, deliberately outside packages/).

WHAT IT IS: a Tier-1 RAW ARCHIVER. Playwright drives a logged-in session against app.fisiozero.pt and saves raw bytes per patient - ficha.html, per-episode HTML, export_ficha_utente.xls, attachments - with a manifest.json carrying SHA-256 and byte count per file. tools/fisiozero-extractor/README.md:1-10.

WHAT INPUT IT EXPECTS: not files at all. A live authenticated web session (FISIOZERO_STORAGE_STATE) plus an integer patient-id range, default 174159..199974.

DOES IT MATCH THE VENDOR'S CSV-PLUS-ZIP SHAPE: NO, and it exists precisely because that shape did not exist when it was written. README.md:15-20, heading "Why scraping (not a CSV/ZIP export)": no JSON API, no free bulk export, and the paid bulk export TERMINATES CLINIC ACCESS. Last touched 2026-06-19.

CURRENT PATH OR ABANDONED: NEITHER. It is a raw-bytes insurance archive and it is orthogonal to the import. THE IMPORT PATH IS packages/db/src/migration/, and packages/db/src/migration/source.ts:1-12 says so in the file: "ADAPTER SEAM, interface only, deliberately UNIMPLEMENTED. TODO(Phase 5, blocked): implement a FisiozeroSource over the CONFIRMED CSV+ZIP EXPORT once a sample export arrives. No implementation, scraping, or field mapping may be written before that sample exists - the raw format is unknown and guessing it would bake wrong assumptions into the mapper."

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it narrows this card sharply: the pipeline BEHIND the seam is already built - staging.ts (254 lines), upsert.ts (574), validate.ts, batch-validate.ts, reconciliation.ts, health.ts, 1,660 lines total, against migration_staging_rows shipped in migration 0014. The ADAPTER is the only missing piece, and it is blocked on exactly the artefact the vendor hands over once. So the rehearsal is: implement FisiozeroSource against a SYNTHETIC CSV-plus-ZIP built to the vendor's described shape, run it through the existing staging and upsert path, and the one-shot pull then meets a proven pipeline instead of an untested one.

ONE THING STILL WORTH ASKING THE VENDOR BEFORE THE LAST DAY IS NAMED, and it costs nothing: a SAMPLE export of a handful of patients. Eduardo's one-shot condition is about the FULL pull; a sample is a different request. If a sample can be had, the adapter is written against the real format instead of a guess, and the docs/migration-notes.md edge cases (duplicates, missing NIF/DOB, orphan appointments, local-path attachments) are met with evidence rather than assumption.

=== THE EXPORT SPECIFICATION IS AUTHORED (2026-08-06). SEE LAUNCH-03a-caderno-encargos. ===

docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md, pt-PT, formal register, ready for Ivan to forward to Eduardo. Its field list is derived from packages/db/src/migration/types.ts and validate.ts rather than written from memory, so the import adapter will be built against OUR specification and not against a guess at the vendor export.

THIS CARD IS NOW THE PIPELINE WORK ONLY: implement FisiozeroSource against a synthetic CSV-plus-ZIP built to that spec, run it through the existing staging and upsert path, and rehearse. The spec itself, the vendor quote and the fee approval live on LAUNCH-03a and run in parallel.

=== SILENT APPEND 2026-08-07: THE ACCEPTANCE SESSION LEAVES PRODUCTION ROWS THAT
    ARE NOT REAL CLIENTS, AND THEY MUST NOT ENTER THIS RECONCILIATION. ===

Appended rather than carded, and NOT surfaced to Ivan: it is a note for whoever
runs the Fisiozero import, not an action for the owner.

WHAT THE SESSION CREATES, in production, permanently:
  A PATIENT ROW, `ZZ Teste Aceitacao` (docs/acceptance-session-wave-13.md section
  0e). Created deliberately so the terms-acceptance check does not write an
  APPEND-ONLY, UNREMOVABLE legal record against a real person. It carries no
  phone and no email so nothing can ever reach it.
  A TERMS ACCEPTANCE against that patient. Append-only by ruling: no UPDATE
  policy, no DELETE policy, grants revoked. IT CANNOT BE DELETED, which is why
  the patient exists at all.
  A THERAPIST/STAFF ROW, the test therapist (section 0f), used for the
  split-shift check and DEACTIVATED at item 24 rather than deleted.
  Its availability_templates rows survive the deactivation.

WHY THIS BELONGS ON LAUNCH-03 SPECIFICALLY, and it is two distinct hazards:

  1. THE RECONCILIATION COUNT. Any "patients on the platform" figure compared
     against the Fisiozero export will be OFF BY AT LEAST ONE, and a
     reconciliation that is off by one is indistinguishable from an import that
     dropped one - which is exactly the failure that check exists to catch. The
     import must EXCLUDE by id, not by name: renaming the row would break the
     exclusion silently, and a name match is not an identity.

  2. PATIENT EXPORT. These rows must not appear in any export produced for the
     clinic, for counsel, or for a data-subject request. A test fixture in a
     patient export is a data-quality defect at best and a confusing disclosure
     at worst.

THE IDS ARE WRITTEN INTO THE SESSION DOCUMENT at 0e and 0f as blanks Ivan fills
in. Whoever runs the import reads them from there. If those blanks are empty when
the import is planned, ASK before counting - do not assume the session skipped
the steps, because the acceptance row cannot be un-created and a missing id means
it is there and unidentified.

THE DEACTIVATED THERAPIST IS THE EASIER HALF: `is_active = false` already
excludes it from every staff-facing list. The patient row has no such flag, which
is why it needs an explicit exclusion rather than a filter that already exists.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-08-06. The document exists and is at docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md. What it now waits on is Ivan forwarding it to Eduardo. That is the whole of the block.

WHY IT EXISTS. The vendor asked the clinic to specify exactly which data, which fields and which format. Answering that specifies the CONTRACT the import is built against: the adapter is then written to OUR spec rather than to a guess at his export, and a delivery that deviates is a non-compliant deliverable rather than a surprise discovered on the clinic's last day.

THE FIELD LIST IS DERIVED, NOT REMEMBERED. Every column in the spec traces to a committed shape:
  pacientes.csv <- MigrationPatient (types.ts:39-57). sourceId and fullName required; dateOfBirth, sex, nif, email, phone, address, postalCode, city, notes nullable BECAUSE the target columns are; locationKeys is the clinic association.
  marcacoes.csv <- MigrationAppointment (types.ts:60-78). sourceId, patientSourceId, practitionerKey, locationKey, startsAt, endsAt and status all required, because validate.ts:46-55 rejects the row without them and the target columns are NOT NULL. serviceKey optional, matching the target.
  episodios.csv <- MigrationClinicalEpisode + MigrationClinicalRecord, deliberately merged into ONE vendor-facing file. The vendor plausibly has no episode concept, and demanding two files for a distinction their schema may not draw is how a spec becomes unquotable. The spec says exactly what to do in that case: one line per clinical record, id_episodio = the record id, estado = fechado.
  documentos.csv <- MigrationAttachment (types.ts:123-131). fileName and the ZIP path are required; mimeType and sizeBytes are optional because the clinic can derive both from the file itself.

THE STABLE PATIENT IDENTIFIER IS THE SPEC'S SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING REQUIREMENT, and it is written as such. Migration 0014's unique key is (tenant_id, source_system, entity_type, source_id), and the whole cross-record resolution in upsert.ts runs through it. Without a consistent id_paciente across all four CSVs the delivery is not reconstructable and has no value, which is why it has its own section rather than a row in a table.

CONSTRAINTS EXPRESSED THAT COME FROM THE PIPELINE, not from convention: no filtering (validate.ts accepts missing NIF and DOB, so there is no reason to drop those patients); duplicates exported as separate rows (mergeImportedPatient exists precisely to fix them AFTER import, and merge_patients() from 0005 does the repointing); cancelled and no_show exported (both are appointment_status values); the clinical signature explicitly NOT requested, because MigrationClinicalRecord.status admits only draft and locked - a signature attests a review in THIS system.

THE ONE THING ASKED FOR THAT THE DISPATCH DID NOT LIST: a 20-to-50 patient SAMPLE, framed as a request distinct from the full pull so it does not read as an attempt to reopen the one-shot condition. If it arrives, the adapter is written against the real format instead of this specification's best reading of it. If it is refused, nothing is lost and the rehearsal runs on synthetic data built from this same document.

FIELDS FLAGGED AS PLAUSIBLY UNSUPPLIABLE, each with a fallback, in section 8 of the document: appointment end time (fall back to duracao_minutos), the episode concept (one row per record), NIF/DOB/sex (leave empty, the platform allows it), mime type and size (derived), the timezone of stored instants (declare it in the manifest), appointment state (declare the vocabulary), and the clinical signature (not requested at all).

SEQUENCING, and this is why the card is high priority while the migration itself is not launch-blocking. THE SPEC GOES OUT EARLY so the vendor quote and JP's fee approval run in PARALLEL with the build. The real pull stays at the very end, on the clinic's named last day, after the platform and portal are fully validated. The rehearsal in between runs against SYNTHETIC data generated from this same document, which is what makes the one-shot pull meet a proven pipeline. A delivery that deviates from the spec is a non-compliant deliverable and goes back to the vendor: the one case where re-delivery does not violate the one-shot condition.

WHAT IS STILL NOT BUILT, and is not in scope here: the FisiozeroSource adapter itself (packages/db/src/migration/source.ts is an interface with no implementation, deliberately), the synthetic generator, and the attachment byte-copy into Supabase Storage. The 1,660 lines behind the seam - staging, upsert, validate, batch-validate, reconciliation, health - are already on main against migration_staging_rows from 0014.

=== UNDER OWNER REVIEW 2026-08-06. THE DOCUMENT IS FROZEN. ===

One correction is pending on the LOCATIONS line. Instruction, binding: DO NOT MODIFY docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md until that correction arrives. Not a wording pass, not a typo fix, not a re-render. The next edit to that file is the owner's correction and nothing else.

The document was published for review at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/faefe7e7-978b-4300-82f7-37b4b9663cce so it could be read and forwarded without waiting on #830 to merge. Sending it was never gated on the merge: it is a document, and forwarding it is an email. The board card saying blocked_on ivan meant waiting for Ivan to SEND it, which was ambiguous enough to read as waiting for a merge - recorded here so the next reader does not repeat the misreading.

=== OWNER CORRECTION APPLIED 2026-08-06. MONTEMOR-O-NOVO DOES NOT EXIST. THE DOCUMENT IS UNFROZEN AND READY TO SEND. ===

The clinic has EXACTLY TWO locations: Linda-a-Velha and Castelo Branco. The emitente line named a third. Fixed, and the whole document was grepped: zero occurrences remain.

THE STATED CAUSE IS WRONG, AND CORRECTING IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TYPO. The relay recorded this as "a location introduced into a vendor-facing binding document without any source in repo, board, or ruling". There IS a source, and it is the most authoritative file in the repo:
  CLAUDE.md:4 - "Unified clinic platform for OsteoJP (Linda-a-Velha, Castelo Branco, Montemor-o-Novo)." CLAUDE.md is loaded into EVERY session and its instructions are declared to override default behaviour.
  README.md:3 - the same sentence.
  docs/architecture.md:13 and :202 - three locations, one marked "(opening)".
  docs/jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md:49-56 - a JP ruling ABOUT Montemor-o-Novo: configured as a third clinic, not yet open, to appear with a "Coming soon" notice or be hidden.
  47 committed files in total mention it, including the cutover runbook, launch comms, the QA load-test record and two PDF templates carrying a TODO for its address.

SO THE FAILURE WAS NOT INVENTION. It was TRANSCRIPTION FROM COMMITTED GROUND TRUTH THAT IS ITSELF WRONG. That distinction is the whole lesson: the rule "state only facts traceable to committed ground truth" was FOLLOWED here and still produced a wrong vendor-facing document, because the ground truth is stale. Recording the cause as invention would leave 47 files intact to seed the same error into the next document, the next session and the next vendor email.

WHAT I FIXED, and the boundary is deliberate: the caderno, plus the six Supabase auth email footers written in this same session, which are PATIENT- AND STAFF-FACING and would have mailed a nonexistent clinic to real people. supabase-email-templates.test.ts now pins it - 40/40, with an explicit assertion that no template contains "Montemor", so a future edit copying the stale line out of CLAUDE.md fails instead of shipping.

WHAT I DID NOT FIX, and it needs an owner decision rather than my initiative: the other 45 files. Correcting them touches a committed JP RULING (jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md), the architecture doc, the cutover runbook and historical QA records. Rewriting a recorded ruling is not a typo fix. RECOMMENDED, in order: correct CLAUDE.md:4 and README.md:3 FIRST and on their own, because CLAUDE.md is loaded every session and is therefore the one that keeps reproducing the error; then decide separately whether the JP ruling is superseded (Montemor abandoned) or historical (recorded as it was). Carded as LE-montemor-ground-truth.

=== DEFERRED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-06. DO NOT RE-RAISE. ===

The caderno is sent to the vendor AT THE VERY END of the project, not now. The document stays FROZEN as corrected and is not edited again.

THE COST IS ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A SURPRISE: a late send puts the vendor QUOTE, JP's FEE APPROVAL and the EXTRACTION PREP on the end-phase critical path, in series rather than in parallel with the build. The original sequencing note on this card argued the opposite. That argument is superseded, not forgotten.

LANE DEVIATION as on END-legal-sweep: deferred-by-decision does not exist in the pinned lane set, so this is status HALTED with home_lane loose_ends and blocked_on null - not todo, not blocked, out of the people lane, skipped by the next-card picker.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the corrected document is at docs/migration/caderno-encargos-exportacao.md, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/faefe7e7-978b-4300-82f7-37b4b9663cce, and it is ready to send whenever the end phase arrives.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-06 by grepping the repo after the owner corrected the caderno. The clinic has EXACTLY TWO locations, Linda-a-Velha and Castelo Branco. Montemor-o-Novo does not exist.

IT IS NAMED IN 47 COMMITTED FILES, and two of them are the files every session is told to trust:
  CLAUDE.md:4 - "Unified clinic platform for OsteoJP (Linda-a-Velha, Castelo Branco, Montemor-o-Novo)." This file is loaded into EVERY session and declares that its instructions override default behaviour. It is the single highest-leverage wrong fact in the repo.
  README.md:3 - the same sentence, the first thing a new contributor reads.
  docs/architecture.md:13, :202, :560 - three locations, one "(opening)", plus an open item for its opening date and contacts.
  docs/jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md:49-56 - a JP RULING about it: configured as a third clinic, not yet open, to appear with a "Coming soon" notice or be hidden from booking entirely.
  docs/cutover-runbook.md:81, docs/launch-comms.md:83 - launch-day checklists that send staff to a clinic that does not exist.
  docs/pdf-templates/invoice-fatura-recibo.html:492 and declaration-tratamento.html:316 - commented-out footer blocks with a TODO for its address, on documents that are printed for patients.
  docs/qa-performance-loadtest-2026-06-20.md:24 and qa-seed-appointments-2026-06-19.md:65 - historical QA records asserting 3 locations and 24 appointments there.

WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT A TYPO. It already produced one wrong VENDOR-FACING binding document and six PATIENT-FACING email footers in a single session, by a terminal that was following the rule - state only what is traceable to committed ground truth. The rule held; the ground truth is stale. Until CLAUDE.md is corrected, every future session starts by being told the wrong thing, and the next document repeats it.

WHY IT IS BLOCKED ON IVAN RATHER THAN JUST FIXED. Three of these are not typo fixes and are not mine to decide:
  1. jp-decisions-2026-06-17.md records a RULING. Rewriting a recorded ruling to match present reality destroys the record of what was decided and when. The question is whether Montemor was ABANDONED (the ruling is superseded and should be annotated, not deleted) or never existed (the ruling was made on a false premise, which is a different and worse finding).
  2. The QA records are HISTORICAL measurements. They say what was measured then. Editing them makes past evidence lie.
  3. The PDF templates carry a TODO for its address. Deleting the TODO is right if it is abandoned; nobody should guess.

RECOMMENDED, in this order, because the first is cheap and stops the bleeding:
  A. Correct CLAUDE.md:4 and README.md:3 ALONE, in one small PR. Two lines. This is the one that keeps reproducing the error, because CLAUDE.md is loaded every session.
  B. Correct docs/architecture.md and the two launch checklists - forward-looking operational docs that would send a person somewhere.
  C. Owner decides on the JP ruling and the QA records: annotate as superseded, or leave as history with a dated note. Never silently rewrite either.

ALREADY FIXED, in the branch that found it: the caderno (vendor-facing) and the six Supabase auth email footers (patient- and staff-facing). supabase-email-templates.test.ts asserts no template contains "Montemor", so the stale line cannot be copied back out of CLAUDE.md without failing CI.

cards.title: merge-on-green.sh hardcoded the required-check list, so it would have merged on a partial picture

evidence.ref: #824 merged 2026-08-06 (3fdd1b6) - merge-on-green.sh now reads the required-check set from branch protection instead of a hardcoded list, refuses any PR that is not OPEN, and RE-READS the PR state after merging rather than trusting the exit code. Distinct exit codes: 0 merged, 1 red or refused, 2 timed out, 3 bad usage. .claude/commands/ship.md updated to match.

cards.notes:
SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS W13-CI-03, found the same day and one layer down. Branch protection owns the list of what gates a merge; anything that keeps its own copy eventually disagrees with it.

WHAT WAS WRONG. scripts/merge-on-green.sh, which /ship drives, carried a literal set of THREE contexts: Lint + typecheck + test, DB-gated tests, Playwright E2E. The owner made a FOURTH required on 2026-08-06 (Validate spec + drift check). The script could not know: it would have declared GREEN while that check was still pending, fired a merge GitHub then refused, and - had the check gone on to fail - reported a green that was never true.

NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS LANE. The script predates the wave (#311, session 13). What changed under it was the required set. It is fixed here because this lane found it and because the ruling that exposed it landed here.

THE FIX: the required contexts are read from the branch-protection API on every run, and if that read fails the script REFUSES rather than falling back to a guessed list - guessing is precisely what broke it. A context that has not reported at all counts as PENDING, never as green, which is the distinction the old version lost and the one that matters when a required check is path-filtered and never runs.

TWO MORE THINGS FIXED WHILE IN THERE. GH_TOKEN is no longer demanded: gh is already authenticated in the shells this runs in and honours GH_TOKEN by itself, so requiring it only produced a failure mode where a usable session was refused. And exit codes are now distinct - 0 merged, 1 red or refused, 2 timed out, 3 bad usage - so a caller can branch on them instead of on 0-or-not.

A DEFECT IN MY OWN REWRITE, CAUGHT IN TESTING AND WORTH RECORDING. The first version had no state guard, and gh pr merge on an ALREADY-MERGED PR prints "was already merged" and EXITS 0 - so the script announced MERGED for a merge it had not performed. A false green in the tool whose only job is to tell green from not-green. Two guards now: it refuses any PR that is not OPEN, and after merging it RE-READS the PR state rather than trusting the exit code of the call that was supposed to change it. Same doctrine as verifying a migration against the database instead of trusting "applied successfully!".

.claude/commands/ship.md updated to match: no GH_TOKEN step, and the exit-code table documented.

cards.title: The session cookie is host-scoped to the API and the portal has no way to carry it

evidence.ref: #826 merged 2026-08-06 (2c0c708) - the mint routes return the session token in the RESPONSE BODY and the portal server writes its own first-party cookie via writePortalSession. Tests prove the body token and the cookie token are the same credential, the device token is absent from the body, and neither mint route redirects or builds a query string (constraint 3, no token in a URL).

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-06 WHILE STARTING THE LOGIN SCREENS. HALT, not improvised. The ruling settled WHAT the session is; it did not settle HOW the portal carries it, and the portal existing architecture has no slot for it.

THE MISMATCH, re-derived from committed code:
1. The API sets __Host-ojp_session. The __Host- prefix means HOST-ONLY, no Domain attribute - the browser scopes it to api.osteojp.pt and nothing else. That prefix is load-bearing and I would not drop it.
2. apps/portal/lib/api/client.ts:96-110 calls the API SERVER-TO-SERVER with an Authorization: Bearer header built from the portal own Supabase session. Its comment says it deliberately avoids forwarding cookies at all: "the fragility of manually forwarding the Cookie header string (encoding edge cases, SameSite restrictions, cookie-path scoping)".
3. There is NO credentialed browser-to-API call anywhere in the portal: a search for credentials: across apps/portal returns zero hits, and no client component reads NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL. Every API call is made by the portal SERVER.
4. An OTP patient has no Supabase session, so the Bearer the portal knows how to build does not exist for them.

CONSEQUENCE: the portal server cannot read a cookie scoped to another host, and the browser never calls the API directly. The session works - it is minted, signed, verified and tested - and nothing in the portal can present it.

OPTIONS, with what each costs:
(a) BROWSER CALLS THE API DIRECTLY for patient routes, credentials: include. Cost: the API needs CORS with Allow-Credentials and a pinned origin, which it has today for nothing; and the portal gains a second, different call pattern beside the server-side one.
(b) PORTAL OWNS THE COOKIE, API ONLY SIGNS AND VERIFIES. The API verify/trusted return the session token in the RESPONSE BODY; the portal server-side login action calls them, sets its OWN __Host- cookie on the PORTAL host, and forwards the token as Authorization: Bearer on every later call - the pattern that already exists. The API Bearer path tries verifyPatientSession before the Supabase verifier. Cost: the token appears in a response body. That is smaller than it looks: the only caller is the portal SERVER, so an XSS on the portal origin still cannot see that response, and a patient calling verify directly with their own code receives their own credential, which is not a leak.
(c) SHARE THE COOKIE ACROSS SUBDOMAINS with Domain=.osteojp.pt. Cost: drops the __Host- prefix and broadcasts a patient credential to every subdomain in the estate including the staff platform. NOT RECOMMENDED, listed so nobody proposes it later believing it was missed.

RECOMMENDED: (b). It keeps the __Host- prefix, keeps the secret in the osteojp-api project alone (the portal relays, never verifies), reuses the portal existing Bearer path so no new call pattern appears, and needs no CORS surface. It is also the only option that leaves the XSS argument intact where it matters.

NOTHING IS BUILT ON THIS UNTIL IT IS RULED. The session module, both routes, the cookie helpers and the principal path are merged and correct under every option; only the transport differs.

=== RULED 2026-08-06: OPTION B. Portal owns the cookie, API only signs and verifies. UNBLOCKED. ===

CONSTRAINTS AS RULED, all three load-bearing:
1. THE PORTAL TREATS THE TOKEN AS OPAQUE. It wraps it in its own __Host- cookie on the portal host and forwards it as Bearer. It NEVER parses, decodes or trusts the contents locally. The API remains the single verifier, forever. Asserted by a test in the WF-08 style: no JWT decode or verify symbol is reachable in the portal against this token.
2. PORTAL COOKIE: __Host- prefix, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, path scoping per the prefix rules. Lifetimes MIRROR the ruled artefact - 12h session, 30-day trusted device, device-refresh semantics unchanged from #825.
3. THE TOKEN TRAVELS ONLY IN THE BODY of the server-to-server response. Never in a redirect URL, never in a query string. Both are logged by proxies, kept in browser history and leaked by Referer.

BUILT 2026-08-06. All three ruled constraints implemented and asserted.

API SIDE: verify and trusted now return sessionToken IN THE BODY alongside the cookie, for the portal SERVER. The Bearer path in getPatientPrincipal tries verifyPatientSession BEFORE the Supabase verifier - neither kind can be mistaken for the other, since ours is rejected by the Supabase verifier on signature and a Supabase token is rejected by ours on issuer, so trying both is not weaker than trying one.

PORTAL SIDE: apps/portal/lib/auth/session.ts owns __Host-ojp_session on the PORTAL host - httpOnly, secure, sameSite lax, path /, maxAge 12h mirroring the ruled artefact. apiHeaders() now prefers it over the Supabase session, because an OTP patient has no Supabase session at all.

CONSTRAINT 1 (OPACITY) IS ASSERTED BY A SOURCE SCAN, WF-08 style, in apps/portal/lib/auth/session-opacity.test.ts: no jwtVerify, decodeJwt, decodeProtectedHeader, SignJWT, jwt.verify, jwt.decode, jsonwebtoken or createRemoteJWKSet anywhere in the portal; the session module contains no base64 decode, no JWT split and no reference to exp/payload/claims; and the client forwards the token verbatim with no slicing. A behavioural test could only prove the paths someone remembered to call - the scan proves absence across the app. 11 assertions, green.

WHY OPACITY IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN TIDY: the signing secret lives in osteojp-api and nowhere else, so the portal COULD NOT verify honestly even if it tried. A portal that checked a token it cannot verify would be reading the attacker own claims and believing them - the exact defect behind SEC-W1-patient-jwt-verify, where apps/api decoded a token and trusted the payload.

CONSTRAINT 3 (NO URL) IS ALSO ASSERTED, replacing the now-obsolete no-token-in-body test: neither mint route may contain a redirect() call or build a query string. A body is bounded to the portal server; a URL is written to proxy logs, kept in browser history and leaked through Referer.

THE BODY TOKEN AND THE COOKIE TOKEN ARE PROVEN IDENTICAL by test - one credential carried two ways, not two live sessions per login. And the DEVICE token is proven absent from the body: it belongs to the browser, and the portal has no use for it.

CLOSED 2026-08-06. PR #826 merged at 2c0c708. This is what unblocks the W13-03 login screens: the portal now has a supported way to carry a session, so the screen after the code entry has somewhere to put it.

cards.title: PORTAL_TENANT_ID must be set on the portal project, or the login screens answer unavailable

evidence.ref: DEPLOYED-SCREEN CHECK by Ivan, 2026-08-06. PORTAL_TENANT_ID set on osteojp-portal only, all three environments, followed by a production redeploy. The login screen at portal.osteojp.pt renders the phone input, the pt-PT title and the send-code button, with NO unavailable message - which is the specific thing this card was open for: an unset variable makes the screen answer otp_unavailable and logs the variable name. Same evidence class WF-03 makes load-bearing.

cards.notes:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING W13-03's SCREENS, 2026-08-06. Not a defect - a variable that has never existed until now.

WHY IT IS NEEDED AT ALL, since the obvious question is why the portal does not just know. Both OTP routes take tenantId IN THE BODY because they run BEFORE any authentication: there is no verified token to derive a tenant from, and /otp/request deliberately never touches the patient table, which is the property that keeps it from leaking clinic membership. The alternatives were a host-to-tenant mapping table (a migration, and the one in-flight slot belongs to LOOP 5) or an id hard-coded in source (forbidden, and wrong the first time this app is deployed for a second clinic).

OWNER ACTION, one line, same shape as PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET: set PORTAL_TENANT_ID on the osteojp-portal project only, all scopes. The VALUE is the production tenant's uuid, which this terminal has never seen and must not - it is read from the production tenants table by the owner.

UNTIL IT IS SET, the behaviour is loud and correct rather than broken-looking: the screen says the service is unavailable (otp_unavailable), the server logs a line naming the VARIABLE and never a value, and no patient sees a 401 they would read as their own mistake. The assertion is at HANDLER scope, never module scope - a module-scope throw fails `next build` on every PR, which is the defect W13-03a had to unpick on the API side.

E2E is unaffected: playwright.config.ts supplies the seeded test tenant to the portal dev server.

The absence of the unavailable message is the proof, not the presence of the form: an unset PORTAL_TENANT_ID fails at handler scope and answers otp_unavailable, so a rendering phone screen means the tenant resolved.

WHAT THIS SCREENSHOT DOES NOT CLOSE, kept separate on purpose: it is ALSO the first WF-03 evidence for the W13-03 login gate, but that gate flips in the batch at the acceptance session, not here. This card is about a variable being set. PG1 is about a patient logging in, and OTP_LIVE_SEND is still off.
