cards.title: Signing out drops the device COOKIE but cannot revoke the device ROW - there is no endpoint

evidence.ref:
pr:#843 MERGED 2026-08-07, merge commit 45f05c4, verified ancestor of origin/main. #843 OPEN. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/revoke, authenticated by the DEVICE COOKIE itself so it needs no patient id, wired into the portal signOutAction BEFORE clearDeviceToken (reversing that order would silently restore the cookie-only sign-out this fixes). 8 DB-gated assertions in apps/api/lib/auth/otp-revoke.db.test.ts including the card's DoD verbatim - a revoked row is refused by /otp/trusted - plus a negative control that the device was live first, re-revoke not moving the timestamp, and that only the PRESENTED device is revoked. The store's revoke() already existed since 0056 and had no caller.

STALE-REF CORRECTION 2026-08-11: this card recorded "#843 OPEN". gh pr view #843 returns state MERGED at 2026-08-07T15:45:38Z, merge commit 45f05c4, and git merge-base --is-ancestor 45f05c4 origin/main exits 0. The work is on main. Corrected during the PURPLE gate reconciliation; the board, not the work, was wrong.

cards.notes:
FOUND IN W13-03, 2026-08-06, while making sign-out actually sign a patient out.

WHAT IS TRUE NOW: signOutAction clears the portal session cookie AND the trusted-device cookie, so the token is gone from that browser and unrecoverable - that browser can never present it again. The bound is real and it is what a patient on a shared handset needs.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE: the ROW in patient_trusted_devices survives its full 30 days with revoked_at still null. The schema was built for revocation (the column exists, and its comment says 'revoked on the 4th stays an answerable question') but nothing writes it, because there is no API route to write it and the portal must not touch the database directly.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: the token only exists in one browser, so a dropped cookie is effectively a revocation for every practical case. The gap is the case where the value was captured before sign-out - a shoulder-surfed device cookie is not a realistic attack, but 'we cannot revoke' is the wrong answer to have when someone reports a lost phone.

DoD: a POST route on apps/api that revokes the CALLER's device row (authenticated by the device cookie itself, so it needs no patient id), called by signOutAction, plus a test that a revoked row is refused by /otp/trusted.

=== BUILT 2026-08-07, PR #843. ===

THE STORE ALREADY HAD revoke(). It has existed since 0056 with a comment saying
"revoked on the 4th stays an answerable question", and its ONLY callers were
tests. The gap was the route and the wiring, exactly as the card said.

THREE DESIGN POINTS, each a deliberate refusal of something simpler:
  NO BODY AND NO PATIENT ID. The device cookie IS the authentication - whoever
  holds it may revoke it, and holding it is the only thing that could authorise
  revoking it. A patient id would be a caller-supplied value needing
  reconciliation against the device row, and the two can disagree. Same argument
  that kept the phone number out of /otp/trusted.
  ALWAYS 204, for an unknown, expired, already-revoked or absent token. The
  honest outcome is identical, and distinguishing them would make this an ORACLE
  for whether a given device token is live - the enumeration surface /otp/trusted
  was built not to be. A 401 for a missing cookie would also make sign-out noisy
  for a patient who never trusted the browser.
  NO PATIENT_SESSION_SECRET ASSERTION. The route mints nothing, so that variable
  is irrelevant to it. Asserting it would make a REVOCATION fail on a
  misconfiguration that cannot affect the revocation - the wrong direction for a
  security control.

ORDER IN signOutAction IS LOAD-BEARING and commented as such: the revoke needs
the token, so it runs BEFORE clearDeviceToken. A tidy-looking reorder would turn
this back into a cookie-only sign-out.

BEST-EFFORT BY CHOICE. If the API is unreachable the cookies still clear and the
patient IS signed out of this browser. Failing the sign-out because a revocation
could not be recorded would leave them signed IN, which is strictly worse.

cards.title: nif-required.spec.ts flakes under load - second occurrence, now with a controlled comparison

evidence.ref:
pr:#843 MERGED 2026-08-07, merge commit 45f05c4, verified ancestor of origin/main. #843 OPEN. CAPTURE, NOT FIX, honouring the card's own instruction. gotoPatientEdit() in apps/web/e2e/helpers/index.ts navigates to the edit route and, on a 404, immediately GETs /patients/{id} on the same origin, session and database. detail 200 means THE ROW EXISTS and the EDIT ROUTE is at fault; detail 404 means the row is not visible and it is a data problem. The verdict is attached to the Playwright report and thrown, so the third occurrence arrives already diagnosed. No retry, no fix.

STALE-REF CORRECTION 2026-08-11: this card recorded "#843 OPEN". gh pr view #843 returns state MERGED at 2026-08-07T15:45:38Z, merge commit 45f05c4, and git merge-base --is-ancestor 45f05c4 origin/main exits 0. The work is on main. Corrected during the PURPLE gate reconciliation; the board, not the work, was wrong.

cards.notes:
OBSERVED 2026-08-06 on run 31105176063, shard 2 of #829: 'an existing NIF cannot be edited back to empty' timed out at 120s, three times counting both retries. Recorded because it is the kind of thing that gets written off as flake and then costs an afternoon later.

WHAT THE ARTIFACT SHOWED, and it is not what the summary suggested. The click did not time out on a slow element: the PAGE WAS A 404. The snapshot is Next's own 'This page could not be found', so getByLabel(/^NIF/i) was waiting for a field that was never going to exist.

WHY THAT IS ODD RATHER THAN ORDINARY: createPatient asserts the URL becomes /patients/{uuid} within 15s BEFORE it returns, and that assertion passed. So a patient WAS created, a real uuid came back, and the app was demonstrably working at that instant - and then the edit route for that same uuid answered 404.

WHAT RULES OUT THE BRANCH: apps/web application code is identical across the failing run and both parent runs. W13-03 touched only e2e harness files in that app and the merge changed nothing under apps/web/app; W13-04 is apps/api, which the staff platform does not import. The same test passed in 6.0s and 6.4s on the two parents and in 4.8s on a re-run of the identical commit.

WHAT IS LEFT: a Next DEV-SERVER 404 (the snapshot carries the Dev Tools button) with hydration errors in the same window, on a runner hosting three Next servers plus Supabase. Plausible, and NOT PROVEN - a single green re-run never proves the absence of a race, which is why this is a card and not a conclusion.

IF IT RECURS: do not re-run. Capture whether the patient row exists in the database at the moment of the 404, which separates 'the row is not there' from 'the route did not compile'. Those have different fixes and guessing between them is how the last four CI causes were called wrong.

=== SECOND OCCURRENCE 2026-08-07, and this time the code path was PROVEN unchanged rather than assumed. ===

SYMPTOM, different from the first: nif-required.spec.ts:129 timed out clicking getByLabel(/^NIF/i), 120s, on all three Playwright retries. The first occurrence was a 404 on /patients/[id]/edit. Same spec, same under-load character, different surface.

THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON, which is what makes this a flake claim rather than a guess. Shard 2 PASSED at a4de096 and FAILED 3/3 at 0df8668 on the same PR. git diff between those two commits touches exactly three files: 0058_patient_terms_acceptances.sql in both mirrored trees, and patient-terms-acceptances-rls.test.ts. Filtering the SQL diff to non-comment lines returns NOTHING - the change was comment-only. No app code, no seed, no e2e spec.
So the spec ran identical application code against identical fixture data, and flipped. That is a flake with evidence behind it.

LOAD IS THE COMMON FACTOR IN BOTH OCCURRENCES. Shard 2 took 13m10s on the failing run against roughly 7m for shards 1 and 3 - the three 120s timeouts plus retries account for most of it, but it was the slow shard before the retries began. The first occurrence was also recorded as happening under load.

A HYDRATION MISMATCH FIRES IN THE SAME WINDOW, three times, seconds before each timeout. It is LE-notes-list-hydration-mismatch (notes-list.tsx:139, toLocaleString server vs client) on the patient profile page. NOT CLAIMED AS THE CAUSE - the two are correlated in the log and nothing more, and this project has paid for causal claims made on correlation. But a hydration failure can leave a client tree unattached, and a form field that never becomes interactive is exactly this symptom, so it is the first hypothesis to test if there is a third occurrence.

ACTION TAKEN: job re-run, which is legitimate here only BECAUSE the diff proved the code path unchanged. Re-running to make a red go away without that proof is how a real defect gets buried.

=== DIAGNOSTIC CAPTURED, 2026-08-07, PR #843. NOT FIXED, BY INSTRUCTION. ===

The card says: do not re-run, capture whether the patient row exists at the
moment of the 404, because "the row is not there" and "the route did not
compile" have different fixes and guessing between them is how the last four CI
causes were called wrong. That is what shipped.

THE HARNESS CANNOT QUERY POSTGRES AND DOES NOT NEED TO. The DETAIL route
/patients/{id} reads the same row from the same database as the edit route. At
the instant of the 404:
  detail 200 -> THE ROW EXISTS, so the EDIT ROUTE is the problem (dev-server
  compile or chunk serving, which the Dev Tools button in the first artefact
  already hinted at);
  detail 404 -> THE ROW IS NOT VISIBLE, so it is a data or transaction problem.

The verdict, both statuses and the patient id are ATTACHED to the Playwright
report and thrown, so it survives the runner and is readable from the artefact
without re-deriving anything. A pass is silent. There is NO retry and NO fix.

cards.title: JP ruled: an unconfirmed pedido does NOT hold the slot (option B)

evidence.ref: JP ruling 2026-08-06, verbatim choice: "o horario fica livre ate a rececao confirmar". Option B, over the recommended default and over the behaviour as built. He accepted the stated trade-off: reception's confirm can fail when another booking takes the slot first. Recorded in the dispatch of 2026-08-06 and carried into code as the mandatory transactional re-check in confirmAppointmentRequest (apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts) and the patient-facing copy change in packages/i18n/src/portal/strings.pt.json. The QUESTION is closed; the availability half it created is carded separately as W13-04a-availability-exclusion.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-06 while designing the reception confirm surface. NOT A BLOCKER for that surface, which is correct under either answer, and carded so it is ruled rather than absorbed.

WHAT HAPPENS TODAY. A portal booking calls bookAppointment, which picks a conflict-free therapist and WRITES THE APPOINTMENT immediately, status=scheduled. The patient is told it awaits confirmation, reception is notified, and the appointment already occupies that therapist's calendar. Nothing is auto-CONFIRMED, so JP's ruling as recorded ('zero auto-confirmed') IS satisfied - the lifecycle stays scheduled until reception acts.

THE QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS: should an unconfirmed pedido OCCUPY THE SLOT while it waits?
  HOLDING IT (today) means two patients cannot request the same slot, and reception's confirm is a formality that never fails. The cost is that a pedido reception never gets to blocks the calendar, and a patient who requests and is refused has still denied that slot to everyone meanwhile.
  NOT HOLDING IT means a pedido is a request against an open calendar, several patients may request the same slot, and reception's confirm can FAIL on a conflict - which needs its own refusal path and its own pt-PT copy.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT IF NO ANSWER ARRIVES: keep holding it. It is what is built, it cannot double-book, and the failure mode it creates (a stale pedido blocking a slot) is visible to reception in the queue and fixable by cancelling. The alternative introduces a conflict path on the confirm action, which is new failure surface at launch. A STARTING POINT FOR JP, NOT A RULING.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: at launch every bookable service is request-mode and the clinic is small, so a stale pedido is a phone call, not an outage.

=== RULED 2026-08-06. OPTION B. THE QUESTION IS CLOSED. ===

JP chose NOT HOLDING IT, against the recommended default recorded above. His words: "o horario fica livre ate a rececao confirmar". He was told the cost and took it: a confirm can fail on a conflict, and that needs its own refusal path and its own pt-PT copy.

WHAT THAT MAKES BINDING, in the order it has to be built:
  1. Availability, staff AND portal, must exclude an unconfirmed pedido. NOT BUILT - it needs a migration and the slot is LOOP 5's. See W13-04a-availability-exclusion.
  2. The confirm action re-checks availability in the same transaction as the status write. BUILT.
  3. Patient copy must not promise the slot. BUILT.
  4. Both therapists of a dual-therapist service are covered by the exclusion, per R2. FOLLOWS FROM 1, so it is unbuilt with it.

THE CARD IS CLOSED AS A QUESTION, NOT AS WORK. Closing it while item 1 is unbuilt is deliberate: the thing this card asked for was a RULING, and the ruling exists. Leaving it open would hide the build behind a question that is no longer being asked.

cards.title: Option B availability exclusion - the FINAL migration, sequenced after LOOP 5

evidence.ref: MIGRATION 0059 APPLIED AND PROVEN 2026-08-07, owner-run, FIRST ATTEMPT. Evidence at docs/migration-apply-0059.md section 9. Pre-check: pending 1, PENDING 0059_pedido_does_not_block_slot when=1786700000000 against last-applied 1786600000000, forward. Checker: is_unconfirmed_pedido EXISTS, appointment_conflicts EXISTS and its INSTALLED BODY contains the token (the 0052 body does not), 2 of 2 passed. #836 MERGED after the apply in the ruled order, squashed to be0e1d4. All three occupancy sites landed together. Next free migration number is 0060; nothing in the repo holds an unapplied migration. This was the wave's final planned migration.

cards.notes:
HALT, LOUD, 2026-08-06. The dispatch said to halt if the clean mechanism for JP's option B needs a schema change. It does. This card is that halt, and it is the ONLY thing on W13-04 that is stopped - everything else in the ruling was built and merged in the same session.

WHAT OPTION B REQUIRES: whatever availability computation staff booking and portal booking read must exclude an unconfirmed pedido. RECON, READ-ONLY, WITH FILE EVIDENCE. There are exactly THREE places that answer "is this slot occupied", and they were found by grepping the occupancy predicate rather than trusted from a note:
  1. apps/api/lib/appointments/store.ts:150 apptOverlapExists. ONE fragment, feeding listOpenSlots (the patient slot sweep), listAvailableTherapists, the createBooking guard and hasWindowConflict. APP LAYER, no migration.
  2. apps/web/lib/scheduling/day-availability.ts:51 NON_BLOCKING. The staff free-interval display, shared by the new-appointment panel, the batch engine and multi-therapist conflict reporting. APP LAYER, no migration.
  3. public.appointment_conflicts(), defined in packages/db/migrations/0052_conflicts_no_show_releases_slot.sql:49. The staff HARD BLOCK on save, reached through apps/web/lib/scheduling/conflict.ts findConflicts. A SECURITY DEFINER SQL FUNCTION. Changing it is a migration.

WHY THERE IS NO APP-LAYER ESCAPE FROM (3), and both alternatives were checked rather than dismissed:
  POST-FILTER THE FUNCTION'S OUTPUT in apps/web/lib/scheduling/conflict.ts. It would need to ask, per returned id, "is this an unconfirmed pedido", and the only provenance is a staff_notifications row whose SELECT policy (0055) is pinned to recipient_user_id = auth.uid(). A caller who is not a recipient - an admin, a therapist who is not on the appointment - would classify every pedido as a normal booking. The pedido would then block THEM and not reception, inconsistently and invisibly. apps/web/lib/scheduling/data.ts:34 also forbids getDbAdmin in this module by name, so there is no sanctioned way to read past RLS here.
  USE created_by IS NULL as the portal marker. Refused on evidence: packages/db/tests/appointments-created-by-provenance.test.ts proves 7/7 against live Postgres that 0049's WITH CHECK is a DISJUNCTION, so a staff principal satisfying another branch may insert a null created_by and the database accepts it. Keying the exclusion on it would put staff rows into the does-not-block set, which is a double-booking generator.
  MOVE THE PEDIDO OUT OF appointments until confirmed. Also a migration, and a bigger one: staff_notifications.appointment_id is NOT NULL with an FK, and the row carries no service, location or practitioner, so a pedido could not be stored at all without new columns or a new table. It would also undo what #829 shipped.

THE OWNER DECISION, and it is his because the rule is his: a SECOND migration in flight repo-wide, or LOOP 5 waits. One migration in flight is not a lane rule, it is a repo rule, and the slot belongs to LOOP 5 (terms acceptance). Two options, and a recommendation:
  A. AUTHORISE THE SECOND SLOT. W13-04 finishes to the ruling now. Cost: two unapplied migrations at once, which is the exact condition that double-booked migration number 0053 twice before.
  B. LOOP 5 FIRST, THEN THIS. No rule is bent. Cost: W13-04 stays in flight longer, and until it lands the product behaves as option A of the question JP already answered - the pedido keeps holding the slot.
  RECOMMENDED: B. Nothing is broken while it waits. The behaviour in production today is the SAFE side of the ruling: a pedido holds the slot, so no double booking is possible, and JP's "zero auto-confirmed" is still satisfied. What is missing is only the freedom he granted, not a protection he required. B also keeps the one-in-flight rule intact, and that rule exists because breaking it has cost this repo real time twice.

WHAT THE MIGRATION WOULD BE, so the estimate is not a guess. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.appointment_conflicts(...) with the 0052 body reproduced verbatim and ONE added clause per branch: exclude rows that are status = scheduled AND have a staff_notifications row of kind appointment_request for that appointment id. Signature unchanged, so no re-GRANT and nothing dependent breaks. No data read, written or backfilled. No table locked. Reversible by re-applying the 0052 body.

IT LANDS AS ONE PR WITH ALL THREE SITES, never staged. Sites 1 and 2 are app-layer and could ship today; they must not. Shipping half means the portal and the staff agenda disagree about which slots are free, which is precisely what PG8 (SYNC) exists to prove does not happen.

THE DRIFT GUARD MUST GROW WITH IT. apps/api/lib/appointments/blocking-status.test.ts reads the migration file and store.ts as TEXT and fails when their status sets disagree. A pedido exclusion is a FOURTH occupancy dimension that its regexes do not see, so the guard has to be extended in the same PR or the sites can drift again with CI green - which is the exact failure that test was written for.

TESTS THAT ARE WAITING ON THIS, from the ruling's own list. They are NOT written as failing tests: an unconfirmed pedido does not block staff booking the same slot; an unconfirmed pedido does not block another patient booking the same slot. Both are DB-gated by nature. The other three from that list are already green - confirm succeeds on a free slot, confirm fails clean on a taken slot with no write, and cancelled/declined pedidos never block (they leave via the status predicate that already exists).

A SEPARATE GAP FOUND WHILE BUILDING THIS, worth ruling on with the same decision. emitPatientChange is best-effort and never throws (apps/api/lib/notifications/patient-change.ts:138). If the notification write fails, the appointment exists with no appointment_request row: it is invisible in reception's queue AND, once this exclusion ships, it would block like a staff booking. The notification being the sole provenance record is what makes that failure silent. Not urgent - the emit is a local insert in the same process - but it is the one place where losing a row loses a pedido.

=== RULED 2026-08-06 BY STRATEGY. THE HALT IS RESOLVED AND THIS IS NO LONGER WAITING ON A PERSON. ===

THE RULING: LOOP 5 first, no second in-flight migration. The recommendation on this card was accepted as written.

SEQUENCE AMENDMENT, BINDING, and it changes a fact this board carried until now: LOOP 5 IS NO LONGER THE LAST MIGRATION. The order is LOOP 5, then THIS CARD as the FINAL migration of the wave. Each alone in flight. Each under the full post-0057 apply-block doctrine: a worktree path VERIFIED against the filesystem before the block is issued, a COMMITTED checker naming exactly what that migration created (tables -> check-migration-tables.mjs, columns -> check-migration-columns.mjs, never a one-off), and the evidence section written in the SAME TURN the output arrives.

THE AMENDED APPLY DOCTRINE BINDS THIS CARD.
docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md, section "The pre-check is mandatory": the apply

=== BUILT 2026-08-07, PR #836, ALL THREE SITES IN ONE PR. HELD FOR APPLY. ===

THE CARD'S RECON WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE THREE SITES AND INCOMPLETE ABOUT THE
MECHANISM. It proposed an inline NOT EXISTS in the SQL function with sites 1 and
2 as plain app edits. THAT WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED AT EITHER APP SITE:
apps/api store.ts runs under set local role patient, which has NO GRANT on

apps/web day-availability.ts runs as authenticated, where 0055 pins the policy to

public.is_unconfirmed_pedido(uuid), STABLE, tenant-scoped, granted to

THE DRIFT GUARD GREW to four sites and two axes, proven load-bearing by removing

A NEW COMMITTED CHECKER, because an existence check would be worthless here:

cards.title: drizzle-kit migrate prints success on a no-op - 0049 and 0058 are the same failure class

evidence.ref: CLOSED. #834 MERGED 2026-08-07, squashed to 4c60416. The doctrine amendment is on main: docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md section 'The pre-check is mandatory', the banner at the top of that file, three quick-reference rows, and docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-07. Both guards were already on main from #833 (45d0bcf): packages/db/scripts/check-pending-migrations.mjs and the strictly-increasing `when` assertion in scripts/check-journal.mjs. The 0058 evidence is at docs/migration-apply-0058.md section 8.

cards.notes:
THE PATTERN, which is why this is a card and not two unrelated entries in a log.
drizzle-kit migrate prints "migrations applied successfully" when it applies
NOTHING. The message answers "did the command run", never "did the schema
change". Twice now a migration has been reported applied when it had not run, and
BOTH times the checkout, the connection and the SQL file were fine, or looked it.

0049, 2026-07-30: the prod-apply worktree sat on main, because git checkout
<branch> is rejected in that worktree and the fallback went unnoticed. The
migration was not in the tree. Caught afterwards, by the owner asking for schema
evidence.

0058, 2026-08-07: the journal `when` for 0058 was LOWER than 0057's. Drizzle's
pending test is lastDbMigration.created_at < folderMillis
(drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:62), so a backwards timestamp reads as
already-applied and the entry is skipped. Caught afterwards, by
check-migration-tables.mjs.

WHY THE 0058 MECHANISM IS NOT A TYPO ANYONE WOULD SPOT. This repo's journal
`when` values are a SYNTHETIC series stepping +100000000, already years ahead of
wall-clock time. A hand-appended entry using a real Date.now() produces a value
BELOW its predecessor. 1786093200000 looks like a perfectly ordinary millisecond
timestamp, because it is one. It is just smaller than the line above it.

THE CHECK THAT WAS GREEN THE WHOLE TIME. check-journal.mjs asserted file count,
idx contiguity and filename order. All three reconciled while the migration was
unappliable. None of them looked at `when`. A green check on an adjacent property
reads exactly like a green check on the property you cared about, and that is the
transferable half of this incident.

THE RULE: a command's own success message is never evidence that its side effect
occurred. Verify the side effect from a different source, and in BOTH directions -
before, that the work is pending; after, that the object exists. The 0049 lesson
was recorded as "check the schema afterwards", and that half ALONE still cost a
full owner round-trip on 0058, because an after-check reports the failure once
the owner's terminal session is already over.

CLOSES when the doctrine amendment merges. The two guards are already on main.

UPDATE 2026-08-07: the doctrine amendment is on PR #834 (portal/W13-05-0058-evidence),
docs-only. This card closes when that merges. Both guards were already on main.

=== A THIRD OCCURRENCE OF THIS CLASS, CAUGHT BY CI, 2026-08-07. ===

Migration 0059 was drafted, synced to the supabase mirror, then REWRITTEN around a
SECURITY DEFINER helper - and never re-synced. CI's db-tests job applies the
MIRROR (supabase db reset), so the DB-gated suite ran against a superseded body
and failed with "function public.is_unconfirmed_pedido(uuid) does not exist".

SAME SHAPE, ONE FILE OVER. check-journal.mjs reported "59 .sql files match 59
journal entries in order" the whole time, and every word was TRUE. A rewritten
migration keeps its NAME, its NUMBER and its journal entry; only its BODY
changes, and nothing was looking at the body.

The partial failure is what made it confusing: the appointment_conflicts
assertions PASSED, because the stale mirror body did exclude pedidos inline,
while the three tests calling the helper directly failed. A suite that
half-passes reads like a flake rather than a stale artefact.

FIXED IN #836: check-journal.mjs now compares the mirror BY CONTENT, proven
against the real bug (restore the stale mirror, it fails and names the file;
re-sync, it passes). sync --check already existed and DID fire.

cards.title: A failed appointment_request emit loses the pedido - invisible in the queue, and it blocks
cards.notes:
FOUND while building W13-04a and carded rather than fixed inside it, because
fixing it is a change to the EMIT path and not to occupancy.

emitPatientChange is best-effort and never throws
(apps/api/lib/notifications/patient-change.ts:138). If the notification write
fails, the appointment row exists with NO appointment_request row. Two
consequences, and the second one arrives with migration 0059:

  1. It is invisible in reception's confirm queue, which is derived from that
     notification. Nobody is told to confirm it.
  2. Once 0059 is applied it also BLOCKS like a staff booking, because the
     notification row is the only provenance marker the exclusion can key on.

THE DIRECTION OF FAILURE IS THE SAFE ONE, which is why this is medium: it
OVER-blocks. No double booking becomes possible. What is lost is the patient's
request, silently.

WHY THE NOTIFICATION IS THE SOLE PROVENANCE, since the obvious fix is a column
instead: created_by IS NULL was refused on evidence -
packages/db/tests/appointments-created-by-provenance.test.ts proves 7/7 against
live Postgres that 0049's WITH CHECK is a DISJUNCTION, so a staff principal may
insert a null created_by and the database accepts it. A dedicated column would
work but is a migration, and the one-in-flight rule means it queues.

cards.title: Every SECURITY DEFINER function is owned by whoever ran migrate, and nothing pins or checks it

evidence.ref: MIGRATION 0060 APPLIED AND PROVEN 2026-08-07, owner-run, FIRST ATTEMPT, detached at 1ea8697. Evidence at docs/migration-apply-0060.md section 10. EXECUTION PROVEN BY THE PENDING COUNT MOVING 1 -> 0, which is the only line in the output that could: four of the six would have printed on a run that did nothing, because 0060 is a no-op. Ownership 13/13 postgres before AND after, identical, which is the second finding - a difference would have meant the migration was not a no-op and pinning was an unauthorised ownership MOVE. #844 merged after the apply in the ruled order. Next free number 0061; nothing holds an unapplied migration.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-07 answering a SECURITY DEFINER interrogation on the freshly applied
0059. The question asked for the owning role. THE ANSWER IS THAT NOTHING SAYS.

THE MECHANISM. Postgres gives a SECURITY DEFINER function the privileges of its
OWNER, and the owner is whoever ran the CREATE unless an explicit
ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO says otherwise. NO MIGRATION IN THIS REPO CONTAINS
ONE - verified by grep across all 59, zero hits for OWNER TO. So every such
function in production is owned by the principal in the env file used at apply
time.

THAT OWNERSHIP IS NOT INCIDENTAL. IT IS THE MECHANISM THE PLATFORM DEPENDS ON.
RLS on these tables is ENABLE, not FORCE, so a table's owner BYPASSES RLS BY
OWNERSHIP. Three load-bearing behaviours rest on it:
  jwt_tenant_id() / jwt_patient_id() are readable by the patient role, which has
  no grant on the auth schema;
  appointment_conflicts() reports a conflict a caller could not otherwise see
  past location RLS - a conflict must block even when the row is invisible to
  you;
  is_unconfirmed_pedido() answers for the patient role, which has NO GRANT AT
  ALL on staff_notifications.

TWELVE DISTINCT FUNCTIONS ACROSS NINE MIGRATIONS: assign_patient_number,
clinical_admin_sees_patient, clinical_therapist_sees_patient,
custom_access_token_hook, is_unconfirmed_pedido, jwt_patient_id, jwt_tenant_id,
location_in_viewer_scope, merge_patients, patient_appt_at_viewer_location,
patient_appt_treated_by_viewer, viewer_has_location_assignment. 37 occurrences
across 0002, 0005, 0010, 0012, 0045, 0047, 0048, 0052, 0059.

THE SILENT-FAILURE MODE, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS IS HIGH AND NOT LOW.
If the applying principal changes, every SECURITY DEFINER function created after
that point inherits a DIFFERENT owner. Functions created earlier keep the old
one, so the set silently splits in two. NOTHING DETECTS IT:
  drizzle-kit migrate succeeds - ownership is not its concern;
  check-migration-functions.mjs reports EXISTS and a live body, both TRUE;
  check-journal.mjs reconciles - counts and timestamps are unaffected;
  CI passes, and CI STRUCTURALLY CANNOT REPRODUCE IT: supabase db reset builds a
  fresh database where one principal creates everything, so the split cannot
  exist there.

The production symptom is a WRONG ANSWER, not an error: fewer rows, or false
where true is correct, because the new owner does not bypass the RLS the old one
did. For appointment_conflicts that means A CONFLICT IS NOT REPORTED, which is a
double booking.

Same shape as INC-07 and as the stale-mirror incident: every green check stays
green while the property that matters has changed.

WHY IT IS NOT REMEDIATED IN THIS TURN, and this is deliberate rather than
timid. Pinning ownership means naming a role, and NOBODY HAS READ THE CURRENT
OWNER FROM PRODUCTION. Authoring ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO <guess> would either
no-op or MOVE ownership away from the role the whole availability path depends
on - the failure this card exists to prevent, caused by the fix for it. No
migration is authored until the read comes back. NOTHING MAY OCCUPY MIGRATION
NUMBER 0060 until then.

WHAT IS NEEDED FROM IVAN: one READ-ONLY query, run in his own shell against
production, output pasted back. It reads pg_catalog only, touches no patient
table, and writes nothing:

  select p.proname,
         pg_get_userbyid(p.proowner) as owner,
         p.prosecdef as security_definer
  from pg_proc p
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
  where n.nspname = 'public' and p.prosecdef
  order by owner, p.proname;

WHAT THE ANSWER DECIDES. If all twelve share ONE owner, the exposure is latent
and the fix is a pin plus a CI assertion, authored against the real name. If they
DO NOT all share one owner, the split has ALREADY happened and this becomes an
incident with a live behavioural consequence to hunt.

WIRED AS A HARD DEPENDENCY of the pre-launch credential rotation:
docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md, section "SECURITY DEFINER ownership is UNPINNED,
and it is a rotation dependency". Rotating a PASSWORD is safe - same role, new
secret. Changing the ROLE is what triggers this, and a rotation that moves the
apply to a new service account would do exactly that.

=== THE READ RETURNED. THIRTEEN, NOT TWELVE. 2026-08-07. ===

MY GREP WAS WRONG AND PRODUCTION WAS RIGHT. I reported twelve functions;
production has THIRTEEN. THE MISSING ONE IS appointment_conflicts - the function
at the centre of the entire 0059 work, and the one whose wrong answer is a double
booking.

WHY IT WAS MISSED, measured rather than guessed: the grep read SIX lines of
context above each SECURITY DEFINER marker (grep -B6). appointment_conflicts has
a six-parameter list plus a RETURNS TABLE block, so its CREATE line sits
EIGHTEEN lines above its SECURITY DEFINER line. A FIXED-SIZE CONTEXT WINDOW IS
THE BUG. Two other definitions have gaps of 39 and 127 lines and were caught only
because they carry a second, closer marker - so the same grep was already lucky
twice.

A PINNING MIGRATION BUILT ON THE TWELVE-ITEM LIST WOULD HAVE LEFT THE MOST
IMPORTANT FUNCTION UNPINNED WHILE REPORTING SUCCESS. Same failure class as the
backwards journal timestamp and the superseded mirror: an artefact that
reconciles on everything except the property that matters.

A SECOND ERROR CAUGHT BEFORE THE APPLY, by checking each signature against its
CREATE rather than writing them from the name list: merge_patients takes THREE
uuid parameters (p_source_id, p_target_id, p_actor_id DEFAULT NULL), not two. A
two-argument ALTER would have failed mid-migration with "function does not
exist". A DEFAULT does not change a function's identity, so the argument list is
all three types.

THE CHECKER ASSERTS TWO THINGS, and the second is the one people forget. Owner is
obvious. COUNT is not: an owner-only check passes happily on a FOURTEENTH
function that arrived correctly owned, which is exactly how an unreviewed
SECURITY DEFINER function enters the schema. Both negative arms are proven -
a fabricated wrong owner fails with the function named, and a count of twelve
fails while every remaining owner is correct.

CI CAN ONLY CATCH HALF, and the workflow says so rather than implying otherwise:
supabase db reset builds a database where ONE principal creates everything, so an
owner SPLIT cannot exist there and CI cannot detect it. What CI DOES catch is the
count. The owner half is enforced where it is enforceable - against production,
by the same script, twice per apply block.

=== APPLY BLOCK CORRECTED 2026-08-07 BEFORE IT REACHED IVAN. ===

THE FIRST DRAFT COULD NOT PROVE THE MIGRATION RAN. It checked ownership before
and after, and the pre-check for pending 1 - but 0060 is a NO-OP, so its correct
end state is identical to its correct start state. Every state check would pass
whether migrate executed or not, and drizzle prints success on a no-op. The block
would have produced a receipt.

FIXED: check-pending-migrations.mjs 0 AFTER migrate. The pending count moving
from exactly 1 to exactly 0 is the ONLY thing in the block that proves execution,
because only a tracking row written into drizzle.__drizzle_migrations can move
it. The block now states which of its six outputs is the proof and which are not.

ALSO PINNED THE SHA, not the branch: git checkout --detach 1ea8697. A push to the
branch between validation and apply would otherwise silently change what runs.

=== APPLIED AND PROVEN 2026-08-07. THE CARD CLOSES. ===

The block was correct as validated and ran first time. Evidence at
docs/migration-apply-0060.md section 10.

WHAT THIS CARD LEAVES BEHIND, beyond the pin itself:
  ownership is now a REPO FACT (0060) rather than an accident of who ran migrate;
  check-security-definer-owner.mjs enforces owner AND count, in CI (count only -
  supabase db reset cannot reproduce an owner split, and db-tests.yml says so)
  and against production in every future apply block (both halves);
  docs/runbook-prod-migrations.md carries the rotation rule in one sentence:
  rotating the postgres password is safe, same role and new secret; introducing a
  separate migration role is what splits ownership, and that failure is silent.

AND THE APPLY-BLOCK DOCTRINE GAINED ITS LAST PIECE from this migration. 0060's
first draft could not prove a no-op had run. That produced the standing rule that
every apply block now starts NOT VALIDATED - STRATEGY REVIEW REQUIRED - DO NOT
RUN, written into the runbook and into PORTAL-REHYDRATE.md section 4 item 9 so it
survives a rehydrate.

cards.title: Portal pedidos reached a STUB consumer in production - invisible to reception AND blocking the slot

evidence.ref: #848 merged 2026-08-09, squashed to a4b45ce. Root cause proven from .next/server build output, not inferred: Turbopack emitted TWO copies of patient-change.ts. instrumentation.js reached chunks/..._patient-change_ts_*.js (1 setPatientChangeConsumer); the appointments route reached chunks/..._booking_ts_*.js with patient-change INLINED, 0 setPatientChangeConsumer and no reference to the other chunk. The booking copy had no setter compiled into it at all. Fix: emitPatientChange resolves ./centre itself per call via a literal dynamic import, so every copy reaches the real consumer without cross-bundle mutation; verified in the rebuilt booking chunk as `await t.A(36883)`. Guard consumer-default.test.ts PROVEN RED on 3dcfa1e: 5 failed / 5 passed including `expected '[notifications] patient-change NOT DE...' not to contain 'NOT DELIVERED (stub consumer'`. Gates lint 4/4, typecheck 10/10, test 422 passed, build 4/4. || OWNER-VERIFIED ON PRODUCTION 2026-08-11 (WF-03): after deploy, production SQL shows 16 staff_notifications rows written for two portal pedidos, kind appointment_request, real recipients. Before the fix: ZERO. The reception queue renders for a recipient account. The bundle-duplication diagnosis and the fix both hold on prod.

cards.notes:
PRODUCTION FACT, 2026-08-09. Two portal pedidos created against osteojp-api at 09:02:52 and 09:04:08 both logged "[notifications] patient-change NOT DELIVERED (stub consumer, centre not built yet)". A LEFT JOIN to staff_notifications returned null for both. A GET at 09:03:39 logged "consumer registered" BETWEEN them, which is what made the shape legible.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both owner-observed on production. (1) Neither pedido appeared in reception's queue at /notificacoes. (2) A staff Nova marcacao for the same therapist at the same time was REFUSED with "Conflito de terapeuta", because migration 0059 keys is_unconfirmed_pedido on a staff_notifications row with kind appointment_request and there was none. JP's PEDIDO SLOT option-B ruling was silently INVERTED in production. 0059 is correct; it cannot see a pedido that left no trace.

NOT A COLD-START RACE, and that mattered: the obvious reading was that the POST beat instrumentation. It did not. The 09:04:08 POST hit the stub a full minute AFTER registration succeeded, because registration mutated a module copy the booking path does not share.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT, which is the part worth keeping. Every suite that emitted called setPatientChangeConsumer first, so every suite tested a REGISTERED module. Nothing tested an UNREGISTERED one - and that was the only state production was ever in on that path. The new guard emits from a fresh module copy with no registration call, which is the defect's actual shape.

DOCTRINE THIS ADDS: a module-level singleton mutated from a boot hook is not wiring, it is a hope about bundling. If correctness depends on a swap, the thing that needs the value must be able to resolve it ITSELF.

CLOSED ON OWNER EVIDENCE 2026-08-11. Ivan re-ran the path against production: 16 rows for two pedidos where there had been none, kind appointment_request, real recipients, queue rendering. That is the deployed-screen half WF-03 requires and it is what closes this, not the green CI.

cards.title: Portal booking: preselect the patient's home clinic, keep a discreet switch for the other
cards.notes:
OWNER REQUEST, 2026-08-09. CARDED, NOT BUILT.

Today the patient picks a location with no default. Most patients only ever attend one clinic, so the first step of every booking is a choice they do not have.

SHAPE: preselect the patient's home clinic and keep switching possible but quiet - a link or a small control, not a required step.

THE DATA ALREADY EXISTS: patients.primary_location_id (migration 0043, R16), which the staff patient profile already renders as the identity line (app/patients/[id]/page.tsx:104-105). This is a default, not a restriction.

cards.title: Portal booking: a therapist step after service, with an explicit 'escolha por mim'
cards.notes:
OWNER REQUEST agreed with Rodica, 2026-08-09. CARDED, NOT BUILT.

Today the patient CANNOT choose a therapist and is never told so. The API assigns one server-side from whoever has covering hours (apps/api/lib/appointments/store.ts:462-479), tie-broken by lowest full name (therapist.ts:27-47). A returning patient has no way to ask for the person who treated them.

SHAPE: a step after service. List the therapists who can take the slot, plus an explicit "escolha por mim" option that keeps today's behaviour. Slots then filter to the chosen therapist.

THIS IS A FILTER AND A STEP, NOT NEW AVAILABILITY LOGIC - stated because it would be easy to over-build. Availability is already real and already per-therapist: listOpenSlots generates from availability templates (booking.ts:288-317) and listAvailableTherapists already answers "who can take this window". The work is to surface the second, narrow the first by it, and keep the auto path as a first-class choice rather than a fallback.

NOTE FOR THE BUILD: chooseTherapist already prefers the patient's PRIOR therapist when available (therapist.ts:33-37). "Escolha por mim" must keep that, or returning patients get a WORSE result than today.

cards.title: Pre-launch sweep: every patient with a non-null auth_user_id is silently locked out of the portal
cards.notes:
FOUND ON PRODUCTION 2026-08-09. CARDED, NOT BUILT. LAUNCH-RELEVANT.

Patient row 76a7d76d carried auth_user_id = 07ccbf22, an auth.users row created 2026-07-29 with no matching public.users row. OTP login for that patient was REFUSED, because resolvePatientByProvenPhone requires isNull(patients.authUserId) (patient-linkage.ts:73). Cleared by hand on the test patient; nobody has looked at the rest.

EVERY SUCH ROW IS A PATIENT WHO CANNOT LOG IN, and who gets the same generic refusal as a wrong code - so it is indistinguishable from a typo, by design, and will be reported as "the portal does not work".

WHAT THE MIGRATIONS SHOW, walked rather than assumed: the column is pre-Decision-D. 0010 defines a patient as "a Supabase auth user linked to ONE patients row via patients.auth_user_id" and the access-token hook resolves that link (0010:203-220). Decision D retired the model in the APP but nothing dropped it from the DATABASE. No current code path WRITES the column - the only write in the repo is the e2e seed (seed-e2e.mjs:616), and otp-claim.db.test.ts:365-372 asserts the claim path leaves it null.

SO THE ROWS ARE HISTORICAL and cannot be re-created by anything running today.

SCOPE: an owner-run read-only count first (PURPLE authors, Ivan runs, output pasted back), then a decision on clearing. NOT a migration - this is data, and a blanket UPDATE over a clinical table is owner-confirmable. The one live read that would change behaviour is the token hook's patient branch (0010:209), which only matters for a Supabase patient JWT the portal does not use.

OWNER RAN THE COUNT, 2026-08-11: ZERO rows. Only the one test patient was ever affected and it was cleared by hand on 2026-08-09. Dropped high -> low: the class is real and the column is still live, so the card stays as the record of a trap that can only be re-created by hand, but there is nothing to sweep.

cards.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-11 BY JP RULING: NO CAP.

THE RULING. Multiple unconfirmed pedidos may stack on one therapist slot without limit. Reception resolves the contention at confirm time. No code change, no migration, 0061 stays free.

WHAT IT CONFIRMS. The committed behaviour was already correct. Migration 0059's header says verbatim (0059:4-9): 'Staff may book over it AND ANOTHER PATIENT MAY BOOK IT, until reception actually confirms.' What had never been decided was the unconfirmed-versus-unconfirmed case. It is now decided in favour of the existing behaviour.

NOT A DATA-INTEGRITY RISK, and this is why 'no cap' is safe rather than merely cheap. confirmAppointmentRequest takes slot locks, re-checks in-transaction, and the second confirm finds the first 'confirmed', which has always blocked (0059:96-102). Nobody can double-book by confirming twice. The cost of the ruling is reception workload and patient experience, not integrity.

DOWNSTREAM, and a future session needs this: the REMINDER path must now assume several unconfirmed pedidos can exist on one slot at reminder time. Carried into the LOOP 6 reminder scoping rather than left implicit.

ORIGINAL FINDING PRESERVED. The exclusion is at THREE sites and the middle one produced D1: store.ts:165 (portal booking guard), 0059:192 (staff path), day-availability.ts:113 (agenda read).

cards.title: Duplicate pedido rows in the queue - the stated premise is DISPROVED by the code; needs one owner-run read
cards.notes:
REPORTED: one pedido produced SEVEN staff_notifications rows of kind appointment_request, with Raquel Monteiro, Tamara Tabarra and Carlos Barrelas each receiving TWO.

HALTED RATHER THAN BUILT, because the code disproves the stated mechanism and building a dedupe on a wrong premise would hide the real cause.

WHAT THE CODE PROVES. resolveRecipients ALREADY DEDUPES: it accumulates reception rows and practitioner rows into a Set<string> and returns [...set] (apps/api/lib/notifications/centre.ts, the recipients Set). The reception query cannot fan out either - innerJoin on roles is one role per user. So ONE emit can produce AT MOST ONE ROW PER RECIPIENT. Duplicates within a single appointment_id cannot come from a single emit, and cannot come from a missing dedupe, because the dedupe is there.

SO EITHER THE EMIT FIRED TWICE, OR THE SEVEN IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE.

The second reading is very plausible and must be excluded FIRST. 16 rows for TWO pedidos is 8 each. If the tenant has 7 reception-role users plus 1 practitioner, 8 rows per pedido is CORRECT FAN-OUT, and "Raquel, Tamara and Carlos each received two" is each of them receiving ONE ROW PER PEDIDO - which is right, not a bug. Counting across both pedidos would look exactly like duplication.

IF IT IS A REAL DOUBLE EMIT, the dedupe index cannot stop it: 0055's unique index is (recipient_user_id, appointment_id, kind, occurred_at) and occurred_at comes from a per-request a per-request Date, so two emits carry different instants and both persist. One candidate worth checking then: the portal confirm button has loading={pending} but NO disabled prop (BookingFlow.tsx:327), unlike the step-3 button at :276 which does carry disabled.

WHAT IS NEEDED: one read-only query from Ivan, grouping by appointment_id and recipient_user_id. If every (appointment, recipient) count is 1 there is NO duplication and the finding becomes "why are Raquel, Tamara and Carlos reception-role", which is a data question. If any count is 2 it is a genuine double emit and the button guard is the first suspect.

=== ROOT-CAUSE READ 2026-08-11, PURPLE, CODE ONLY, NO PROD TOUCH ===

ALL THREE PROPOSED MECHANISMS ARE REFUTED, and the refutation is structural rather than probabilistic.

THE DEDUPE KEY IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. 0055:145-147 is UNIQUE(recipient_user_id, appointment_id, kind, occurred_at) and centre.ts:145 writes through onConflictDoNothing(). occurred_at is NOT a per-write clock: it is e.occurredAt, carried on the event, stamped once by the caller at booking.ts:411 as now.toISOString() where now is a parameter of bookAppointment (booking.ts:339). So TWO ROWS FOR ONE (recipient, appointment, kind) REQUIRE TWO DISTINCT occurredAt VALUES, which requires two separate executions of bookAppointment carrying two different now.

(1) DOUBLE POST FROM THE CONFIRM STEP - REFUTED TWICE OVER. confirmAppointmentRequest (apps/web/lib/scheduling/actions.ts:1021) does NOT emit at all; the staff app never calls emitPatientChange, it only READS staff_notifications and inner-joins on kind=appointment_request (actions.ts:1052-55). No confirm can write a notification row. Separately, a double POST to the portal BOOKING route would run store.createBooking twice and mint TWO appointment ids, so it cannot produce eight rows on ONE id.

(2) INNGEST AT-LEAST-ONCE REPLAY - REFUTED. emitPatientChange (patient-change.ts:204-215) is a plain inline await in the request, post-commit. No step wrapper, no queue, no retry. INC-06 corroborates: the stub logged at request time.

(3) TURBOPACK DOUBLE MODULE COPY - REFUTED BY THE DEDUPE, and this is the subtle one worth keeping. Even if two copies of the module each resolved a consumer and both ran, both receive THE SAME event object and therefore the SAME e.occurredAt. The unique index collapses the second write to zero rows. Module duplication yields ONE row, not two. It was the INC-06 mechanism because that was a NOT-DELIVERED bug; it cannot be a DOUBLE-delivered bug.

SO THE WHOLE-WRITE-TWICE HYPOTHESIS IS STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE ON THE CREATE PATH, and the most likely reading is that these are NOT DUPLICATES AT ALL - the same misreading D3 was already halted on once.

THE LIKELY BENIGN EXPLANATION: two rows per (recipient, appointment) pair with DIFFERENT kind. There are four kinds (patient-change.ts:46-49): booked, cancelled, rescheduled, appointment_request. The only emit sites in the codebase are the three PATIENT paths in booking.ts - create :403, cancel :441, reschedule :548. So an appointment the patient created AND then cancelled or rescheduled through the portal legitimately carries TWO rows per recipient, and that is correct behaviour, not duplication. Appointment 1863b4f5 having 2 per pair while 1b5979db and 37e049b5 have 1 per pair fits exactly: one of the three was acted on afterwards, the other two were not.

THE DISPATCHED SQL WAS INSUFFICIENT AND WAS WIDENED. A block returning only created_at CANNOT distinguish these hypotheses, because both produce rows at different instants. kind and occurred_at are the discriminating columns and the corrected block selects them. If the 8 rows show TWO DISTINCT kinds, D3 closes as not-a-defect. If they show ONE kind with two occurred_at values, there is a real double execution and the next question is the route layer, not the notification layer.

cards.title: Portal: 48h/24h reminder the patient confirms by interacting, status reflecting back to the platform
cards.notes:

cards.title: Portal: multi-appointment booking with frequency, quantity and time - portal exposure of Agendar lote
cards.notes:
OWNER REQUEST 2026-08-11. CARDED, NOT BUILT.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS ON STAFF. Agendar lote is live in the appointment drawer with recurrence expansion (expandRecurrence, lib/scheduling/actions.ts), per-occurrence conflict collection (collectConflicts loops the windows), and a batch failure dialog for partial success. This is PORTAL EXPOSURE of that, not a new engine - which is the single most important thing for whoever picks it up, because building a second recurrence implementation is the drift shape 0059's header warns about.

WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW: showing availability and conflicts to a PATIENT across N occurrences. Staff get a conflict list and a Save-anyway; a patient must not get either. So the portal version has to resolve every occurrence to a free slot BEFORE offering, or offer partial success honestly ("4 of 6 times are available").

TWO THINGS TO CHECK BEFORE BUILDING, both of which change the shape:
  1. D1's outcome. If a pedido comes to hold a slot, a 6-session lote holds SIX, and an abandoned one holds six. That interacts badly and the sizing depends on JP's D1 ruling.
  2. The portal is request-mode: every booking is a pedido (PORTAL_BOOKINGS_ARE_REQUESTS, booking.ts:333). A lote is therefore N pedidos for reception to confirm, not one. Reception's workload per patient action multiplies by N, which is worth JP seeing before it ships.

cards.title: OTP request endpoint is an unauthenticated SMS pump when OTP_LIVE_SEND is armed - no patient lookup, no refusal branch, ~200M accepted inputs
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-11 BY CODE READ, NOT BY EXERCISING THE ENDPOINT. No prod touch, no request issued. VERDICT: EXPOSED.

THE FINDING. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request accepts any well-formed Portuguese number from any caller and, when OTP_LIVE_SEND is armed, dispatches a real Twilio SMS to it. There is NO patient lookup and therefore NO refusal branch for a number matching zero patients.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS, apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/route.ts:
  :36-41  rate limit per client key
  :43-54  parse body, require phone and tenantId
  :58-59  normalizePhonePT, 400 if malformed
  :64-69  rate limit per phone hash
  :71-74  requestCode - ISSUE AND SEND
  :77     204 always
The route states the absence itself at :20-22: 'AND IT NEVER LOOKS THE PHONE UP. There is no patient query on this path at all.'
apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts:245 is the send, unconditional. :216-220 states the intent: 'A code is issued for any well-formed number; an unknown number simply receives an SMS that helps nobody.'
apps/api/lib/auth/otp-transport.ts:171-172 - resolveOtpTransport returns the real Twilio adapter if and only if OTP_LIVE_SEND === 'true', else a sink. THE FLAG IS THE ENTIRE CONTROL.

BLAST RADIUS. PT_SUBSCRIBER at apps/api/lib/notify/phone.ts:19 is /^[29]\d{8}$/ - first digit 2 or 9 plus eight digits = 200,000,000 accepted inputs. RULES.otpRequest at apps/api/lib/rate-limit/limiter.ts:184 is {limit: 3, windowMs: 3600000}. The per-phone limit caps harassment of ONE handset at 3/hour and does NOT bound spend: an attacker rotating numbers never approaches it. The per-client limit keys on the first x-forwarded-for hop (limiter.ts:117-119), so a proxy pool yields 3 sends per IP per hour with no global ceiling. Route is public: apps/api/proxy.ts:5 confirms authorization is per-route via requirePatient, which this pre-auth route cannot and does not call.

THE MULTI-PATIENT QUESTION DOES NOT ARISE HERE. The exactly-one-row rule lives in resolvePatientByProvenPhone at CLAIM time (apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.test.ts:40). A number matching 0, 1 or 5 patients is treated identically at request: SMS sent. The refusal happens at verify, after the message has left.

THIS IS DELIBERATE DESIGN, NOT A BUG, and that is why it is an owner decision rather than a fix. The trade is documented at apps/api/lib/auth/otp.ts:7-13: a lookup-then-refuse endpoint would be a patient-list oracle for anyone with a phone book, and this clinic's patient list is itself sensitive. The engineering is sound. What is unsound is arming the flag on a public origin and leaving it.

OWNER ACTION REQUIRED: confirm whether OTP_LIVE_SEND is currently 'true' on osteojp-api Production, and disarm it if so. PURPLE performs no cloud writes and cannot read the value. Governed by docs/rulings/R9a-otp-live-send-not-separable.md.

DESIGN DIRECTION, SET BY STRATEGY 2026-08-11. NOT IMPLEMENTED THIS DISPATCH. The fix MUST preserve enumeration resistance. A lookup-then-refuse design is REJECTED OUTRIGHT: it converts the endpoint into the patient-list oracle the current design exists to avoid.
  (a) GLOBAL SEND CEILING, highest value per unit of work. A tenant-wide cap on OTP sends per rolling hour and per rolling day, independent of the existing per-IP and per-phone rules. Once tripped every caller receives the SAME generic response, so no enumeration signal is added. This bounds spend ABSOLUTELY, which neither existing limit does.
  (b) REJECT LANDLINES. phone.ts:19 accepts the 2 prefix, which is geographic and cannot receive SMS. Rejecting it removes roughly half the accepted input space AND supplies the enforcement point PG1's own DoR requires for the landline degradation case, which today has none. Leaks nothing: prefix ranges are public numbering-plan facts, not patient data.
  (c) INVISIBLE BOT CHALLENGE on the request route, ONLY if (a) and (b) prove insufficient. Weigh against accessibility for elderly patients before proposing it.

TEST DEBT, RECORDED: there is NO test file for this route. ls apps/api/app/api/v1/auth/otp/request/ returns route.ts alone. The send-for-unknown-number behaviour is currently UNASSERTED, which is how a deliberate trade became an unreviewed one. Any fix ships with a guard proven RED against the pre-fix sha.

HOME_LANE IS in_flight, NOT incidents, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The lane derivation puts an in_flight card that is blocked on a person into BLOCKED ON PEOPLE, under the owner column, which starts the answer-latency clock. This card is not an incident RECORD, it is active work whose next step is an owner decision (is the flag armed, and disarm it), followed by build directions (a), (b) and (c). Filing it under incidents would leave the most urgent item on the board out of the column the owner reads for what he owes.

THE PLAN ALREADY RULED THIS, AND THE RULING IS COMMITTED. docs/acceptance-session-wave-13.md:1161-1165, section 11 'Disarm - a named step, and not optional': 'OTP_LIVE_SEND IS DISARMED AT THE END OF THIS SESSION. R9 authorises supervised canaries, not a standing arm. "Left armed" is NOT permitted merely because it was written down - writing it down is a note, not a decision.' The voided amendment proposed exactly the standing arm that paragraph refuses.

WHY THE EXPOSURE IS LIVE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL, and this is the load-bearing fact: item 25 is the disarm step and it carries two blanks in the committed file, `Disarmed at: ______` and `Redeploy Ready at: ______`. BOTH ARE UNFILLED. The sittings ran 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-09; no results file existed until 2026-08-11. There is NO COMMITTED RECORD THAT THE DISARM WAS EVER PERFORMED. Absent a filled-in item 25, the flag must be treated as ARMED. The plan even anticipated the failure mode: 'STOP if the redeploy errors. The flag is still armed until one succeeds.' A save without a successful redeploy does not disarm a running deployment.
